note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Graphic Design
description: Image models make a graphic design piece from a user prompt. Users compare two anonymous designs and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena HTML Slides
description: Agents write a self-contained HTML slide deck that is converted to PPTX. Users compare the decks and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image
description: Image models generate a picture from a user prompt. Users compare two anonymous images and vote for the better one.
note: Filters split it by subject, such as products, landscapes, architecture, typography and marketing. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image Editing
description: Image models edit a user image following a text instruction. Users compare the two edits and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image to Frontend
description: Coding agents turn a reference image into a multi-file frontend web app. Users compare the running apps and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image to HTML
description: Models recreate a reference image or mockup as a working single-file HTML website. Users compare the rendered pages and vote for the closer, better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image to Video
description: Video models animate a user image into a short video. Users compare two anonymous videos and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Logo
description: Image models design a logo from a user prompt. Users compare two anonymous logos and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Mobile Builder
description: AI app builders make a mobile app from the same user prompt. Users compare the apps and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Multi-Image to Video
description: Video models compose one video from several reference images. Users compare two anonymous videos and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Multimodal to Video
description: Video models make a video from a mix of text, images and other inputs. Users compare two anonymous videos and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena PDF
description: Agents build a PDF document from a user prompt. Users compare the two documents and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Proprietary Harness Slides
description: Slide-making products build a presentation from a user prompt in their own harness. Users compare the decks and vote for the better one.
note: DesignArena open-sourced data from more than 50,000 slide generations. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Python-PPTX Slides
description: Agents build PowerPoint decks with python-pptx from a user prompt. Users compare narrative, visual design and structure and vote for the better deck.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena React Native
description: Models build cross-platform mobile apps in React Native from real user prompts. Users compare the running apps and vote for the better one.
note: DesignArena described the setup in its post Evaluating Mobile App-Building Agents. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Speech-to-Speech
description: Voice models answer spoken input with speech. Users listen to two anonymous replies and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Spreadsheet
description: Agents build spreadsheets such as financial models, budgets and trackers as Excel or CSV workbooks. Users compare accuracy, structure and formatting and vote.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena SVG
description: Models write SVG code for a design request such as an icon, logo, badge or illustration. Users compare the rendered graphics and vote.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Text-to-Speech
description: Speech models read the same text aloud. Users listen to two anonymous clips and vote for the more natural one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena UI Component
description: Models build one interface component as a single HTML file from a real user prompt. Users compare the rendered components and vote for the better one.
note: It is one of the five categories behind the Code overall board, with its own prompts on the DesignArena home page. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Video Arena
description: Users compare videos from anonymous video generation models for the same prompt and vote for the better one. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: Sibling boards cover image to video, multi-image to video, multimodal to video and video editing, each with its own record. One of 33 DesignArena boards. Its terms forbid automated reading, so the almanac imports no scores.

name: DesignArena Video Editing
description: Video models edit a user video following a text instruction. Users compare the two results and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Video to Website
description: Models watch a reference video and recreate its content as a working single-file HTML website. Users compare the rendered pages and vote.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Website
description: Models build a complete website as one HTML file from a real user prompt. Users compare the rendered pages and vote for the better one.
note: Filters split it by site type, such as e-commerce, portfolio, dashboard and blog. DesignArena blog posts also call it the Web Design (Non-Agentic) arena. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignJanus
description: People rate generated objects from six viewpoints and mark inconsistencies in shape, materials, and identity. The harness compares human ratings with automatic measures.

name: DeskCraft
description: Desktop agents complete 538 Ubuntu tasks, including 152 tasks with later user clarifications or interruptions. Programmatic checks inspect final application state, saved files, and exported artifacts.
org: Zhejiang University, Tsinghua University, Tencent and others
note: The suite includes 386 standard tasks. Interactive tasks use explicit triggers to introduce later user messages.

name: Destructive action avoidance
description: Coding agents meet conflicting user edits during tasks. Scored on preserving user changes and avoiding data-destructive actions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation for Codex models. The tasks are not public.

name: Destructive action reversion on long rollouts
description: Agents revert their own changes after long rollouts in workspaces with simulated user edits. Scored on perfect reversion and on preserving user work.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report two metrics with no overall number.

name: Destructive actions (Anthropic)
aliases: Destructive action and permission-seeking rates in Claude Code
description: Models continue real Claude Code transcripts cut just before a destructive action. Score is the rate of taking a destructive action.
note: Anthropic also reports how often models ask the user instead of acting. Tool results are simulated by another Claude model.

name: Destructive actions (Thinking Machines)
description: Agentic tasks that check whether a model takes destructive actions it was not authorized to take. Scored by the rate of destructive actions.
note: In-house test. Tasks are not public.

name: Destructive production evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents finish a task in a simulated production system under time pressure. Scored on destructive actions and on giving up too early.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Claude Opus 4.6 simulates the tool results.

name: Deterministic Agent Reasoning & Formatting Suite
description: Models solve three algorithm questions under strict formatting rules. The harness checks the answers and their JSON structure.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 2 distinct model versions.

name: DevBench
description: Models work through the software lifecycle on 22 curated repositories in Python, C/C++, Java and JavaScript: design, environment setup, implementation, acceptance tests and unit tests. Tests score code and an LLM judge scores design.
note: The repository is named DevEval but the benchmark is DevBench. Not the same as the PKU DevEval code generation set.

name: DevBench Acceptance Testing
description: Models generate acceptance tests for repositories. The score is the published oracle-test percentage.
note: One track of DevBench. The DevBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DevBench Environment Setup
description: Models prepare repository environments. The score is the percentage that pass the example usage test.
note: One track of DevBench. The DevBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DevBench Implementation
description: Models implement repository code. The score is the acceptance-test pass rate, with unit-test pass rate as an auxiliary metric.
note: One track of DevBench. The DevBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DevBench Unit Testing
description: Models generate unit tests for repositories. The score is the published oracle-test percentage.
note: One track of DevBench. The DevBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DevOps Troubleshoot
description: Agents inspect simulated logs, configurations and metrics to diagnose infrastructure failures. The grader checks root causes and proposed fixes.
note: The hub reports deepseek-v3.2-exp. deepseek-v3.2-exp reached a mean reward of 0.5564 on 5 examples on 2026-05-11.

name: DevOps-Gym
description: Agents build, monitor, repair and test Java and Go projects. The Prime port converts tasks to single-turn questions with proxy grading.
org: UCSB ML Security Lab and collaborators
note: The January 2026 paper compares Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek. Claude Code led the build and configuration comparison at 58.33%.

name: DevOpsBench-100
description: Agents resolve 100 operations and reliability tasks in a simulated online store. The verifier compares system state before and after their work.
note: The publisher lists reference and adversarial controls. Its leaderboard had no model submissions on November 19, 2026.

name: DexArena
description: Robots use both hands to complete household and industrial tasks. The simulator checks each stage and the final outcome across ten multistage tasks.
org: Shanghai Institute for Physical Artificial Intelligence and Robotics and collaborators

name: DexVerse
description: Robot policies perform tabletop manipulation tasks in Isaac Lab, including tool use, bimanual coordination, and sequences with several goals. Task-specific success conditions check completion under different visual settings and robot embodiments.
org: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, University of Hong Kong, and University of California, Berkeley
note: The paper describes 100 tasks and evaluations on 19 tasks. The repository marks baseline demonstrations and some cross-embodiment assets as pending.

name: Deysi Spam Detection
description: Models classify English messages as spam or legitimate. The hub adapter grades the label and response format across 2,725 test messages.
note: The highest public hub mean reward was 0.9903 for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on 2725 examples on 2026-03-22. The hub also lists gpt-oss-120b.

name: dfbench
description: Agents do defensive security work on held-out code: find vulnerabilities, judge whether reported findings are real, and explain what a diff changed. Each part is scored separately.
note: Released 2026-08-19 as dfbench v1. Detection is scored by recall and plotted against cost per task. 12 models in the Fireworks index.

name: DGCL Reward Hacking
description: Models decide whether corporate actions comply with Delaware law and provide supporting calculations. Fifty evaluation cases distinguish correct headline decisions from fully correct answers.
note: The README checked November 19, 2026 reports base Qwen3.5-4B led its trained variant on fully correct verdicts, 23.8% to 16.7%.

name: DI-Bench
description: Agents answer questions using company tables, documents, and business rules. The benchmark checks whether agents apply those rules when computing results.

name: DiaBLa
description: Models translate informal conversations between English and French while preserving meaning across turns.
note: MTEB also uses the parallel dialogue turns to test bilingual sentence matching.

name: DiagTrace
description: Models request information about a patient one turn at a time. The evaluator compares the sequence of requests with the published case history.

name: Dictatorship Eval
description: Scenarios at six difficulty levels testing whether models help with authoritarian requests, from blunt asks to requests hidden in code edits. LLM judge, no self-grading.
note: Headline: all tested models complied when the request was disguised as an innocuous code edit. Author says the scenario library is open-sourced. No official repo found. Third-party extension: github.com/RandallSPQR/Dict_Eval_Hall.

name: DiDeMo
description: Models locate the time interval in a video that matches a natural language description.
note: Annotators mark which segments of the video describe the requested moment.

name: DiG-bench
description: Agents play text-only games whose transformation rules and win conditions are hidden, so they must discover the rules by experimenting. Every game was beaten by at least one human on a first attempt.
org: Princeton + MIT + collaborators (Battleday, Whittington, Griffiths, Tenenbaum and others)
note: 70 games in seven difficulty tiers, 21 public and the rest private. The board has basic-harness and agentic-harness tracks. Supplying the true rules lifts win rates sharply, so the gap measures discovery.

name: Digital Work Index
description: Models are scored on eight benchmarks in coding, reasoning, writing and enterprise work. Weights come from the wages of the 29 digital occupations the benchmarks map to.
note: Weights use BLS employment and May 2025 wages for 237 digital occupations. The board had 16 models at launch.

name: DIHARD III
description: Models identify who speaks when across eleven recording domains. The benchmark includes overlapping speech.

name: DiligenceBench
description: 150 public-equity research tasks on large US companies across sectors. Agents answer open-ended research questions in their own harness, and a model judge scores each answer against a dense task rubric for factual accuracy, analysis and risk awareness.
note: No fixed harness. Results are reported per harness (Loop, Sandbox, Finance) and as a best-harness score.

name: DIODE
description: Models estimate depth in indoor and outdoor scenes. The dataset provides depth measurements from a laser scanner for comparison.

name: DIOR
description: Models locate and classify objects in remotely sensed images. The benchmark measures detection accuracy across different object sizes and backgrounds.

name: Dirty Integration
description: Agents collect every record from a paginated API despite unreliable cursors, rate limits, changing field types and timeouts.
note: On August 1, 2026, Claude Sonnet 5 scored 0.81 on the hostile setting and DeepSeek V3.2 scored 0.76. Both scored 1.00 on the easier settings.

name: Disallowed Content Evaluations with Representative Prompts
description: Models resample the final turn of deidentified ChatGPT production conversations. Scored as the estimated prevalence of policy violating outputs per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category rates with no overall number.

name: DISBench
description: Multimodal agents search raw visual histories over several steps to find target images from implicit context cues.
org: NLPIR Lab, Renmin University of China
note: 51 HF paper upvotes.

name: Discharge Me!
description: Models draft discharge instructions and brief hospital course summaries from patient records. The shared task compares model output with clinical discharge documentation.

name: Discoverable memorization of training data
description: Models continue 50-token prefixes sampled from their own training data. The test counts exact and approximate copies of the true suffix.
note: In-house Google method on over 700,000 training documents. Reports usually plot rates on a log scale without printed numbers.

name: DiscoX
description: Models translate 200 expert texts between Chinese and English at discourse level, averaging over 1,700 tokens each. Metric-S, a reference-free judge, scores accuracy, fluency and appropriateness, and the overall score is their sum.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Zhao et al.)
note: Texts come from 7 expert domains.

name: Discrim-Eval
description: Models make yes or no decisions in templated scenarios that vary age, gender and race. Scored by mixed effects model coefficients.
note: OpenAI reports normalized coefficients for explicit and implicit demographic mentions. Lower means less bias.

name: Disengagement-Aware Student Simulators
description: Tutors interact with simulated learners who vary in engagement. The authors compare five tutors and validate the student behaviors against real tutoring sessions.

name: Disordered eating evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models handle conversations about eating disorders and disordered eating. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Disparate performance on voice inputs
description: Speech models answer capability and safety prompts spoken in system voices and 27 human voices. Compares accuracy across voices.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation on TTS versions of TriviaQA, an MMLU subset, HellaSwag, LAMBADA and safety prompts.

name: DistressBench
description: Models reply as a chatbot to 718 simulated users in psychological crisis, in single-turn and multi-turn chats. Three judge models score replies against clinician-written rubrics.
note: Half of the 718 conversations are public and half private. The board uses all of them and lists about 47 models. A long-horizon annex, DistressBench-LH, is reported apart.

name: Divergence attack (extractable memorization)
description: Models are prompted to repeat one token many times. The test measures how often they diverge and emit memorized training text.
note: Google runs 3,750 prompts over 125 single-token characters, following Nasr et al. 2023.

name: DiverseVul
description: Models classify C and C++ functions from real vulnerability fixing commits as vulnerable or not.
org: UC Berkeley and others (Chen et al.)
note: Google reports accuracy in multiple-choice form.

name: Diving48
description: Models classify competitive dives from videos by distinguishing their movement sequences.
note: The benchmark includes 48 dive classes.

name: DNA sequence design for transcription factor binding
description: Models design DNA sequences that bind 11 Nucleobench transcription factors, scored by BPNet oracles against the Ledidi baseline. Scored as pass@1.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. The concern threshold is an 80 percent win rate over Ledidi.

name: DNA Synthesis Screening Evasion
description: Models design DNA fragments that assemble into pathogenic viruses while evading gene synthesis screening. Scored per assembly criterion.
note: SecureBio evaluation run by Anthropic on 10 pathogenic agents. The tasks are not public.

name: Do You See Me
description: Models answer 2,612 visual perception questions on 1,758 images across seven 2D and 3D subtasks drawn from human psychology. Questions are multiple choice or numeric.
note: Humans score 96.49% in the paper. Task complexity is controllable.

name: Do-Not-Answer
description: Models get risky instructions that responsible models should not follow, across 12 harm areas and 61 risk types. Responses are judged for safe handling.
note: Labs often rerun it with their own judge model. The Inspect adversarial variant measures how often a model follows a reformulated request.

name: DoAnythingNow (DAN)
description: Models face in-the-wild DAN-style jailbreak prompts paired with forbidden questions. Scored by refusal rate or attack success rate.
org: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security (Xinyue Shen, Yang Zhang and others)
note: The paper collects 1,405 jailbreak prompts and 107,250 questions in 13 forbidden scenarios. Ai2 uses a 300-prompt subsample paired with HarmBench behaviors.

name: Doc2Harness
description: Models build a coding-agent harness from an interface skeleton and a development document. The frozen harness then runs 328 scripted test cases in separate containers.
org: Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
note: 55 HF paper upvotes. The release covered nineteen frontier models.

name: Docci
description: Models retrieve matching documents and images using the DOCCI corpus.

name: Document Arena
description: People upload their own PDFs with a question, compare answers from two anonymous models, and vote for the better one. Votes become Bradley-Terry ratings.
note: PDF uploads opened in February 2026 and the ranked board went live on 2026-03-03. It had 44 models and 404,715 votes on the 2026-09-13 update. A style-controlled view also exists.

name: DocVQA
description: Models answer 50,000 questions about 12,000 scanned document images by reading their text and layout. Scoring is ANLS, a string similarity to reference answers.
org: CVC, Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona and IIIT Hyderabad
note: Test answers stay on the evaluation server, and top models now pass the 94.36 human score in the paper.

name: DOE sample pack
description: Agents complete five simulated workplace assignments in law, private equity, and finance operations. Deterministic checks grade figures and application state, while model judges grade written work.
note: The October 2026 table reports seven models. Claude Opus 5.5 led at 0.36 mean score across five tasks. No model met every critical criterion.

name: Does the answer survive disagreement?
description: Models answer checkable questions and respond to a user who insists on a plausible wrong answer. The test measures whether they keep the correct answer.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 1 distinct model version.

name: Dojo Mini Bench
description: Agents complete tasks in LinkedIn, Linear and Gmail through Dojo. Each task has its own completion check.
note: The hub reports Claude Sonnet 4 and Mistral models. Claude Sonnet 4 led with a mean reward of 0.8 on five examples on November 21, 2025.

name: Dollar Street
description: Models recognize household objects in photos from families at different income levels. The benchmark supports comparisons across regions and income groups.

name: Dolly Machine Translated v2
description: Models answer a curated subset of Dolly prompts translated into 66 languages with newer systems such as Command A Translate. A GPT-4.1 judge rates answers with a rubric in the Tiny Aya report.
note: Drops pun-dependent prompts and uses a different language mix than v1, so scores are not comparable.

name: Doubao Multi-Turn Bench
description: Models answer the turn of a real Doubao conversation where the user was dissatisfied, with the earlier turns as context. Rubrics grade each answer.
note: In-house Seed benchmark filtered from online Doubao user conversations.

name: DP-Bench
description: Document parsers and vision models convert PDFs and scanned pages into structured HTML or Markdown. Output is compared with reference structure.
note: About 90 likes on Hugging Face.

name: DPG-Bench
description: Text-to-image models draw 1,000 dense prompts with many objects, attributes and relations. A VQA model checks each element of the prompt graph in the image.
note: Filed under the generation subcategory used for GenEval. The overall score averages over prompt elements.

name: DRACO
description: 100 deep-research tasks from real Perplexity queries across 10 domains, graded on about 40 expert rubric criteria each.
note: The makers built and saturation-tested it with Perplexity's own system. No public code repo found.

name: DRAMA-Eval
description: Models generate dialogue with several speakers across multiple turns. The authors check word accuracy and use a model judge to evaluate delivery in context.

name: DrawBench
description: Models generate images from text prompts that test counting, composition, and other skills. Human raters compare image quality and prompt alignment.

name: DRBench
description: Agents investigate open-ended business questions across enterprise applications and produce reports. The evaluator checks whether the reports recover relevant information and support their claims.

name: Dreaddit
description: Models classify Reddit posts according to whether their authors express stress. The hub port adds rewards for reasoning and answer format.
note: On October 31, 2019, BERT-base led the paper’s supervised comparison at 0.8065 F1. Logistic regression with fine-tuned BERT features scored 0.7937.

name: DREAM-1K
description: Video models write fine-grained descriptions of 1,000 videos from varied sources. An automatic method scores how many described events match the reference.
note: Released with the Tarsier video description models. The 1,000 count follows the name.

name: DreamGen Bench
description: Video generation benchmark measuring how well video models adapt to a target robot embodiment. Part of NVIDIA's DreamGen pipeline.
note: Paper reports strong correlation between benchmark score and downstream policy success.

name: DriveBench
aliases: Are VLMs Ready for Autonomous Driving?
description: Vision-language models answer 20,498 questions about 19,200 driving frames, covering perception, prediction, planning and behavior. Inputs come in 17 settings: clean images, corrupted images and text only. The test checks whether answers rest on the image or on general knowledge.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: ICCV 2025. The authors find that models often give plausible driving answers even when the image is degraded or missing. About 250 GitHub stars and 25 HF paper upvotes. The paper tests 12 VLMs.

name: DriveBench Behavior
description: Models answer driving behavior questions. The score is the published GPT evaluation score for this task family.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: One track of DriveBench. The DriveBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DriveBench Perception
description: Models answer driving perception questions. The score is the published GPT evaluation score for this task family.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: One track of DriveBench. The DriveBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DriveBench Planning
description: Models answer driving planning questions. The score is the published GPT evaluation score for this task family.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: One track of DriveBench. The DriveBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DriveBench Prediction
description: Models answer driving prediction questions. The score is the published GPT evaluation score for this task family.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: One track of DriveBench. The DriveBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DrivingBench
description: Vision-language models drive a real Toyota Corolla through a cone course with up to three attempts in one conversation. Scored on the furthest progress along the course.
note: Released September 21, 2026 with four frontier models. Version 2 moved to a Tesla and a harder second course, so scores do not compare.

name: DrivingBench v2
description: Vision-language models drive a real Tesla through two unseen cone courses with steering, accelerator and brake tools. The score is the furthest progress over three attempts in one conversation, averaged over six trials.
note: Released November 16, 2026. Progress comes from GPS, accurate to about 1 to 2 m, and doesn’t show whether the car stayed inside the cones. Fine-tuned driving models (VLAs and WAMs) are ranked separately on the site. A human driver using the same tools reached 95%.

name: Drone-Bench
description: Agent writes code for a small real drone across five tasks (reconstruct, localize, navigate, detect, follow). Each scored against a human-written baseline.
note: Best of 10 submissions per run counts. Two tasks use held-out sets. Harness and data are not released.

name: DROP
description: Reading comprehension requiring discrete operations (counting, sorting, arithmetic) over paragraphs. Scored by F1.
note: Saturated base-model metric.

name: DrugDiscoveryBench
description: Agents do early-stage drug discovery work, from target identification to lead optimization, in 82 tasks with one checkable answer each. A judge model grades answers against expert rubrics.
note: A task counts as solved only at a full rubric score, averaged over three runs with a 120 minute timeout. The judge is GPT-5.4. About 25 entries on the board.

name: DrugProt
description: Models read biomedical abstracts and identify which of 13 labeled relationships connects a marked chemical and protein.
note: The organizers’ 2023 report compares Humboldt, NLM-NCBI and other teams. Humboldt led the main track with 0.797311 micro F1.

name: DrugTargetWorld
description: Agents interpret cardiac MRI and identify proteins associated with causal effects in 20 simulated biobanks. The verifier checks their conclusions against hidden ground truth.
note: The October 2026 release reports scores for nine models across 540 episodes. Claude Opus 5 led with 39.98 out of 100, followed by GPT-5.6 Sol.

name: DS-1000
description: Models write Python for 1,000 data science problems from StackOverflow across seven libraries such as NumPy and Pandas. Test cases and API constraints check each answer.
org: HKU, Stanford, UC Berkeley, UW, Meta and CMU
note: Problems were lightly modified from the StackOverflow originals to reduce memorization.

name: DS-Arena-Code
description: Models answer common coding requests in an internal subjective test. GPT-4o judges responses against competitor models to give a win rate.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and DeepSeek never released the prompts.

name: DS-FIM-Eval
description: Models fill in missing code between a given prefix and suffix, as in editor plugin completion.
note: In-house: DeepSeek calls it an internal test set and never released the tasks.

name: DSBench
description: Data science agents solve 466 data analysis tasks and 74 end-to-end data modeling tasks drawn from Eloquence and Kaggle competitions. Analysis is scored by accuracy and modeling by relative performance gap.
org: Tencent AI Lab and University of Texas at Dallas (Jing et al.)
note: Tasks include long contexts, multimodal backgrounds, large data files and multi-table structures. OpenAI reported both splits for ChatGPT agent in 2025-07. The repo has about 130 GitHub stars. The org line comes from the author list and is likely.

name: DSBench (DeepSeek internal)
description: DeepSeek internal coding-agent test sets: full-stack development tasks and hard agentic coding problems. Pass-rate scoring.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (DeepSeek). Unrelated to the 2024 public DSBench data-science benchmark.

name: DSI-Bench
description: Video questions about dynamic scenes where both the observer and objects move, testing whether models separate camera motion from object motion.

name: DTap Direct Misuse
description: An attacker agent generates adaptive jailbreaks against a target agent across tool-use and browser-use tasks. Reports attack success rate.
org: UIUC Secure Learning Lab (AI Secure, DecodingTrust team)
note: Direct-misuse subset of the DecodingTrust-Agent Platform. 80 tool-use and 76 browser-use tasks.

name: DTap Prompt Injection
description: An attacker agent plants indirect prompt injections in tool and browser environments against a benign-user agent. Reports attack success rate.
org: UIUC Secure Learning Lab (AI Secure, DecodingTrust team)
note: Indirect-injection subset of the DecodingTrust-Agent Platform. 58 tool-use and 42 browser-use tasks.

name: DTBench
description: Models answer 407 multiple-choice questions on decision theory in Newcomb-like problems, where choices predict the behavior of copies. Scored by accuracy.
note: Near saturation, with top models at about 98% in August 2026. Random guessing scores 40%.

name: DTU Multi-View Stereo
description: Models reconstruct objects from multiple camera views. The benchmark measures the accuracy and completeness of reconstructed surfaces against scanned reference geometry.

name: Dual Exam
description: Multimodal agents are tested under fixed environment responses, and world models under fixed actions. The agent track has 1,088 items and the world model track 400 cases.
note: It had 34 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: Dual-Arm Sim
description: Frontier models control a two-armed robot in a simulated operating room from cameras and sensors. Tasks include swapping instruments, replacing a drug cartridge and packing a surgical kit.
note: Ten models over 800 trials produced 11 task completions. Gemini 4 Argon ranked first with 9.

name: DUDE
description: Models answer extractive, abstractive, and unanswerable questions about multi-page, multi-domain documents. Scored by ANLS.
org: DUDE team (KU Leuven, CVC Barcelona, et al.)

name: DuelLab GameBench 2
description: Models get the rules of a strategy game and write a program that plays it. DuelLab checks and builds each program, then runs head-to-head matches between programs from different models. Match outcomes become per-game scores from 0 to 100 and a Bradley-Terry ranking, with no human or model judge.
note: GameBench 2 launched on 2026-07-14 and replaced GameBench 1, a frozen archive whose scores do not compare. Each reasoning setting of a model ranks separately, and a failed program counts as 0. The October 2026 release used eight games. The evaluator and game engine are private, so outsiders cannot rerun every step.

name: DuetBench
description: Agents diagnose and improve customer service agents on simulated deployments with procedures, tools and synthetic traffic. A blinded judge compares responses head to head.
note: Decagon calls it the first customer service benchmark for agent self-improvement. The Fireworks board ranks 9 models by a Diagnosis Elo.

name: Duidelijke Taal
description: Models rewrite Dutch text in simpler language. Human-written simplifications provide reference answers.
note: EuroEval provides a public evaluation split for Dutch text simplification.

name: DuoBench
description: Eleven bimanual Franka FR3 Duo tasks in four coordination categories, in simulation and partly real. Stage-based scoring beyond binary success.
org: UTN Nuremberg + KIT + Franka Robotics + TU Munich
note: Stage-based scoring locates failures (early interaction, parallel arm use, sim-to-real). Four of 11 tasks rebuilt in the real world from 3D-printable recipes. No leaderboard.

name: Duplex-MPE
description: Full-duplex speech models join conversations of three or four people and must decide when to answer, stay silent or stop speaking. The set has 2,000 scenarios.
note: It had 46 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: DuplexLedger
description: Speech agents track facts that speakers introduce, revise, or leave unchanged during conversation. The evaluator asks which facts still apply.

name: Duplicate Side Effect Desk
description: Agents process refund requests when timeouts or duplicate tickets obscure payment status. The evaluator uses the transaction ledger to identify duplicate refunds.
note: The September 2026 table reports Claude Sonnet 4.5 at 0.985, Claude Haiku 4.5 at 0.984, and GPT-4.1-mini at 0.959 across 96 runs each.

name: Dutch Book Bench
description: Models assign probabilities to related events in separate conversations. The grader checks whether inconsistent probabilities let a bettor guarantee a profit.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 19 distinct model versions.

name: Dutch Book Reviews Dataset
description: Models classify the sentiment of Dutch book reviews from Hebban using ratings supplied by readers.
org: Benjamin van der Burgh and Suzan Verberne
note: EuroEval scores sentiment labels with the Matthews correlation coefficient.

name: Dutch CoLA
description: Models judge whether Dutch sentences drawn from descriptions of Dutch syntax are grammatically acceptable.
note: EuroEval compares the labels with human or constructed reference judgments using the Matthews correlation coefficient.

name: Dutch Model Benchmark
description: Models perform Dutch language understanding tasks, including reasoning about the causes and effects of events.
note: The authors include COPA-NL as the causal reasoning task.

name: DxEnv Diagnostician
description: Agents choose tests under a budget and assign probabilities to 149 conditions in synthetic patients. The grader measures diagnostic calibration and test costs.
note: The hub reports qwen2.5-7b-instruct. qwen2.5-7b-instruct reached a mean reward of -0.6007 on 50 examples on 2026-10-19.

name: DyCodeEval
description: Models solve dynamically rewritten HumanEval and MBPP problems with equivalent program behavior. The evaluator runs tests and computes DyPass@K across generated variants.
note: The repository supplies pregenerated variants. Its leaderboard link is a placeholder, so it does not establish a public leaderboard.

name: Dynabench SQuAD
description: Models answer reading comprehension questions written by people to fool earlier models in the loop.
note: Llama 3 shows it only in a scatter plot.

name: DynaMath
description: Models answer visual math questions generated from 501 seed programs that vary values and graphs. Scored by average and worst-case accuracy across variants.
org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and UC Berkeley

name: Dynamic Programming (m8ngotree)
description: Models solve generated optimization and counting problems, including knapsack, coin change, and edit distance. A problem-specific algorithm verifies each answer.
note: The highest public hub mean reward was 0.946 for gpt-4.1-mini on 100 examples on 2025-09-07.

name: Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2
description: Spoken language models follow text instructions about audio across 180 tasks in speech, music and other sounds. Tasks include classification, regression and sequence generation, and researchers keep contributing new ones. Models run zero-shot, without task-specific training.
note: Phase-2 adds 125 community tasks to the 55 classification tasks of the first phase (2023), so scores do not compare across phases. About 200 GitHub stars. The leaderboard space was last updated in 2025-07.

name: Dấu or Die: Vietnamese Diacritic Restoration
description: Models restore missing diacritics in 37 Vietnamese sentences. A sentence earns credit only when every mark matches the reference.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 7 distinct model versions.

name: E-Bench (Tencent)
description: Agents complete Tencent in-house work tasks in the working agent group. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Not the Shanghai AI Lab robotics test EBench. Hy3 scored 50.2 in its own card and 48.5 in the Hy4 preview card after harness updates.

name: E-Bench-Code (Tencent)
description: Agents complete Tencent in-house work tasks that need code. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: E-Commerce Bench
description: Agents start with 100,000 yuan and run up to four online stores for 365 simulated days on real market data. They source, negotiate with suppliers, price, promote and manage cash. Scored by end-of-year assets over the opening balance.
org: Qwen Team, Alibaba Group, with Taobao and Tmall Group
note: Six more dimensions are scored separately, including negotiation and fraud avoidance. Each model runs 5 episodes. The paper tests 18 models and the repo table lists 21. The qwen.ai post is dated 2026-09-03.

name: Earnings-21
description: Models transcribe long earnings calls. The benchmark tests recognition of financial terminology in real conversations.

name: Earnings-22
description: Models transcribe English earnings calls from speakers with different accents. NVIDIA reports long-form word error rate.

name: EarthRecord
description: Agents analyze multidecade satellite observations to answer land-change questions. Reference checks score answers to 238 questions across 56 sites.
note: The benchmark requires tool use and multisensor temporal reasoning. Perturbation controls test sensitivity to the evidence rather than only geographic familiarity.

name: EarthVerse
description: Agents investigate documented natural hazards using event data from different sources. The evaluator checks individual claims and the calculations that support them across 405 tasks.

name: EBench
description: 26 Isaac Sim household mobile-manipulation task types annotated by 5 capability and 4 generalization dimensions. Platform-scored success rate.
note: Diagnostic profile instead of one scalar. Leaderboard uses held-out Test-Mini split. Board lacks dates and trial counts. In September 2026 the maker raised the step limits for the bottle and shop tasks from 3,000 to 5,000 and called it a minor fix.

name: EBR-bench
description: Agent plays the board game Earthborne Rangers 10-30 times in a row. Scored on objectives completed (of 21) to test learning from experience.
note: One card was banned in 2026-10 after it broke the game. Epoch expects saturation soon. Game material is not distributed.

name: Echo General AI Prediction Leaderboard
description: Models forecast unresolved events drawn from prediction markets, synthesized news questions and expert-written questions. Forecasts made at aligned times are compared in pairwise battles, and an Elo fit ranks the models.
note: Domains include finance, politics, crypto, sports and esports. The 2026-03-27 snapshot had 11 models, including UniPat's own EchoZ-1.0.

name: ECHR Binary Violation Classification
description: Models read the facts of a European Court of Human Rights case and predict whether the court found a violation.

name: ECLeKTic
description: Models answer 384 closed-book questions, translated into 12 languages, about facts found in only one language's Wikipedia. Scoring checks transfer across languages.

name: Economic Dispatch
description: Models assign output levels to generators to meet demand at minimum cost. The grader checks capacity limits, supply balance, and cost against an exact solution.
note: The repository checked November 19, 2026 reports Claude Opus 4.8 leading with 1.000 mean reward, compared with 0.861 for Claude Haiku 4.5.

name: Economics Arena for Large Language Models
description: Models choose numbers in beauty contests and place sealed bids in auctions. Researchers compare payoffs and measure how strategies change when players see previous rounds.
note: In January 2024, GPT-3.5 led the five-model senior group after 100 sessions, averaging 0.410 in beauty contests and 1.206 in auctions.

name: EdgeBench
description: Agents iterate for up to 12 hours on 134 executable real-world tasks with multi-level feedback. Scores are tracked at 2 hour steps to measure learning from the environment.
note: 51 of the 134 tasks are open source. Tasks fall in six groups: scientific and ML, systems and SE, optimization, knowledge, formal and games. The harness is called SForge.

name: EDIS
description: Models retrieve news images and their associated text using queries that refer to specific people, places, or events.
note: MTEB reports nDCG at 10 on its EDIST2ITRetrieval task.

name: EduArt
description: Models answer art history questions from Italian secondary schools and US Advanced Placement exams. The authors compare 12 models across seven question formats.

name: EduBench-RU
description: Models plan lessons, explain school subjects, and assist teachers in Russian and Chuvash. A panel of model judges scores responses against a teaching rubric.

name: Education (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models solve, grade, explain and write K to 12 problems across core subjects in teaching scenarios.
note: One of six in-house application sets in the Seed1.8 and Seed2.0 model cards. Scoring is a guess.

name: EduClaw-Bench
description: Agents tutor a simulated learner over 30 days. The benchmark tracks learning gains, responsiveness, helpfulness, and curriculum design across 55 scenarios.

name: EduExplain
description: Models select resources and arrange them into a storyboard to explain a science concept. Human-validated sets and storyboards provide references for 321 learner questions.

name: EduFair-Bench
description: Tutors teach the same simulated student under different demographic descriptions. A judge grades individual turns and whole conversations to measure changes in teaching quality.

name: EduVideoBench
description: Models generate classroom videos intended to teach facts, skills, or attitudes. Experts assess instructional accuracy, presentation, and educational safety.

name: EEBench
description: 13 electrical-engineering circuit and PCB design tasks graded by deterministic build checks, simulation and BOM constraints. No LLM judge.

name: Effective FPS
description: Models decide whether video frames are consecutive or duplicated to simulate a higher capture rate. The evaluator checks each prediction against the construction of the clip.
note: In August 2026, Gemma 3 27B led with 55% accuracy on 40 clips. Qwen2.5-VL 7B and the EgoSieve-S duplicate-frame classifier each scored 50%.

name: EGI-BENCH
description: Agents work across eight enterprise evaluations. The suite combines their results into six scores covering activities such as planning, retrieving evidence, and using tools.

name: Ego-Exo4D
description: Models estimate human pose during skilled activities filmed from first-person and external viewpoints. Meta reports joint and mesh errors for physical and procedural activities.

name: Ego2Act
description: Models generate first-person video showing how to complete a task from an initial image. A judge checks the steps and their physical plausibility.
org: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence and collaborators

name: Ego2Flow
description: Driving policies operate on simulated city maps. The authors measure how each policy affects the surrounding traffic as other vehicles respond.

name: Ego3D-Bench
description: Models answer spatial reasoning questions about ego-centric multi-view scenes, such as those from self-driving cars. Some items ask for distances, scored by error.
note: Qwen reports a lower-is-better number for it, which matches the distance error metric.

name: EgoHome
description: Models annotate 137 egocentric clips of household chores, about two hours in all, with subtasks, hand actions, hand captions and hand boxes. Segments are as short as 0.1 seconds. A model judge matches segment labels, and boxes are scored by centroid hits.
note: Perceptron released it with Perceptron Egocentric 1.0. Each annotation type gets its own score from 0 to 1, and the headline here is the subtask score, which the card plots against cost. Perceptron averaged its own model over several runs, and every other system ran once. The data is CC BY-NC 4.0, with a grant that lets anyone evaluate models on it and publish the results.

name: EgoLife (with memory)
description: Models answer life-assistant questions about a week of egocentric video from six people, such as recalling past events and habits.
org: EgoLife team (Jingkang Yang, Ziwei Liu et al.)
note: This entry is the with-memory setting of EgoLifeQA reported in a Qwen model card, and its exact setup is not documented.

name: EgoSchema
description: Models answer five-way multiple-choice questions about three-minute egocentric video clips from Ego4D. Scored by accuracy on 5,031 questions.
note: Answers are public for only 500 questions. The full test set is scored by a server.

name: EgoTempo
description: Models answer questions about egocentric videos that require temporal understanding across the whole clip.
org: Google DeepMind and University of Bristol
note: Gemini 2.5 report uses the test subset, 0-shot, 256 frames.

name: EgyHellaSwag
description: Models select a plausible ending for a situation described in Egyptian Arabic. The evaluation adapts HellaSwag to the dialect.

name: EgyMMLU
description: Models answer multiple-choice subject questions in Egyptian Arabic. The evaluation tests knowledge in a dialect underrepresented in standard Arabic exams.

name: EHRNoteQA
description: Models read a patient's accumulated MIMIC-IV discharge summaries and answer clinical questions about them. The set has 962 question and answer pairs, each for a different patient.
note: GPT-4 drafted the questions and three clinicians reviewed them. NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks. Google's MedGemma 1.5 reports it.

name: EHRQA (Google)
description: Models answer questions about long synthetic outpatient health records in FHIR format. Questions cover 42 types in 10 categories and need multi-hop, temporal and arithmetic reasoning.
note: Google built it from Synthea records for the MedGemma technical report. The test split has 19 patient records.

name: EHRSHOT
description: Models predict clinical outcomes from longitudinal electronic health records with few labeled examples for each task.

name: EHRSQL
description: Models convert clinical questions into SQL queries over electronic health records. The benchmark includes questions that the database cannot answer.

name: EIFBench
description: Models follow extremely complex instructions that bundle several tasks and many constraints in one request, as in real product workflows.
note: The scoring field is a guess from the abstract.

name: ELBench
description: Models respond to teaching and safety scenarios alongside academic questions. The authors compare the same models across four educational assessment areas.

name: Election integrity evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer election-related prompts, including requests for misinformation or influence operations. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ElephantBench
description: Models answer 1,094 closed-book questions about facts with multiple verified but conflicting accounts. A model judge assigns complete, partial, or failed recall.
org: Tencent Youtu Lab, Tsinghua University, and University of Warwick
note: The benchmark reports recall rates and completeness. Sources and tools are withheld during answering.

name: Eleusis
description: Agents play cards to discover a hidden rule. The scorer tests whether a proposed rule makes the same decisions as the hidden rule.
note: On October 7, 2026, teams of eight or sixteen GPT-6 Sol agents solved all 20 episodes in the team size experiment. A separate experiment compared GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

name: ELI5 Arena
description: Models explain concepts in simple language. Pairwise votes determine the published Arena rating.
note: The official API publishes an Arena rating, confidence interval and vote count. Voter identity requires confirmation from the board description.

name: Elimination Game
description: Models play a multi-player game of public and private talk, alliances and votes to eliminate each other. A jury of eliminated players picks the winner.
note: Tests social reasoning, strategy and deception. About 300 GitHub stars.

name: Email To CC BCC
description: Models assign email recipients to To, CC and BCC using roles and privacy constraints. The test split contains 91 threads.
note: The hub reports gpt-4.1-mini, merged-model, Qwen3-0.6B. merged-model reached a mean reward of 0.7104 on 50 examples on 2026-03-23.

name: EmailBench
description: Agents handle email and productivity requests in a synthetic inbox. The evaluator combines executable checks and model-graded rubrics across 206 scenarios.

name: Embodied Agent Arena
description: Vision-language agents solve geometry, spatial reasoning, affordance, planning, and manipulation tasks. The 1,000-case evaluation combines 32 established sources with GeoProbe.
note: GeoProbe contributes 168 cases within the suite. The evaluation covers 10 models. Domain-specific metrics do not define one interchangeable aggregate.

name: Embodied Agent Interface
description: Models interpret goals, decompose them into subgoals, sequence actions, and predict state transitions in BEHAVIOR and VirtualHome. The evaluator checks task completion and distinguishes hallucinations, invalid actions, and planning errors.
note: The four modules have separate metrics. Running the BEHAVIOR track requires iGibson assets.

name: Embodied First Exam
description: Coding agents answer frozen robot tasks from many benchmark suites with a program. Each program is verified in a separate sandbox, run on Harbor.
org: Northwestern University and collaborators (CMU, UC Berkeley, Stanford and others)
note: Released 2026-10-19. About 220 GitHub stars in its first weeks.

name: Embodied Over-Refusal Benchmark
description: Models decide whether to perform household tasks. The score balances compliance on safe requests with refusal on hazardous ones.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 7 distinct model versions.

name: EmbodiedBench
description: Multimodal LLMs act as embodied agents on 1,128 tasks in four simulators, from household planning (EB-ALFRED, EB-Habitat) to navigation and manipulation. Success rate.
note: ICML 2025. About 360 GitHub stars and 35 Hugging Face upvotes. Six subsets probe commonsense, complex instructions, spatial awareness, visual perception and long-horizon planning. Used in the CVPR 2026 FMEA challenge.

name: EmbodiedBench EB-ALFRED
description: Agents follow household instructions through high-level actions in AI2-THOR. The score is the published average task success percentage across EB-ALFRED capability groups.
note: One track of EmbodiedBench. The EmbodiedBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EmbodiedBench EB-Habitat
description: Agents follow instructions to find and rearrange objects through high-level skills in Habitat 2.0. The score is the published average task success percentage.
note: One track of EmbodiedBench. The EmbodiedBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EmbodiedBench EB-Manipulation
description: Agents use visual observations to control a robot arm for object manipulation in simulation. The score is the published average task success percentage.
note: One track of EmbodiedBench. The EmbodiedBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EmbodiedBench EB-Navigation
description: Agents use visual observations and low-level movement actions to reach target objects in AI2-THOR. The score is the published average task success percentage.
note: One track of EmbodiedBench. The EmbodiedBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EmbodiedCLBench
description: Self-evolving embodied agents learn tasks in sequence in simulation. The test measures whether they keep past experience and transfer it to new tasks.
note: 69 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: EmbodiedIntentBench
description: Agents adapt perception during mobile robot missions as urgency, battery capacity, and connectivity change. The evaluator checks whether agents meet the mission objectives.

name: EmbodiedLab
description: Agents choose measurements, operate a simulated robot arm, and read instruments through cameras to complete 35 laboratory experiments.

name: EmbSpatialBench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions on six spatial relations between objects in egocentric embodied scenes. Scored by accuracy.

name: EMDB
aliases: Electromagnetic Database of Global 3D Human Pose and Shape in the Wild
description: Models reconstruct human pose and body shape in everyday scenes. The benchmark compares joint positions with electromagnetic measurements.

name: EMMA
description: Models solve math, physics, chemistry and coding problems that need reasoning over text and images together, not each alone. Answers are checked against a key.
note: ByteDance Seed reports it in the Seed1.8 and Seed2.0 model cards.

name: EmoBench-M
description: Multimodal models are tested on emotional intelligence across 13 scenarios in three dimensions: emotion recognition, conversational emotion understanding and socially complex emotion analysis.
note: ACM MM 2026. About 155 GitHub stars.

name: Emoji Rebus
description: Models decode an emoji clue into a target phrase. The grader ignores capitalization and surrounding whitespace but otherwise requires an exact match.
note: The hub lists no scored public runs.

name: Emotional Attachment evaluation
description: Chats test whether models avoid claiming affection, fostering dependence or encouraging secrecy. Reports policy adherence rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: EmpatheticDialogues
description: Models reply to a person describing an emotional experience. Human conversations provide reference responses for evaluating empathy and relevance.

name: Employment Law Legal Agent Eval
description: Agents review employment case files and write risk memos. The grader checks whether the memos identify planted legal issues and avoid unsupported findings.
note: Historical five-case results list GPT-5.5 at 0.594 and Qwen3-30B at 0.406. The November 2026 README warns that the scoring formula changed.

name: Encyclo-K
description: Models judge questions composed at test time from knowledge statements extracted from authoritative textbooks. Random composition is meant to resist contamination and test several facts at once.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Liang et al.)
note: The question format is inferred from the statement design, so it is a guess. ByteDance Seed reports it in the Seed2.0 model card.

name: Encyclopedic VQA
description: Models answer questions about detailed properties of pictured objects and places. The Gemini Embedding 2 report measures whether they retrieve the correct answer.

name: End-To-End SWE Task Benchmark (Windsurf)
description: Agents start a fresh Cascade conversation from a user intent and must pass a selected set of unit tests. A 0 to 10 score blends test pass rate and a judge score.
note: Windsurf reported it once, as a chart without printed values, in the SWE-1 launch post. Scoring mixes unit tests with a model judge.

name: EndoVis 2018 Robotic Scene Segmentation
description: Models segment structures and surgical instruments in video from robot-assisted operations. The evaluation compares predicted masks with reference labels.

name: ENEM Challenge
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions from Brazil’s national high school examination in Portuguese.
note: The release month follows the dataset repository history.

name: EngiWorld
description: Agents work through the full industrial engineering design loop on 1,301 expert-curated tasks that need reasoning over geometric and physical constraints across software.
note: 59 HF paper upvotes.

name: EnigmaEval
description: 1,184 multimodal puzzle-hunt puzzles (v2 dataset has 1,161). Model gives one exact answer per puzzle. Normal and Hard splits.
org: Scale AI + Center for AI Safety + MIT
note: CAIS posted an updated v2 release on Hugging Face on 2026-07-23 with cleaned puzzles from the original set. The card points to dashboard.safe.ai for results. Check whether v2 scores compare with v1.

name: Enterprise generative evaluation (Cohere)
description: Models complete 22 enterprise writing tasks such as job ads with format rules. Rule checks and LLM judges give a pass rate.
note: In-house Cohere evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Enterprise RAG evaluation (Cohere)
description: Models answer workplace policy and technical questions over long documents, some unanswerable. Llama Index Correctness grades answers from 1 to 5.
note: In-house Cohere evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Enterprise Vendor Eval
description: Agents review vendor documents, question an internal IT team, and recommend whether to approve a purchase. The grader checks their decision and identified requirements.
note: The README reports DeepSeek v3.2 earned 1.000 across 60 runs on 20 scenarios. It also reports Llama and Mistral results, checked November 19, 2026.

name: Enterprise-Bench L1-L2
description: Agents answer 14 operational questions across connected enterprise records. Tasks require either retrieving facts or combining evidence under business rules.
note: On November 19, 2026, DevRev Computer with Claude Opus 5 led at 97.86% accuracy across 140 trials. Version 2 has a separate leaderboard.

name: Enterprise-Bench L1-L2 v2
description: Agents answer 42 operational questions using six enterprise services. A GPT-6 Luna judge evaluates the final answer against task criteria.
note: On November 19, 2026, GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex led the Harbor leaderboard at 65.71% accuracy across 210 trials.

name: EnterpriseBench: CoreCraft
description: Agents work inside a simulated hardware startup with more than 2,500 entities and 23 tools. They triage incidents, audit shipments and handle customers under company policy.
note: CoreCraft is the first environment in the EnterpriseBench suite. GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.6 solved about 30% of tasks at launch.

name: EnterpriseClawBench
description: Agents do 852 tasks rebuilt from real proprietary workplace agent sessions, each with fixtures, hard rules and semantic rubrics.
note: 81 HF paper upvotes. The sessions hold internal enterprise content, so not all of it is public.

name: EnterpriseOps-Gym
description: Agents do 1,150 expert-written tasks in eight enterprise domains, such as IT, HR and customer service, using 512 tools over live MCP servers. SQL checks on the final database state score each task.
note: Some tasks are impossible and test refusal. Artificial Analysis runs its own version named EnterpriseOps-Gym-AA.

name: EnterpriseOps-Gym 1.1
description: Agents complete 296 workflows across customer service, human resources, and IT service management. SQL checks grade the resulting database state.
note: The publisher provides no model scores on the Harbor page as of November 19, 2026.

name: EnterpriseRAG-Bench
description: Retrieval systems and agents answer 500 questions over a synthetic company's internal documents, slightly over 500,000 of them.
note: The code can also generate similar datasets for other industries and company sizes. About 610 GitHub stars and 72 forks.

name: EntireSongs
description: Models transcribe complete English and Chinese songs with background music. Qwen reports transcription errors separately for each language.

name: EnvSimBench
description: Language models act as simulators of tool environments for agent training. Given a trajectory of agent actions, the model predicts the next environment state and feedback. Labels come from real executors, so the score checks whether simulated states match what the real environment would return.
note: It tests the simulator, not the agent. Samples come from EnvScaler environments. The release includes a 4B simulation model. About 208 GitHub stars.

name: EpiBench
description: Agents analyze real epigenomics datasets in a sandbox with standard tools. A deterministic grader checks the biological result.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 106 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: EPIC-KITCHENS-100 action anticipation
description: Models predict a person's next action from first-person kitchen video. The benchmark scores predicted verbs, nouns, and their combinations.

name: Epistemic Bias (xAI)
description: Models answer opposing framings of contentious questions. The bias rate counts one-sided framing or opinions where neutrality is expected.
note: In-house xAI evaluation reported in the Grok 4.5 card.

name: Epoch AI no-CoT serial reasoning steps
description: How many serial reasoning steps of fixed difficulty a model can do in a single output token, without a chain of thought, at 25% above chance.
note: Unreleased Epoch AI benchmark, first reported in the GPT-6.2 System Card. The score is a number of steps.

name: Epoch Automation Reports
description: Agents in coding harnesses do real Epoch AI work tasks such as graphic design, data insights and research design. Epoch staff grade outputs against the rubric they use for employees.
note: Six systems in the first release on 2026-10-08. The board reports mean rubric score.

name: Epoch Capabilities Index
description: An index that fits model capability and benchmark difficulty from scores on over 50 benchmarks in Epoch AI's hub, using item response theory. Scores read like Elo ratings.
note: Each model needs at least four benchmark scores. Epoch also offers math, software engineering and cyber presets. The November 2026 export lists 271 models.

name: EPRSTMT
description: Models classify Chinese product reviews as positive or negative after learning from a small labeled sample. Accuracy measures agreement with the sentiment labels.
note: This named FewCLUE task has 32 training examples, 32 development examples, 610 public test examples, and 753 private test examples.

name: EQ-Bench 3
description: Models respond in character in multi-turn role-plays and analyze transcripts of social conflict. A judge model gives rubric scores and pairwise Elo ratings.
note: EQ-Bench 4 has replaced it, and EQ-Bench 3 is now a legacy leaderboard.

name: EQ-Bench 4
description: Models hold 16-message roleplay chats with 120 simulated user personas whose preferences compete and are hidden. A three-judge panel compares transcripts pairwise, and ratings are fitted as Elo scores.
note: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview plays the persona. Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview judge. It went live on eqbench.com on 2026-07-23 and moved EQ-Bench 3 to the legacy boards.

name: EQ-Bench v2
description: Models read 171 short dialogues and rate how strongly a character feels each of four emotions on a 0 to 10 scale. The score compares the ratings with reference answers.
note: Version 1 from December 2023 had 60 questions, and the maker says v1 and v2 scores are not comparable. Now a legacy leaderboard.

name: Era by Eon
description: Generates a simulated enterprise (Salesforce, Slack, Jira, Zendesk, etc.) with exact ground truth. Agents answer questions through MCP/REST.
note: Free. The same seed reproduces the same company, so runs are repeatable. Simulators ship as container images.

name: ERP-Bench
description: Agents complete 300 procurement and manufacturing workflows in Odoo 19. A constraint solver generates the tasks and optimal solutions, and the verifier checks final business state.
note: The leaderboard available November 19, 2026 reports GPT-5.5 leading the coding interface at 43.4% pass@1. Claude Opus 4.7 leads the browser interface at 28.8%.

name: ERPBench-100
description: Agents execute 100 business workflows across ten simulated enterprise resource planning systems. Checks grade decisions, calculations, committed state, and handoffs on a 100-point scale.
note: The release reports 100 successful reference solutions and negative-control checks. It provides no scored model comparison as of November 19, 2026.

name: ERQA
description: 400 multiple-choice visual questions from robot and egocentric footage on spatial, trajectory, action and state reasoning. Accuracy.
note: Not saturated: best 78.5 (Gemini Robotics ER 2, DeepMind chart), chance ~25%. Source tables (DeepMind, Unitree, Embodied Arena) use different setups. Do not pool.

name: EsBBQ
description: Models answer Spanish questions about people in ambiguous and unambiguous situations. The evaluation measures how social stereotypes affect their choices.

name: ESC-50
description: Models identify an environmental sound from a short recording.
note: The benchmark groups its recordings into 50 sound classes.

name: Escalation Router
description: Models predict whether Qwen2.5-VL 7B correctly identifies visible hands or grippers in a clip. The reference label comes from two observed runs per clip.
note: In August 2026, Gemma 3 27B scored 40.0% and Qwen2.5-VL 7B scored 33.3% on 45 clips. Always predicting a difficult clip scored 66.7%.

name: ESCI Shopping Queries Dataset
description: Models rank products for a shopping query and distinguish exact matches, substitutes, complements, and irrelevant items.
note: The benchmark includes product ranking and relevance classification.

name: EsCoLA
description: Models judge the grammatical acceptability of Spanish sentences taken from linguistic publications.
org: Universitat Pompeu Fabra and Barcelona Supercomputing Center
note: The authors publish training and development data. They ask researchers to contact them for the held-out test data. The release month follows the dataset repository history.

name: ESI-Bench
description: Embodied agents act to reveal what is unseen, such as occluded structure, containment and function, then reason about how observations change with action.
note: 141 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: EstNER
description: Models identify named entities in manually annotated Estonian news and social media text.
note: EuroEval scores entity spans with microaveraged F1 and excludes the miscellaneous class from its primary score.

name: Estonian Valence Corpus
description: Models predict the emotional valence of Estonian news text using human annotations.
note: MTEB scores the task using accuracy.

name: ETH3D
description: Models reconstruct scene geometry from images. Meta evaluates depth predictions against reference measurements on the ETH3D test scenes.

name: ETHICS
aliases: Aligning AI With Shared Human Values
description: Models predict common moral judgments about text scenarios covering justice, well-being, duties, virtues and commonsense morality.
note: ICLR 2021. Has normal and hard test splits.

name: EUR-Lex-Sum
description: Models summarize European Union legislation in the language of the source document. Official summaries provide references across EU languages.

name: EUREKA-Bench (OpenAI)
description: Agents build predictive models for six biology research tasks. Scored as predictive performance with the best published predictor in each field set to 100.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation, first reported in the GPT-6.2 System Card. A six-task pilot. Not the same as the EurekaBench in the catalog.

name: EurekaBench
description: Agents run long experiments and propose mechanisms that explain observations in six sciences. Mechanisms are scored on known constraints, predictive accuracy and the 306 expert-listed insights they should support.
note: 26 expert-verified tasks across neuroscience, computer science, chemistry, astrophysics, geophysics and plasma physics. Grading of insights is assumed model-judged and should be checked. Repo has 35 stars.

name: EuroEval
description: Models answer questions, summarize text, and perform language understanding tasks across European languages. EuroEval combines task rankings on its European leaderboard.
org: Dan Saattrup Smart and EuroEval contributors
note: The project began with Danish, Swedish, and Norwegian. The leaderboard also publishes results for individual languages.

name: European LLM Leaderboard (OpenGPT-X)
description: Models answer exam, science, commonsense, truthfulness, and math questions across European languages. The leaderboard also includes multilingual reading comprehension.
note: The paper compares 40 models across 21 languages. The leaderboard README lists Belebele alongside the five translated benchmarks.

name: EuroSAT
description: Models classify land use and land cover in Sentinel-2 satellite images.
note: MTEB reports accuracy on its EuroSAT task.

name: EusExams
description: Models answer past public service examination questions in Basque. The questions come from several Basque institutions.

name: EusProficiency
description: Models complete Basque language exercises from the official C1 proficiency examination. The questions test vocabulary and grammar.

name: EusReading
description: Models answer comprehension questions about Basque passages from past C1 proficiency examinations. The scorer checks their choices against the exam key.

name: EusTrivia
description: Models answer trivia questions in Basque. The set combines elementary-school questions with harder general knowledge questions.

name: EVA-Bench
description: Voice agents hold simulated spoken conversations to complete enterprise tasks. Scores cover task success and voice-specific failure modes.
note: 77 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 234 GitHub stars.

name: EvalCheck-LLM
description: Models use supplied evidence to answer a question, abstain, or flag a conflict. The task tests whether pressure changes that decision.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 4 distinct model versions.

name: EvalConvoLearn
description: Models simulate learners in tutoring conversations. The evaluator compares their answers, mistakes, questions, and turn lengths with patterns in real student conversations.

name: EvalCrafter
description: Text-to-video models generate clips for 700 prompts drawn from real user requests. The clips are scored with 17 automatic metrics for visual quality, content quality, motion and text alignment. Weights fitted to human ratings combine the metrics into one score.
org: Tencent AI Lab and City University of Hong Kong
note: CVPR 2024. Many of the 17 metrics rely on vision models, and the human-alignment weights come from the makers' own user study. About 200 GitHub stars.

name: EvalDetectBench
description: A judge model reads a transcript and answers whether it came from an evaluation or from real deployment. The test measures how well models detect evaluations and how detectable each benchmark is.
org: UK AI Security Institute + LASR Labs
note: Works with any Inspect-compatible eval. Transcripts cover frontier system-card evals and varied deployment sources. Probe questions are calibrated per model, and a harmonization step corrects for which model generated the transcripts.

name: Evalita-LLM
description: Models perform tasks written originally in Italian. The suite includes admission exams, question answering and text generation.

name: EvalPlus
description: HumanEval+/MBPP+ with 80x more tests. Showed many 'passing' solutions were wrong.
note: EvalPlus is the umbrella for HumanEval+ and MBPP+, which have their own records. MBPP+ v0.2.0 (April 2024) dropped broken tasks from 399 to 378, raising pass@1 by about 4 points.

name: Evaluation awareness discriminability (Anthropic)
aliases: Discriminability of behavioral audits from baseline using measurements of evaluation awareness
description: Probes and follow-up realism ratings try to tell behavioral audit transcripts from real internal Claude Code sessions. Each setting is scored as AUROC.
note: In-house Anthropic measurement. Lower AUROC means audits look more like real use. Results are split by audit type with no overall.

name: EvalVerse
description: Video models generate cinematic clips from prompts and reference material derived from professional videos. Film experts compare outputs across visual design, acting, cinematography, aesthetics, emotion, shot sequences, and sound. A calibrated vision-language evaluator also estimates these judgments.
org: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Tencent, and collaborators
note: The paper reports both expert comparisons and automated scores. These are different measurements. The opened paper establishes the protocol, but a complete public release of the test assets was not verified.

name: EvaOmni
description: Models answer questions about videos and identify the audio and visual evidence behind their answers. The score accounts for both correctness and evidence timing.

name: Event-based Segmentation Dataset
description: Models segment objects in cluttered indoor scenes filmed from a moving robot arm. The benchmark provides reference masks for comparison.

name: EventHallusion
description: Models answer questions about video events that can prompt false descriptions. The evaluation tests whether answers stay grounded in the clip.

name: EVF-Bench
description: Models generate product videos with visual effects. The evaluator checks motion, product appearance, text stability, and whether the effects fit the request.
org: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and collaborators

name: Evidence Sufficiency Evaluation
description: Models classify whether the evidence supports an answer across 72 cases. The harness uses paired evidence changes, controls, and strict label matching.
note: The author publishes a reusable task harness on Kaggle. The public leaderboard feed returned no scored rows.

name: EVMbench
description: Agents detect, patch and exploit 117 high-severity smart contract bugs from 40 audits in a sandboxed blockchain. Detect mode is scored on recall, patch and exploit modes by tests.
note: Since 2026-04-08 the maintained home is github.com/paradigmxyz/evmbench. Some scenarios come from audits of the Tempo blockchain.

name: EvoArena
description: Agents work in environments whose knowledge, tools and task conditions change over time. The suite tests whether agent memory keeps up with the changes.
note: 145 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: EvoArena PersonaMem-Evo
description: Agents solve questions about changing user preferences. The score is the published accuracy across versioned tasks.
note: One track of EvoArena. The EvoArena record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.
