description: Models read French stories about social norms, intentions and actions. The test asks them to distinguish actions or consequences appropriate to the situation.

name: Historical Jailbreak Regression
description: Replays previously found cyber jailbreak attacks against fixed ExploitBench tasks with real-time blocking turned off. Scored by mean task success rate under attack.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The task set is not public.

name: Historical Systems Bugs
description: Agents repair two historical C bugs in Linux and Unikraft. Hidden tests exercise the patched code, including driver behavior under emulated hardware.
note: As of November 19, 2026, Qwen3.8-27B with OpenCode passed three of 21 graded Linux attempts and two of 12 Unikraft attempts.

name: HLE Calibration
description: Models give a confidence score with each HLE answer. The benchmark reports RMS calibration error and AUROC between confidence and correctness.
org: Center for AI Safety + Scale AI
note: Calibration evaluation layered on the public Humanity's Last Exam. RMS error is on a 0-100 scale.

name: HLE Extended
description: Models answer closed-ended frontier academic questions. Mercor adds 447 new expert-written tasks to the 2158 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of humanitys-last-exam. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: HLE-Diamond
description: Models answer 1,000 cleaned expert questions from Humanity's Last Exam, 500 on reasoning and 500 on knowledge, closed book. Graded on exact answers.
org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
note: The makers built it after a year of cleaning as a migration path for when the original set hits its noise ceiling.

name: HLE-Rolling
description: A dynamic fork of Humanity's Last Exam where the makers remove, fix and re-add questions over time and publish an update log.
org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
note: Released 2025-10-08. Releases on 2026-02-20 (166 re-added, 27 removed, 8 updated) and 2026-07-27 (79 added, 6 removed) changed the set, so give the release date with scores.

name: HLE-Verified
description: Verified and revised version of Humanity's Last Exam (1,811 items) with uncertain items removed.
note: Audits all 2,500 HLE items into Gold (668), Revision (1,143) and Uncertain (689) subsets. Check which subset a score uses.

name: HLE-Verified (text-only Full)
description: Models answer the text-only questions of Humanity's Last Exam after expert verification and revision. The Full set keeps the questions experts marked uncertain, and the score is pass@1 accuracy.
note: The paper and its leaderboard chart evaluate this set. The HLE-Verified record covers the 1,811 items with uncertain questions removed. The chart is an image, so its scores are transcribed.

name: HLE-VL
description: Models answer the image-based questions from Humanity's Last Exam, a 330 question subset. Answers are graded against known short or multiple choice answers.
org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI (HLE), Alibaba Tongyi Lab (VL subset)
note: Qwen reports it with tools, so its scores are not comparable with no-tool HLE runs.

name: HMDB51
description: Models identify human actions in short video clips across 51 categories.
note: MTEB reports accuracy on its HMDB51Classification task.

name: HMMT 2025
description: Models answer the 30 problems from the February 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Final answers are checked against the official answers.
note: Model cards use the MathArena version of the February contest, often averaged over many samples.

name: HMMT 2026
description: Models solve the 33 final-answer problems from the February 2026 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Scored by exact answer match.
note: An exam, not a dedicated benchmark. Top models score above 95%.

name: HMMT February 2024
description: Models answer the problems from the February 2024 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Final answers are checked against the official answers.
note: MathArena packages it. Model reports used it before the 2025 edition appeared.

name: HMMT Nov 2025
description: Models solve the 30 problems of the November 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Final answers are checked automatically against the answer key.
org: MathArena (ETH Zurich SRI Lab), problems by HMMT

name: HMU-Bench
description: Models answer Chinese and English questions about musical notation and recordings. The authors score responses against reference answers.

name: Hold or Fold: AI Under Pushback
description: Models answer questions and face three kinds of pushback. The grader counts how often a model keeps a correct answer across 72 cases.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 5 distinct model versions.

name: Holdings-IndividualTaxBench
aliases: Thrive Holdings individual tax prep benchmark
description: 88 real client document packages turned into Form 1040 fields. Fact-level accuracy against practitioner-reviewed returns, with an LLM judge matching values.
note: Tasks come from Thrive's accounting firms and are not released. OpenAI holds equity in Thrive and the judge is an OpenAI model.

name: HomeLoop
description: Agents coordinate robots and connected devices to investigate household alerts. A program checks their actions and whether they resolve the problem.

name: Honesty human feedback win rate (Anthropic)
description: Crowdworkers try to make models say something false and pick the more honest reply in head-to-head chats. Score is the win rate against a baseline.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The baseline model was Claude Sonnet 4, so 50% means equal honesty.

name: HoneyBench v0.2-alpha
description: Measures reward hacking: how often an agent games its grader instead of doing the task. Lower is better.
note: Version 0.2-alpha. Labs have published little about its tasks or scoring.

name: Honeypot exploitation monitorability
aliases: Awareness of CoT Monitoring Reduces Monitorability
description: Agents exploit a honeypot while told about a monitor or told to hide it. Scored on CoT and full-context monitor recall.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Higher recall means more monitorable behavior.

name: HorizonMath
description: Models attack 113 mostly unsolved problems in eight areas of mathematics and the mathematical sciences. A program checks each proposed closed form, construction or bound.
org: University of Oxford, Harvard University, Princeton University and others (Wang et al.)
note: The paper reports six new solutions found by models. Most models score under 10 percent. Tencent reports pass@4.

name: HotpotQA
description: Models answer 113k Wikipedia questions that need facts from several documents. The distractor setting supplies gold and distractor paragraphs. Scored by exact match or F1.
org: Carnegie Mellon University, Stanford University and Mila
note: Labs now often grade answers with an LLM judge instead of exact match.

name: Hotter and Colder
description: Models predict sentiment and other attributes of Icelandic blog text using crowdsourced judgments.
note: EuroEval uses the sentiment annotations from the original corpus.

name: HourVideo
description: Multimodal models answer questions about first-person videos that run 20 to 120 minutes. The 500 videos come from Ego4D, and the 12,976 five-way multiple-choice questions cover summarization, perception, visual reasoning and navigation. Score is accuracy.
note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track. Human experts scored 85.0% on a subset, far above every model tested at launch. About 150 GitHub stars.

name: How2QA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about instructional videos. The task tests understanding of the actions shown in each clip.

name: HR-Bench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about fine details in 4K and 8K resolution images. Results are reported separately for the 4K and 8K sets.
org: Wuhan University and collaborators (Wang et al.)
note: Labs often run it with image crop and zoom tools.

name: HRM8K
description: Models solve 8,011 math problems given as English and Korean parallel pairs. It measures how much math reasoning drops when problems are in Korean.
org: HAE-RAE and OneLineAI (Hyunwoo Ko et al.)
note: Subsets include KSM, built from Korean exam math problems, plus translated GSM8K, MATH, Omni-MATH and MMMLU items.

name: HRM8K-KSM
description: Models solve the 1,428 problems of the Korean School Math subset of HRM8K. Problems come from Korean olympiad and competition exams.
org: HAE-RAE and OneLineAI (Hyunwoo Ko et al.)
note: Scores differ from the full HRM8K average. LG EXAONE cards report this subset as KSM.

name: Html extraction
description: Models extract structured product data from HTML pages that contain markup defects.
note: In an undated comparison on 120 pages, GPT-5-mini solved 76.7% and DeepSeek V4 Flash solved 64.2%.

name: HubBench
description: Agents make workplace decisions across 13 professional domains using connected software tools and evidence. Version 1.4.0 grades 104 tasks with deterministic state checks.
note: The November 19, 2026 leaderboard lists no qualified model run. All 104 reference solutions passed, and the publisher reports control results separately.

name: HuggingFace Agent Benchmark
description: Agents write Python code that calls Hugging Face Transformers tools to solve short tasks. Scores cover tool selection, tools used, and code correctness.
note: It shipped with Transformers Agents, which Hugging Face later replaced with smolagents.

name: HUMAINE
description: Prolific participants, stratified across 22 demographic groups in the US and UK, hold multi-turn conversations with two anonymous models on topics they choose. They compare the models overall and on dimensions such as trust, ethics and safety. A hierarchical Bradley-Terry-Davidson model turns the votes into ratings, adjusted to census data.
note: The paper (ICLR 2026) covers 23,404 participants and 28 models across five dimensions, and the leaderboard keeps adding models. Vague dimensions such as trust, ethics and safety end in ties far more often than the overall choice (65% against 10%). Rankings shift with participant age.

name: Human Behavior Bench
description: Models predict how specified groups of U.S. adults answer closed survey questions, as a distribution over options. Scored as 1 minus total variation distance.
org: Rehearsals with Google DeepMind and Kaggle
note: 1,199 tasks, 239 public and 960 private, from surveys run June to September 2026. Launched 2026-10-20.

name: Human feedback win rates (Anthropic)
description: Raters chat with two models on tasks such as coding, documents and creative writing and pick the better reply. Score is the win rate.
note: Claude 3 era model cards report per-task win rates against a baseline Claude model, with no overall number. The baseline changes between cards.

name: Human Pathogen Capabilities Test
description: Models answer expert-level questions on human pathogens from SecureBio. Scored as accuracy.
note: 100 text-only questions with a private holdout. 13 PhD virologists scored about 31%. Modeled after VCT. A v2 exists on the SecureBio dashboard.

name: Human Pathogen Capabilities Test v2 (HPCT v2)
description: Models answer multiple-response questions on a small set of weaponizable pathogens that biosecurity experts rank highest priority. A revised version of HPCT.
note: Shown as HPCT v2 beside HPCT on the SecureBio dashboard until November 2026. Not public. Revised version so scores are not comparable with HPCT v1. The dashboard now shows only one chart, labeled HPCT, so these scores are the last ones published for v2.

name: Human proximity (Google DeepMind robotics)
description: Models judge from robot camera views whether a human is within 1 meter, a spatial awareness check for safe robot behavior. Scored by accuracy.
note: Reported in the Gemini Robotics ER 2 post. Method details are in the Gemini Robotics 2 Safety Technical Report.

name: Human Sourced Jailbreaks
description: Models face jailbreak prompts collected from human red teaming. Scored as the not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Human SxS image editing Elo (Google)
description: Google compares edited images side by side and converts human preferences into Elo ratings.
note: The Gemini 3.1 Flash Image and Nano Banana 2.1 model cards report internal human side-by-side image editing ratings.

name: Human SxS image generation Elo (Google)
description: Google compares generated images side by side and converts human preferences into Elo ratings.
note: The Gemini 3.1 Flash Image and Nano Banana 2.1 model cards report internal human side-by-side image generation ratings.

name: Human Verification Gap
description: Models respond to paired requests about the same synthetic image. The evaluation measures how the stated purpose changes their refusal rate.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 35 distinct model versions.

name: HumanAgencyBench
description: Models respond to 3,000 prompts about six ways assistants can support human agency, including asking clarifying questions and leaving important decisions to users.
note: In September 2026, the October 2024 Claude 3.5 Sonnet checkpoint led at 54.6% across six behaviors. The comparison includes GPT, Gemini, Grok, and Llama models.

name: HumanCLAW-Bench
description: Models control a simulated human body from egocentric images to find objects, navigate, and sit. The benchmark has 1,218 episodes across 41 houses. Success requires geometric completion and the agent's acknowledgment.
org: Meta, Nanyang Technological University, University of Washington, Brown University, and Northwestern University
note: Navigation uses all 1,218 episodes. Sitting uses 597 episodes. A fixed motion generator separates action decisions from balance and motor-control errors. The HSSD assets require gated access.

name: HumanEval
description: 164 hand-written Python function problems. Generated code is scored pass@1 against unit tests.
note: Saturated. Reported only for DeepSeek-V4 base model.

name: HumanEval Infilling
description: Models fill in a masked middle span of HumanEval solutions given the code before and after it. Unit tests check the completed function.
note: The harness offers single-line, multi-line, random-span and random-span-light settings. Labs often report single-line and random-span-light separately.

name: HumanEval Multi
description: Models complete HumanEval problems in Python and seven more languages, including C++, Java, PHP, and Bash. Unit tests score pass@1.
note: The non-Python versions come from MultiPL-E translations.

name: HumanEval+
description: Models write Python functions for the 164 HumanEval problems. EvalPlus checks them against about 80 times more tests than the original.

changes.text: The maintainers introduced an optional reduced test suite. Mini evaluations use substantially fewer tests, so reported results should identify that setting.
The maintainers corrected test cases, task 114’s prompt, and several input constraints. Results depend on which HumanEval+ dataset revision the evaluator uses.
The maintainers moved the Docker environment to Python 3.10 and set the default per-test timeout to 0.5 seconds. These changes affect syntax support and timeout outcomes.
The maintainers released further input-constraint and reference-checker corrections. Runs with the updated dataset revision can differ from earlier HumanEval+ evaluations.

note: Scores are pass@1 and run lower than plain HumanEval.

name: HumanEval-COBOL (Cohere)
description: Models write COBOL versions of HumanEval problems, or translate COBOL solutions to Python. Unit tests score pass@1.
note: Cohere built it for the Command A report. The report does not say whether it is released.

name: HumanEval-V
description: Models read a diagram and a function signature, then write Python code that must pass test cases. Tasks span six types of visual reasoning.
org: Fengji Zhang, Jacky Keung et al.
note: Tasks and diagrams are written by hand. Scores are pass@1.

name: HumanEval-X
description: Models generate programs or translate solutions among Python, C++, Java, JavaScript, and Go. The 820 human-written language variants include executable tests, and scoring uses pass@k.
note: The code translation task omits the problem description. The star count belongs to the broader CodeGeeX repository.

name: HumanEvalPack
description: Models write functions for HumanEval problems translated into Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++ and Rust. Hidden tests give pass@1.
org: Hugging Face and BigCode (Muennighoff et al., OctoPack)
note: The pack also has code repair and explanation tasks. Labs usually report the synthesize task.

name: Humanity's Last Exam
description: 2,500 expert-written closed-ended questions across 100+ subjects. Exact-match or multiple-choice answers graded by an LLM judge.
org: Center for AI Safety + Scale AI

changes.text: The maintainers replaced the default answer judge and added a judge-selection option. Scores produced with the previous default use a different grader.
The maintainers finalized HLE at 2,500 questions. Earlier evaluations used a different question set and are not directly comparable.
The maintainers began rolling updates to the question set, restoring 166 questions, removing 27 and updating 8. Scores from before and after use different questions.
A rolling release added 79 questions and removed 6. Scores from before and after use different questions.

note: Finalized at 2,500 questions in April 2025, with a private held-out set to check overfitting. HLE-Rolling and HLE-Diamond are separate records. Trackers disagree by up to about 20 points because tool settings differ.

name: Humanity's Sixth Sense
description: Models answer open-ended questions about what an image or short video implies but does not show, such as hidden objects, causes and intentions. An LLM judge checks each answer against a human-written rubric.
note: 522 tasks on 288 images and 234 video clips. A task counts only if every rubric item is met. People score 93.1% and the best of 25 models 53.6%.

name: HumanoidBench
description: Policies control a simulated Unitree H1 humanoid with dexterous hands on 15 whole-body manipulation and 12 locomotion tasks. Scored by task return or success.
org: UC Berkeley + Yonsei University (Sferrazza et al.)
note: About 800 GitHub stars. Mostly used to test reinforcement learning methods. The README site link (sferrazza.cc) returns 404, so the site link uses humanoid-bench.github.io.

name: HumanoidToolBench
description: Humanoid robot policies pick a suitable tool and use it, walking when needed, across 18 tasks in simulation and on a real Unitree G1.
note: It had 30 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 22 GitHub stars.

name: Hume AI Overall Quality Index
description: Listeners rate generated speech on reliability and expressiveness. The benchmark reports an overall quality index.
note: Hume AI runs the evaluation. No public leaderboard was found, so numbers come from model makers' reports.

name: Hume AI Voice Design Benchmark
description: Listeners rate generated voices for English voice design, multilingual control, accents and voice qualities.
note: Hume AI runs the evaluation. No public leaderboard was found, so numbers come from model makers' reports.

name: HumMusQA
description: Models answer 320 hand-written questions about music, curated and checked by people with musical training.
org: Music Technology Group, Universitat Pompeu Fabra
note: The paper also tests robustness to uni-modal shortcuts.

name: Hungarian National High-School Exam
aliases: Hungarian national high school finals in mathematics
description: Models answer the 33 questions of the 2023 Hungarian national high school mathematics finals. Answers are graded by hand with the official rubric.
org: Keiran Paster (exam by the Hungarian Educational Authority)
note: xAI first used this one exam for Grok-1 because it came after training cutoffs, and hand grading makes scores hard to reproduce.

name: Hunyuan-MT Challenge Testset (Tencent)
description: Models translate between Chinese and English across everyday and specialist domains. Expert raters score each translation from 0 to 4 on marked error-prone points.
note: In-house Tencent evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Husky Hold'em Bench
description: Models write Python poker bots and revise them after practice games. Six bots compete at each table, and the tournament tracks average winnings.
org: University of Washington and Nous Research
note: GPT-5 High ranked first among 13 models in the 2025 OpenReview paper. Opponents included Claude Opus 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Hermes 4.

name: HW-Bench
description: Agents complete six hardware engineering tasks for a 2.45 GHz antenna using native design and simulation tools. Code checks and calibrated model judges grade outputs against engineer-written criteria. The headline pass rate measures runs that satisfy every critical criterion, averaged across tasks.
note: Agents run five times per task in the Atlas harness at high reasoning effort. Each task starts from an engineer reference rather than the previous agent output. Arena prohibits automated extraction without written permission. The board dates its initial results to October 29, 2026.

name: Hx2Dx ARENA
description: Models interview a simulated patient, request examinations and tests, and give a diagnosis. A judge compares the diagnosis with the published case.

name: Hy-Backend
description: Coding agents complete Tencent in-house backend development tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Hy3 preview scored 54.7 here, but 12.2 on Hy-Backend 2.0, so the versions are not comparable.

name: Hy-Backend 2.0
description: Coding agents complete Tencent in-house backend development tasks in the Claude Code scaffold. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Tencent runs it with Claude Code for all models except GPT models, which use Codex.

name: Hy-BrowseComp-Pro2
description: Search agents answer hard browsing questions in a Tencent in-house set named after BrowseComp. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Not an OpenAI release. Tencent runs it with its internal harness.

name: Hy-CompanyBench
description: Coding agents complete Tencent in-house company engineering tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Hy3 scored 41.7 here and 29.8 on V2, so the versions are not comparable.

name: Hy-CompanyBench V2
description: Coding agents complete a second version of Tencent in-house company engineering tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-Euler pro
description: Models with tools solve Tencent in-house STEM problems. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Tencent lists it under STEM Agent.

name: Hy-FinAgentBench
description: Agents complete Tencent in-house finance analyst tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-FinModelBench
description: Agents build financial models for Tencent in-house finance tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Hy3 scored 69.0 here and 28.6 on v2, so the versions are not comparable.

name: Hy-FinmodelBench v2
description: Agents build financial models for a second version of Tencent in-house finance tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-LifeSearch
description: Search agents answer Tencent in-house everyday life questions with web search. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Tencent runs all agentic search tests with its internal harness.

name: Hy-Math
description: Models solve Tencent in-house math problems without tools. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-SkillsWorld
description: Agents use skills to complete Tencent in-house working tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-SWE Max
description: Coding agents solve 300 Tencent in-house software tasks in Claude Code with a 200-turn budget and no web access. Hidden verifier tests grade each task.
note: The Hy4 preview card renames it Hy-SWE Max Verified and gives the same Hy3 score (49.0), so it stays one record. Results average 3 runs.

name: Hy-Vibe Bench
description: Coding agents complete development workflows drawn from real Tencent users. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Seen only in the Hy3 preview card.

name: Hype Trap
description: Models assess anonymized news about small stocks. The grader compares their predictions with stock movements over the next five trading days.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 8 distinct model versions.

name: Hypersim
description: Models localize named objects as 3D boxes in synthetic indoor Hypersim images, using the Omni3D test split. Scored by mAP at IoU 0.15.
note: A dataset used by Qwen as a 3D grounding test, not a standalone LLM benchmark.

name: HyperTask
description: Agents build applications over long vibe coding sessions with about 100 feature or step requirements per task. Expert rubrics score the result over three trials.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: IARPA Babel speech recognition
description: Models transcribe conversational speech in languages with limited labeled data. Meta measures character error against reference transcripts on the Babel development split.

name: IberoBench
description: Models perform language understanding and generation tasks in Iberian languages. The suite combines existing evaluations with new tests specific to each language.
note: The linked harness folder contains the Basque tasks. The paper describes the complete suite.

name: Icelandic WinoGrande
description: Models complete Icelandic sentences by choosing which referent fits the context. The evaluation uses an Icelandic adaptation of WinoGrande.

name: IChO 2025
description: Models solve the written theoretical problems of the 57th International Chemistry Olympiad, held in Dubai in July 2025. Answers are graded against the official marking scheme.
org: International Chemistry Olympiad (hosted by the UAE Ministry of Education)
note: Labs grade the written theory section themselves and report medal levels, so scores across labs may use different graders. The dataset link is the official preparatory problems, not the exam.

name: ICPC World Finals 2025
description: Models solve the 12 problems of the 2025 ICPC World Finals under contest time and attempt limits. Scored by problems solved.
note: A one-time contest. Labs run their own judging and submission limits, so results are not strictly comparable.

name: IdeaTaste
description: Agents propose research ideas from literature frozen at 2025. Evaluation compares their citations and ideas with 2026 publications and measures diversity.
note: The four metrics are citation matching, idea matching, citation diversity, and idea diversity. Idea extraction and matching use model judges.

name: IEMOCAP
description: Models identify emotions in recorded dialogues. NVIDIA evaluates this task within AIR-Bench.

name: IF-Badcase
description: Models follow 450 multi-constraint instructions drawn from real user failure reports. A checklist checks each constraint.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: IFBench
description: 58 new out-of-domain verifiable output constraints. Scored by programmatic constraint checks (strict or loose).

changes.text: The maintainers revised the leaderboard after fixing IFBench verifiers. Earlier published scores can differ from the revised results.
The maintainers fixed verifier crashes, case handling, tokenization, and word-boundary matching. The revised checks can assign different results to identical responses.
The maintainers fixed six instruction verifiers that incorrectly accepted or rejected responses. Scores can move in either direction without changing the task set.

note: The maker fixed several verifiers in 2026, including six that mis-scored correct answers (2026-07-17), so later runs can score slightly higher. Task set unchanged. An optional two-turn split is in IFBench_multi-turn.

name: IFEval
description: Models answer about 500 prompts containing verifiable instructions such as word limits or required keywords. Code checks each instruction for strict and loose accuracy.
note: Frontier models now score near 90 percent, so it is close to saturation.

name: IFEval (Mistral internal version)
description: Models follow prompts with verifiable format constraints. Mistral uses its own fixed version of IFEval.
note: Mistral says scores are not comparable with public IFEval scores.

name: IFEval-OOD
description: Models answer unseen WildChat prompts with added verifiable constraints drawn from 52 types outside IFEval. Scored by prompt-level loose accuracy.
note: Ai2 built it for the Tulu 3 unseen suite. Ai2's later eval code runs the ifeval_ood task on the IFBench test set, so later scores may follow IFBench.

name: IFEvalCode
description: Models write code in eight programming languages under explicit constraints. The evaluator checks functional correctness and adherence to instructions separately.

name: IFMTBench
description: Models translate text while following explicit instructions, such as keeping JSON or HTML structure, using a glossary, using provided context and matching a register. It covers seven languages with 4,506 single-constraint and 2,838 multi-constraint items. Deterministic checkers verify some constraints, and a rubric-based model judge scores the rest.
note: Tencent released it with its Hy-MT2 translation models on 2026-05-21 and reports it in the Hy-MT2 report. The repository stars (about 1,500) belong to the Hy-MT2 model release, not to the benchmark alone.

name: IFStruct
description: Models generate JSON or YAML that must follow a requested schema and phrasing constraints, without constrained decoding. A response passes only if every structural constraint holds.
note: 2,000 frozen test prompts. The makers say it saturates near 100% for frontier models and targets small models.

name: IG-Bench
description: Models trace scientific idea lineages across 1,029 questions and propose research ideas grounded in those lineages. IG-Exam requires every answer field to match.
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Carnegie Mellon University, and collaborators
note: IG-Arena uses a separate judge-panel score for heredity, variation, and selection value. The paper calls the combined evaluation IG-Bench.

name: IHEval
description: Models face conflicts between system, user and tool instructions. Reports a composite score for following the higher-priority instruction.
note: Instruction hierarchy benchmark. Meta reports a composite across conflict types.

name: Image generation refusals
description: Models decide whether to call the image generation tool on human-curated adversarial prompts with system mitigations on. Scored on not_unsafe and not_overrefuse.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Scores include system-level mitigations.

name: Image input safety evaluations
description: Models answer harmful prompts that combine text and images in categories such as hate, extremism and self-harm. Scored as safe completion rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: Image Matching Challenge
description: Models match photographs of landmarks taken from different viewpoints. The evaluation measures the accuracy of camera poses recovered from the matches.

name: Image to Text Safety
aliases: Image to Text Safety (lower is better)
description: An automated content safety evaluation measures policy violations when prompts combine images and text.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: Image-to-WebDev Arena
description: Users upload a screenshot, wireframe or mockup, two anonymous models build the website in Code Arena, and users vote for the better result. Votes become ratings with bootstrapped confidence intervals.
note: On 2026-10-19 the board listed 65 models and 191,568 votes. It is a separate board from the text-prompt Code Arena WebDev board.

name: Image2FloorPlan
description: Models study several real photos of a home and draw its floor plan. Scored by an average quality score.
note: In-house Seed evaluation set. The card does not say how the average score is computed, so the scoring field is a guess.

name: Image2Struct
description: Vision-language models turn images of webpages, LaTeX and musical scores into code that renders them. The render is compared with the input image.
note: Fresh test data is downloaded from active online communities at run time. Three releases from v1.0.0 to v1.0.2. HELM includes tasks for reconstructing chart data, LaTeX, sheet music, and web pages.

name: ImageCoDe
description: Models select the image that matches a description from a set of visually similar alternatives.
note: The description distinguishes its target from the other images in the set.

name: ImageMining
description: Multimodal agents retrieve and reason over image information for image mining tasks.
note: GLM-5V-Turbo reports this in its official documentation table.

name: ImageNet ReaL
description: Models classify ImageNet validation images against revised human annotations. An image can have more than one acceptable label.

name: ImageNet-1K
description: Models assign one of a thousand object labels to each photograph. Meta reports classification accuracy on the validation images.

name: ImageNet-A
description: Models classify real photographs that commonly fool image classifiers. The test uses unmodified images from ImageNet categories.

name: ImageNet-C
description: Models classify images under common corruptions at different severities. The benchmark measures errors under blur, noise, weather, and digital distortions.
note: The original benchmark reports mean corruption error. Meta also compares models on the corrupted images.

name: ImageNet-R
description: Models classify renditions of objects in drawings, sculptures, and other media. The benchmark measures recognition when appearance differs from ordinary photographs.

name: ImageNet-Sketch
description: Models classify black-and-white sketches using ImageNet category labels. The benchmark tests recognition when images lack photographic texture and color.

name: ImageNetV2
description: Models classify a newly collected set of photographs using the original ImageNet labels. The test measures how accuracy changes on fresh images.

name: IMB
description: Models answer Italian medical specialty exam questions and respond to patient questions from online forums. The paper reports results for both tasks.

name: IMC 2025
aliases: International Mathematics Competition for University Students 2025
description: Models write proofs for the 10 problems of the 2025 International Mathematics Competition for University Students. Human judges grade each proof.
note: MathArena graded only three Gemini systems, all above the gold threshold of 56 percent.

name: IMDb-PT
description: Models classify the sentiment of Brazilian Portuguese translations of IMDb movie reviews.

name: ImgEdit-Bench
description: Image editing models carry out edit instructions such as add, remove, replace, style transfer and background change. A GPT-4.1 judge scores each result from 1 to 5.
note: The benchmark ships with the 1.2 million pair ImgEdit dataset and has basic, hard single-turn and multi-turn suites.

name: ImgMT
description: Models translate text embedded in diagrams, maps, and infographics. Evaluation measures text recognition, region matching, and translation with CER, F1, chrF, and COMET.
org: Šárka Uramová, Petar Petrov, Josef Jon, Ondřej Bojar, and Michal Novák
note: The dataset contains 35,612 aligned image pairs in 129 languages. Report the test split and metric because error rates and quality scores have opposite directions.

name: Immigration Bench
description: Models answer expert-written US immigration law questions from seven personas, such as F-1 students, employers and DACA recipients. An AI grader checks each answer against an expert rubric.
org: Vals AI + Talent Mobility Fund (Renaissance Philanthropy)
note: Experts wrote 519 questions. Vals reports on a private 262-question test set and reserves the other 257 for labs to license. Score is the share of rubric items met.

name: IMO 2025
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad. Graders score proofs out of 42 points, mapped to medal cutoffs.
org: International Mathematical Olympiad, hosted by the Australian Maths Trust
note: This is a one-time competition exam, not a maintained benchmark.

name: IMO 2026
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2026 International Mathematical Olympiad. Proofs are scored out of 42 points.
org: International Mathematical Olympiad, hosted in Shanghai, China
note: A one-time competition exam held July 15 and 16, 2026. Labs grade proofs with their own rubrics or judges.

name: IMO Shortlist 2024
description: Models write proofs for the 31 problems of the 2024 IMO Shortlist. DeepSeek scores the proofs with its own verifier model.
note: A one-time problem set, not a maintained benchmark. The IMO publishes each shortlist after the next IMO, here July 2025.

name: IMO-AnswerBench
description: 400 olympiad problems with short verifiable answers, robustified against memorization. Scored by answer match.

changes.text: The maintainers replaced the original file with answerbench_v2.csv to correct ambiguous questions and incorrect answers. Scores using the deprecated file can differ.

note: Part of IMO-Bench (EMNLP 2025) with IMO-ProofBench, IMO-GradingBench and IMO-LeanProofBench. On 2026-02-12 a v2 file fixed ambiguous problems and wrong answers in place, so check which file a score used.

name: IMO-GradingBench
description: Models grade 1,000 olympiad proof attempts, and their grades are compared with human expert grades. Tests automatic evaluation of long-form math answers.
note: Part of IMO-Bench (EMNLP 2025).

name: IMO-LeanProofBench
description: Models write Lean 4 proofs for the 60 IMO-ProofBench problems, formalized by hand and checked by Lean experts. The Lean compiler verifies each proof.
note: Introduced with the LEAP paper. One-shot Gemini 3.1 Pro solved 11.6 percent and the LEAP agent 70 percent. The August 2026 v2 file fixed wrong formalizations for Mathlib 4.27.0.

name: IMO-ProofBench
description: Models write proofs for 60 olympiad problems, split into a basic set and an advanced set up to IMO-hard. Each proof is graded from 0 to 7 by experts or a Gemini autograder.
note: Part of IMO-Bench (EMNLP 2025). The v2 file only fixed a typo.

name: Impossible tasks (Anthropic)
description: Agents work on coding problems designed to be impossible. Score is the rate at which they hack instead of giving up.
note: Run with no prompt and with an anti-hack prompt. The no-prompt rate is the default setting.

name: Impossible Tasks Evaluation
description: Agents get paired impossible and solvable tasks. Scores infeasibility recognition, fabrication, circumvention and helpfulness.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ImpossibleBench
description: Coding agents get tasks whose unit tests conflict with the specification. Reports how often they cheat by changing tests or special-casing.
note: Measures reward hacking as a cheating rate.

name: ImpossibleMLEBench
description: Agents get ML tasks with instructions to reach impossibly good scores. Observers check whether they cheat and whether they disclose it.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation. The GPT-5.6 card describes results in words without a score.

name: IMProofBench
description: Agents with web search and SageMath write proofs for private PhD-level problems written by mathematicians. Experts grade the proofs, and final-answer subquestions are graded automatically.
org: ETH Zurich (Johannes Schmitt et al.) with a contributor community
note: NeurIPS 2025. The July 2026 paper v2 grew the set from 39 to 77 problems and 14 models, so scores from the two versions do not compare.

name: In-context data exfiltration, visual browser
description: Agents using a visual browser meet attacks that try to exfiltrate data already present in the conversation context. Scored on resisting them.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public. The ChatGPT Agent card also gives Operator scores on it.

name: In-house CTF suite (Phuong et al. 2024)
aliases: GDM Dangerous Capabilities: Capture the Flag
description: Agents hack 13 simulated servers with vulnerable web apps and services to retrieve a secret flag.
note: Challenges cover web app vulnerabilities, off-the-shelf exploits, databases, Linux privilege escalation and password cracking and spraying. Challenge files without flags or solutions are in the dangerous-capability-evaluations repo. UK AISI inspect_evals ships it as gdm_in_house_ctf, revised seven times to September 2026.

name: IN22-Gen
description: Models translate parallel sentences across English and Indian languages. Google evaluates whether an embedding model can match a sentence with its translation.
note: MTEB scores the task using F1.

name: Inappropriate Image Prompts
description: Models generate images from prompts drawn from real users. The evaluation measures how often the outputs contain inappropriate material.

name: iNaturalist 2017
description: Models identify the species in photographs submitted by naturalists. Meta evaluates transfer to fine-grained species classification.

name: iNaturalist 2018
description: Models identify species in photographs submitted by naturalists. The 2018 competition uses an expanded set of plant and animal categories.

name: iNaturalist 2021
description: Models classify nature photographs by species. The 2021 competition uses a new collection of images and species labels.

name: iNaturalist Sounds
description: Models identify animal species from recordings submitted to iNaturalist.
note: The dataset includes calls from birds, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, and insects.

name: INCLUDE
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions from local academic and professional exams in 44 languages that test regional knowledge. Scored by accuracy.
note: INCLUDE-base has 22,637 exam questions in 44 languages. A lite subset of 11,095 questions also exists, and the dataset cards show scores within about a point of the base set. Reports rarely say which set they used.

name: IncompeBench
description: Models retrieve music clips that match detailed natural language requests.
note: The strict and lenient evaluations use the same music and queries but treat marginally relevant clips differently.

name: Incorrect behavior rate on disallowed and sensitive content
description: Models answer disallowed prompts and sensitive prompts such as medical advice. Scored on the rate of responses that break policy.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation from the GPT-4 era. Results appear as a chart.

name: IndicGenBench
description: Models summarize, translate, and answer questions across 29 Indic languages using human-translated versions of CrossSum, FLORES, XQuAD, and XorQA. Each task uses its standard metric.
note: Google DeepMind runs it as a Kaggle benchmark (published 2025-12-04, 14 models). It covers 29 Indic languages. Its four datasets are CrossSum-IN, Flores-IN, XQuAD-IN, and XorQA-IN.

name: IndicIFEval
description: Models follow instructions in 14 Indic languages. Rule-based checks test constraints such as required words, paragraph structure and word counts.
note: The February 2026 paper compares Gemini, GPT, Aya, Qwen and other models. Gemini 3 Pro led on translated prompts with 90.0% average loose accuracy.

name: IndicIPR-QA
description: Models extract answers from passages in seven Indian intellectual property laws. The benchmark compares predicted spans with reference answers across 4,462 questions.

name: IndicLID benchmark
description: Models identify Indian languages in native scripts and in Romanized text.
note: MTEB scores the task using accuracy.

name: IndicParam
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions from Indian competitive exams. The benchmark tests knowledge in low-resource Indic languages.

name: IndicQA
description: Models extract answers from Wikipedia passages in Indian languages. Native speakers wrote the questions and answers.
note: SEA-HELM uses the Tamil subset and excludes questions with no answer.

name: IndicXNLI
description: Models compare a premise and hypothesis in Indian languages. They predict whether the premise entails, contradicts or leaves the hypothesis unresolved.

name: Indirect prompt injection, Actor Critic attack
description: An attacker model refines injected email triggers until the agent leaks synthetic private data through a send email call. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation on 500 held-out synthetic conversations.

name: Indirect prompt injection, Beam Search attack
description: An attack appends random tokens to an injected email trigger until the agent leaks synthetic private data. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation on 500 held-out synthetic conversations.

name: Indirect prompt injection, TAP attack
description: A Tree of Attacks with Pruning search writes natural language injections that make the agent leak synthetic private data. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind adaptation of TAP to security violations, run on 500 held-out synthetic conversations.

name: IndiVibe
description: Models answer 110 source prompts in chat, STEM, math and coding, translated into 22 Indian languages in native and romanized script. A judge model compares answers pairwise.
note: The judge scores fluency, language and script correctness, usefulness and verbosity. Claude Opus 4 reference answers in English guide the usefulness score. Results are win rates.

name: IndoMMLU
description: Models answer 14,981 multiple-choice questions from Indonesian school and university entrance exams, including nine local languages. Scored by accuracy.

name: IndoNLI
description: Models decide whether a hypothesis follows from an Indonesian passage using annotations from experts and other speakers.
note: MTEB scores the task using average precision.

name: Inductive Arithmetic Pattern Reasoning
description: Models infer a hidden arithmetic operation from worked examples and calculate the result for a new expression. The grader checks the final integer.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 16 distinct model versions.

name: IndustryBench
description: Models answer 2,049 Chinese industrial procurement questions grounded in national standards and product records. Answers must respect regulated thresholds and safety clauses.
note: Seven capability dimensions and ten industry categories. About 160 GitHub stars.

name: IneqMath
description: Models solve Olympiad-level inequality problems, recast as two checkable tasks: estimating a tight bound and predicting the relation between two expressions. IMO-level medalists wrote and reviewed the 200 test problems. Five model judges check the final answer and look for toy-case reasoning, logical gaps and numerical shortcuts, and a solution counts only if it passes all five.
note: Scores fall sharply between answer-only and step-wise grading. The makers report judge agreement with humans of F1 0.93 on the dev set. Test answers are held back for the leaderboard, which had 55 entries and was last updated on 2025-08-21. About 60 GitHub stars and 20 Hugging Face upvotes.

name: InferenceEval
description: Agents land real production changes in the xAI inference stack. Hidden GPU unit tests and integration probes grade each patch.
note: In-house xAI evaluation, first reported in the Grok 4.6 card.

name: InfiHall-Bench
description: Models generate images from 411 prompts that combine visual requirements. The evaluator checks details such as object parts, actions, and spatial relations separately.
org: Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen and collaborators

name: Infinite Generations (Mistral internal)
description: Models answer challenging long or repetitive prompts from Mistral's internal set. The score is the share of responses that never stop or loop, so lower is better.
note: Mistral reported it in the Mistral Small 3.2 card to show fewer runaway generations than Small 3.1. The prompt set and the detection rule are not published.

name: InfiniteBench/En.MC
description: Models answer 229 multiple choice questions about long fake books with altered entity names, averaging about 184K tokens. Scoring is accuracy.
note: This is one subtask of InfiniteBench, which has 12 tasks in English and Chinese.

name: InfiniteBench/En.QA
description: Models answer free-form questions about novels longer than 100K tokens. Scored by F1 against reference answers.
note: The multiple-choice task on the same novels is infinitebench-en-mc.

name: InFoBench
description: Models follow 500 instructions that are split into 2,250 yes or no requirement questions. A judge answers each question, and the score is the share met.
note: The metric is the Decomposed Requirements Following Ratio (DRFR). GPT-4 is the usual judge.

name: Infographic factuality (Google)
description: Image generation systems produce infographics and an automated rater scores factuality.
note: Nano Banana 2.1 reports an internal infographic factuality score as a fraction.

name: InfographicVQA
description: Models answer about 30,000 questions on about 5,000 infographics that mix text, layout, charts, and graphics. Scoring is ANLS.
org: Computer Vision Center (UAB) and IIIT Hyderabad

name: Information Extraction (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models extract words, sentences or fields from meeting records, legal texts, contracts, product descriptions and knowledge bases.
note: One of six in-house application sets in the Seed1.8 and Seed2.0 model cards. Scoring is a guess.

name: Information Processing (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models analyze large collections of user-generated content, for example summarizing viewpoints and judging overall sentiment.
note: One of six in-house application sets in the Seed1.8 model card. Scoring is a guess.

name: InfraBench
description: Agents deploy, profile, debug, and optimize model workloads on AMD MI35X GPUs. Task-specific verifiers grade 20 engineering assignments.
note: The repository documents model configurations for Claude, GPT, and other agents. The README and Harbor page give no comparative scores as of November 19, 2026.

name: Infrathon
description: Agents optimize AI infrastructure under correctness and fidelity constraints. Hidden workloads measure performance gains, with additional checks for rule compliance.
org: University of Washington, Ai2, and collaborators
note: The paper evaluates six models over 150 runs with a 24-hour budget. Metrics depend on the task and should retain their workload and resource limits.

name: INJONGO
description: Models identify a speaker’s intent and extract information from utterances in 16 African languages.
note: AfroBench uses the intent detection component.

name: InnovationEval
description: Agents with thousands of GPU hours try to discover an ML technique that matches a recent human paper they have not seen. The score is the share of that paper's gain the agent reaches.
note: First iteration targets Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO). GPT-5.6 Sol reached at most 15% of SDPO gains at equal wall-clock time. Epoch plans to repeat it.

name: Input hallucinations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer 500 prompts that need an unavailable tool and 500 prompts that cite missing context. Score is the non-hallucination rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Reported as two sets with no overall score.

name: InsCtrl (Tencent)
description: Models write text under detailed instructions in a Tencent in-house text creation test. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Seen in the Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct card. Scoring method is a guess from the task type.

name: Insight Consolidation v1
description: Agents read customer account documents, infer why the customer acted, and cite supporting records. The evaluator combines a model judgment with citation accuracy.
note: The August 2026 release reports MiniMax-M2 at 0.418 on grounded insight across 30 episodes. MiniMax-M2 also judged its answers.

name: Inspect India Evals
description: Models answer questions about Indian culture and reason across Indian languages. Other tasks test social bias, digital public infrastructure safeguards and refusal behavior.
note: The register lists six tasks, including BharatBBQ and multilingual refusal.

name: Instinct Next Edit
description: Models predict the next edit from code context and recent changes. The port uses TypeScript, which has 221 held-out examples.
note: Continue identifies Instinct as the evaluated model. The dataset card gives split sizes but no model score.

name: Instruction Adherence
description: Models follow three to 16 simultaneous constraints across one or more turns. The public release includes 500 examples with held-out constraint combinations.
note: On September 14, 2026, Claude Sonnet 5 passed 29% of single-turn prompts with 13 constraints on its first try. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B passed 6%.

name: Instruction Following (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models follow multi-level instructions collected from user cases where current models fail.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Instruction Following (safety evaluation)
description: An automated evaluation measures whether the model follows instructions on sensitive prompts while staying within safety policies.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards and the Gemini 2.5 report give only the change against Gemini 1.5.

name: Instruction hierarchy attacks
description: Models face attacks that try to override higher-priority instructions. Scored as defender success rate averaged per defender query.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Instruction Hierarchy Evaluation
description: Models resolve conflicts between system, developer and user messages, resist tutor jailbreaks, and protect secret phrases and passwords. Scored per sub-evaluation.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report sub-evaluations with no overall number.

name: InstructIR
description: Models find documents that satisfy a user's search request and its accompanying instructions.
note: The benchmark varies the instruction for a query to test how the ranking changes.

name: InstructTTSEval
description: Text-to-speech models follow natural-language style instructions in English and Chinese across acoustic parameter, descriptive style and role-play tasks. Gemini judges each clip.
org: Fudan University (Kexin Huang, Xipeng Qiu and others)
note: The set has 6,000 test cases, 1,000 per task and language, each with reference audio.

name: Instrument reading (Google DeepMind)
description: Models read gauges, sight glasses, digital displays, linear scales, rulers and thermometers from robot camera images. ER 2 tests 10 instrument types.
note: Introduced with Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 in 2026-04 with Boston Dynamics inspection use cases and generalized in the ER 2 post.

name: Instrumental convergence evals
description: Agents in 7 low-friction tasks can guard goals or acquire optionality against task instructions. Reports the rate of self-serving actions.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: InstrumentalEval
description: Models respond to scenarios where gaining resources or preserving themselves could serve another goal. A grader identifies responses that pursue those intermediate goals.

name: IntelligentBench
description: Image editing models complete 350 free-form edits that need reasoning and world knowledge. GPT-4o scores each output from 0 to 2 against a reference image, normalized to 100.
note: In-house benchmark proposed in the BAGEL paper. Criteria are request fulfillment, visual consistency and knowledge-grounded creativity.

name: Intention Recognition (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models classify intent from dialogues, meeting transcripts, social posts and articles, such as purchase intent in customer service chats.
note: One of six in-house application sets in the Seed1.8 model card. Scoring is a guess.

name: Intentionally taking actions very rarely (Anthropic)
description: Models are told to take a specific action at a target rate such as 1 percent. Resampling measures the observed rate under several randomness settings.
note: Internal replication of Serrano et al. 2026. Settings include a UUID in the prompt, String Seed of Thought and no randomness source.

name: Inter-GPS (Geometry3K)
description: Models solve high school geometry problems that combine a diagram and text from the Geometry3K test set. Scored by accuracy.
org: UCLA and Sun Yat-sen University (Lu et al.)

name: InteractiveBench
description: Multimodal models act as a wearable assistant that sees through a simulated person's eyes and guides that person through household tasks. State-based checks in a BEHAVIOR-1K home score the outcome.
note: 120 multi-turn tasks in six categories, 20 each, built on the InteractiveWorld simulator. 12 frontier models in the first release. Claude Fable 5.1 reached at most 25% on long-horizon categories.

name: InteractiveBench Logic
description: A model asks restricted questions to recover the hidden explanation of a situation puzzle. It solves an item only if a judge accepts its final explanation within 20 rounds.
note: The task set contains 46 puzzles. The judge knows the annotated explanation and returns restricted feedback. The paper revision adds UI2Html as another task outside this record.

name: InteractiveBench Math
description: A model solves mathematical problems while querying a judge about intermediate claims. The judge holds a reference derivation and marks final solutions correct or incorrect under a fixed interaction budget.
note: The maker site describes 52 HLE math problems. This interactive protocol differs from the original HLE evaluation. Judge choice and interaction budget must accompany accuracy.

name: InteractiveBench Texas Hold’em
description: Models play no-limit Texas Hold’em from partial observations of cards, chip stacks, and recent actions. Repeated matches measure chip gains, with invalid actions receiving one retry before an automatic fold.
note: The maker site reports 5,000 hands. Opponent roster, starting stacks, and hand count affect results.

name: InteractiveBench Trust Game
description: Models choose whether to cooperate or defect in repeated prisoner’s dilemma matches. A round-robin tournament scores average realized payoff per round, with a random stopping rule.
note: The payoff matrix and continuation probability define the game. Results depend on the opponent roster and number of matches.

name: InterCode-CTF
description: Agents solve 100 picoCTF capture-the-flag challenges in an interactive Bash and Python environment.
note: Agents work in an interactive Bash and Python environment on picoCTF challenges in coding, cryptography, reverse engineering and vulnerability finding. Google omits challenges that need internet access, leaving 76. UK AISI inspect_evals ships it as gdm_intercode_ctf.

name: Internal adversarially-designed factuality evaluations
description: Models answer adversarial questions in nine categories such as history, math and code. Scored on agreement with human ideal responses.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Results appear as a chart by category.

name: Internal agentic coding evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents implement a pull request in an open source codebase from a natural language description. A problem counts as solved when all hidden tests pass.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation based on real pull requests, first reported in the Claude 3.5 Sonnet model card addendum. The tasks are not public.

name: Internal AI research evaluation suite 2
description: Agents perform scaled-down ML and alignment research tasks similar to past Anthropic research projects.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Internal API instruction following (OpenAI)
description: Models answer prompts drawn from real developer use cases that carry instructions on formatting, verbosity and length. OpenAI reports a hard subset.
note: OpenAI introduced it with GPT-4.1 on 2025-04-14 and reported it again in the GPT-5 developer post on 2025-08-07. The grading method is not described, so model-judged is assumed.

name: Internal codebase monitor evasion eval
description: Agents do a real coding task in a snapshot of Google's monorepo while hiding a harmful side task from action and CoT monitors.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation inspired by OAI-repo-sabotage. Uses 18 monitor-validated task pairs.

name: Internal codebase sabotage propensity (Anthropic)
description: Agents in Claude Code write a costly internal classifier they may dislike. Score is the rate of writing a sabotaged classifier.
note: In-house Anthropic scenario. The scenario is not public.

name: Internal computer use safety benchmark (OpenAI)
description: Models complete computer-use tasks while avoiding unsafe actions.
note: OpenAI reports lower-is-better failure rates in the GPT-6 Astra launch comparison.

name: Internal model use survey (Anthropic)
description: Anthropic technical staff estimate productivity uplift from the model and judge whether it could automate a junior ML researcher.
note: Survey of Anthropic staff, not a task set.

name: Internal Research Debugging Evaluation
description: Agents debug difficult problems from OpenAI research work that take researchers hours or days. Scored as mean rubric score.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Internal vulnerability research
description: Agents find a vulnerability from an entry point, with or without source, then write a working exploit. Based on Google red team exercises.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: InternBootcamp
description: Models solve generated reasoning tasks with task-specific answer checkers. The hub port lets users select a task and sample examples with a fixed seed.
note: On August 26, 2026, the authors reported a best Bootcamp-Eval average of 61.1 for Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct with Bootcamp-SFT. Qwen3-235B-A22B scored 54.5.

name: Into the Unknown
aliases: Into the Unknown (DOE open research benchmark)
description: Agents get a science paper and an unpublished follow-up direction from a DOE national lab scientist, then write the follow-up paper. Rubrics built from the scientist's conditions grade it, plus an integrity check.
org: Prometheus-Eval team with US DOE national laboratories (Seungone Kim et al.)
note: Nine agents wrote 15 follow-ups each. None of the 135 papers met all conditions, and 114 failed the integrity check. 152 HF paper upvotes.

name: IntPhys 2
description: Models watch simulated videos and judge whether each event is physically possible, testing object permanence, immutability, continuity and solidity. Scored by accuracy.
note: Released with V-JEPA 2. The leaderboard scores a held-out split of 344 videos whose answers stay private. The CAIS AI leaderboard also runs it on frontier models.

name: IntPhys2-Timing
description: Models identify when a physical rule breaks in a video. The authors add violation intervals to IntPhys2 and score temporal localization.

name: Introductory Sommelier (theory knowledge)
description: Models answer wine theory questions at the introductory sommelier level. Scoring is accuracy.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: Invented O'Clock
description: Models calculate dates and times in 45 scheduling problems. Paired versions remove an essential fact and require the model to answer unknown.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 8 distinct model versions.

name: Inverse IFEval
description: Models follow 1,012 Chinese and English instructions that conflict with habits learned in fine-tuning, such as writing code without comments. A model judge scores compliance.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Zhang et al.)
note: Eight challenge types across 23 domains. It is a different test from IFEval.

name: Inverse Scaling Prize Tasks
description: Models answer questions designed to reveal cases where larger models perform worse. The suite includes hindsight bias and following instructions that conflict with familiar text.

name: Investment Banking Modeling Tasks (OpenAI)
description: Models build first- to third-year investment banking analyst models, such as three-statement and leveraged buyout models, with formatting and citations. OpenAI grades the outputs internally.
note: OpenAI first reported it for ChatGPT agent on 2025-07-17, as first- to third-year analyst modeling tasks such as three-statement and leveraged buyout models. The GPT-5.2 post called it Investment banking spreadsheet tasks, with GPT-5.2 at 68.4 under both names. The grading method is not described, so model-judged is assumed.

name: Investor's Last Exam
description: Financial agents make equity investment judgments from a frozen set of decision-time evidence. Predictions are scored against later outcomes and professional criteria.
note: 128 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: Invoice Approval (Ali Siala)
description: Agents process 60 supplier invoice work orders under a German company’s approval policy. The evaluator compares the resulting database with a reference state.
note: The November 2026 results show GPT-5.6-sol passed 174 of 180 attempts across four tiers. GPT-4.1-mini passed 16 of 50 attempts across three tiers.

name: IOI (Vals)
description: Agents solve International Olympiad in Informatics problems from 2024 and 2025 in C++. A submission tool modeled on the contest grades up to 50 tries per problem by subtask.
note: Vals archived v1 as saturated after 2026-08-09, with Claude Opus 5 first at 91.67%. Not the same as the almanac's single-year IOI 2025 record.

name: IOI 2025
description: Model solves the 2025 International Olympiad in Informatics tasks. Scored with official subtask points (max 600).
note: Contest problems are public. No single public LLM harness found.

name: IOI v2 (Vals)
description: Agents solve 18 International Olympiad in Informatics problems from 2024, 2025 and 2026 in C++ inside OpenCode. Official tests and graders score the final solution by subtask after the run.
note: Unlike v1 there is no interactive grading tool, and Vals says the two harnesses are not comparable. Score is the mean of three yearly scores. Released between 2026-08-09 and 2026-10-29.

name: IOL-AI 2026
description: Models infer linguistic rules from Olympiad problems and answer individual questions. The official competition combines exact match and character-level similarity.
note: Team arvindcr4 led the corrected July 2026 standings at 19.79 out of 100 using a four-bit Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct model.

name: iOSWorld
description: Phone agents work in a native iOS simulator across 26 purpose-built apps that share one persistent user's data. Tasks span single apps, multi-app flows and memory or personalization from the user's history.
note: 133 tasks: 27 single-app, 60 multi-app and 46 memory and personalization. Vision-only and vision plus XML settings. Best setup reached 51.9% overall. Apple's iPrefBench builds on it.

name: IPhO 2025
description: Models solve the theory problems of the 2025 International Physics Olympiad. Answers are graded against the official marking scheme.
note: Labs grade it themselves, so scores across labs may use different graders. Seed reports it for Seed2.1 Pro and Deep Think.

name: IPI Bench
description: Agents complete workplace workflows while attackers add misleading records to an emulated company with 11 services. The benchmark pairs six workflow types with harmful injected objectives across 34 tasks. The headline here measures single-query attack success as a percentage, where lower is better.
note: Models run at medium reasoning effort without added defenses. Judges assess task-specific rubrics, and reviewers check every claimed attack success. The report separately gives independent and iterative attack budgets. Clean-workflow cost and total tokens describe runs without attacks. The report dates itself to October 2026.

name: Iris Safety Evaluations
description: Reflection AI's in-house safety suite of single-turn, multi-turn, jailbreak and agentic requests. Reports the share of harmful requests refused or redirected and the share of harmless requests answered.
note: In-house test. Prompts are not public.

name: IrokoBench
description: Models answer human-translated knowledge, math and inference questions in 16 African languages. The parts are AfriMMLU, AfriMGSM and AfriXNLI.
note: lm-evaluation-harness ships the three parts as afrimmlu, afrimgsm and afrixnli. Masakhane publishes each component separately. The dataset link opens AfriMMLU.

name: IronClad
description: Agents repair security misconfigurations in Terraform repositories. The grader verifies that the repaired configuration satisfies policy and preserves the intended infrastructure.
note: The August 2026 release reports Gemini 3.6 Flash solved nine of the original ten tasks. Gemini 3.5 Flash and 2.5 Flash failed one shared comparison task.

name: Irregular FrontierCyber and Atomic Challenges
description: Irregular's external suites: FrontierCyber (226 real software/hardware challenges) and Atomic Challenges (22 skill-level tasks).

name: Irrelevant instructions, text-based web browser
description: Agents using a text browser meet synthetic web pages with irrelevant instructions or data exfiltration attempts. Scored on ignoring them.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built from synthetic examples. The tasks are not public.

name: Irrelevant instructions, visual browser
description: Agents using a visual browser meet irrelevant instructions or data exfiltration attempts on web pages, based on red teaming scenarios. Scored on ignoring them.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public. The ChatGPT Agent card also gives Operator scores on it.

name: iSAID
description: Models detect and segment individual objects in aerial images. The benchmark measures how well predicted masks match annotated object instances.

name: iSarcasmEval
description: Models identify intended sarcasm in English and Arabic texts labeled by their authors. Other tracks classify ironic speech and distinguish sarcastic text from a literal paraphrase.
org: Ibrahim Abu Farha, Silviu Vlad Oprea, Steven Wilson, and Walid Magdy
note: Task A uses sarcastic-class F1, Task B uses macro-F1, and Task C uses accuracy. Decision Index reports its English Task A adaptation.

name: Italian-Administrative-CaseHold
description: Models classify Italian administrative judgments paired with their official holdings by legal subject.
note: MTEB scores the task using accuracy.

name: ITBench
description: Agents handle IT automation tasks in Kubernetes environments: site reliability incidents, compliance and security checks, and cloud cost work.
note: Presented as an oral at ICML 2025. IBM and Kaggle added an ITBench leaderboard in 2025-12.

name: ITBench-AA
description: Agents read an offline snapshot of a failing Kubernetes cluster and name the entities that caused the incident, in structured JSON.
note: Launched 2026-05-27 with 59 SRE scenarios from ITBench, 40 of them public. FinOps and CISO tasks are planned. An LLM normalizes entities before matching.

name: ITSMBench
description: Agents operate an IT service desk across 53 conversations with simulated colleagues. The verifier grades the resulting database state, including permissions and required actions.
note: The 15-task comparison available November 19, 2026 reports Claude Opus 4.8 alone. Resuming unfinished conversations raised its score from 0.00 to 0.33.

name: Ivo-micro1 ContractBench
description: Models review contracts and return redlines across 350 attorney-written tasks in 35 scenarios and five agreement types. Tasks cover first review and replies to a counterparty.
note: Scores whether models intervene where several attorneys did, plus a surgicality index of targeted inline edits. Attorneys scored 63.5% on surgicality.

name: IWSLT 2017 TED Translation
description: Models translate TED talk transcripts between languages. The campaign includes bilingual translation and multilingual translation with unseen language pairs.

name: Jailbreak Augmented Examples
description: Models face publicly known jailbreaks applied to prompts from the standard disallowed content set. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built from public jailbreak techniques.

name: JailbreakBench
description: 100 harmful and 100 benign behaviors with a standard jailbreak artifact library. Scored by attack success rate.

name: JailTrickBench
aliases: Bag of Tricks: Benchmarking of Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs
description: Models respond to jailbreak attacks under varied attack and defense settings. A GPT-4 evaluator judges attack success across harmful-request datasets.
org: HKUST (Guangzhou), Guangzhou HKUST Fok Ying Tung Research Institute and HKUST
note: The framework varies eight experimental factors and compares multiple attacks and defenses. Scores depend on the attack, defense, and target settings.

name: JamC-QA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about Japan, including regional identity, customs, geography, and law.
note: The llm-jp-eval harness runs this evaluation with Japanese prompts.

name: Jamp
description: Models infer temporal relationships between Japanese sentences. Separate test splits vary the templates, time formats, and time spans.
note: The llm-jp-eval harness runs this evaluation with Japanese prompts.

name: JaNLI
description: Models judge entailment between Japanese sentences designed to expose shortcuts in language inference.
note: The llm-jp-eval harness runs this evaluation with Japanese prompts.

name: Japanese LLM Leaderboard (lm-evaluation-harness)
description: Models complete eight Japanese tasks covering reading, reasoning, math, and summarization. The harness groups the individual results.
note: The task group includes JAQKET v2, JGLUE tasks, Japanese MGSM, Japanese XL-Sum, and Japanese XWinograd.

name: Japanese-English Bilingual Corpus of Wikipedia’s Kyoto Articles
description: Models translate between Japanese and English using parallel Wikipedia passages about Kyoto.
note: The llm-jp-eval harness runs this evaluation with Japanese prompts.

name: JAQKET
description: Models answer Japanese quiz questions.
note: The llm-jp-eval harness includes the AIO quiz task.

name: JBLiMP
aliases: Japanese Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs
description: Models compare 331 pairs of Japanese sentences that differ in grammatical acceptability.
note: The llm-jp-eval harness runs this evaluation with Japanese prompts.

name: JCoLA
description: Models decide whether Japanese sentences are grammatically acceptable. Linguists supply judgments for sentences from textbooks and the research literature.
note: The authors report separate results for in-domain and out-of-domain sentences.

name: JEF-Bench
description: Agents read files that embed jailbreak instructions in tool-call returns. Reports attack success rate across 1800 tasks and 50 disallowed use cases.
note: In-house Meta evaluation introduced in the Muse Spark 1.3 report.

name: JEMHopQA
description: Models answer Japanese questions that require combining facts across multiple documents and provide the supporting reasoning.
note: Version 1.2 fixes questions, answers, and supporting triples.

name: Jester gesture recognition
description: Models classify hand gestures in short videos. The task distinguishes movements with similar appearance but different directions or timing.

name: JETHICS
description: Models judge ethical scenarios in Japanese. The suite includes the Japanese commonsense morality dataset used by llm-jp-eval.
note: The authors provide evaluation samples and a separate download of the full dataset.

name: JevBench
description: Decision models, such as TypeSafe AI's Jev and compatible systems, answer typed decision questions. The board scores accuracy, probability calibration, latency and cost.
note: Maintained independently of TypeSafe AI. Show HN post had 154 points. Related to the Decision Index board.

name: JFBench
description: Models answer Japanese prompts with multiple verifiable constraints. A response passes only if it satisfies every constraint.
note: The verified evaluation reports pass rates by the number of constraints per prompt.

name: JFinBench
description: Models answer questions from six Japanese certification exams in accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking. The authors report scores by exam.

name: JFinQA
description: Models calculate financial ratios, check consistency, and reason about changes over time using Japanese securities reports.
note: The benchmark contains 1,000 questions across three tasks.

name: JGLUE
description: Models classify Japanese sentences, compare sentence meanings, and answer reading comprehension and commonsense questions. The authors publish baseline scores for each task.
org: Yahoo Japan Corporation and Waseda University
note: Tasks include MARC-ja, JCoLA, JSTS, JNLI, JSQuAD, and JCommonsenseQA. The maintainers stopped distributing MARC-ja after Amazon withdrew its source corpus.

name: JGPQA
description: Models answer graduate-level science questions translated into Japanese from GPQA.
note: The llm-jp-eval harness runs this evaluation with Japanese prompts.

name: JHumanEval
description: Models implement Python functions from Japanese prompts. Programmers reviewed machine translations of the HumanEval specifications.
note: The llm-jp-eval harness runs this evaluation with Japanese prompts.

name: Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification
description: Models label Wikipedia talk page comments for toxicity types such as threats, insults and identity hate. Labs report F1 or ROC AUC.
org: Jigsaw and Google (Conversation AI), hosted on Kaggle
note: The data comes from a 2017 Kaggle competition. Amazon uses it as a content moderation test for Nova 2 with F1.

name: JMMLU
description: Models answer 7,536 four-way multiple-choice questions in Japanese, from translated MMLU subjects and new Japan-specific subjects. Scored by accuracy.

name: JMultiWOZ-TC
description: Models use Japanese dialogue history and past tool results to predict which tools to call next.
note: The harness checks the predicted set of tool calls against the annotated set.

name: JobBench
description: 130 tasks from 35 occupations workers most want delegated. Agent works through messy reference files, graded by fact-anchored binary rubrics.
note: Framed as an alternative to GDPval's economic-value framing. Vendor-reported scores run higher than the paper's best (45.9%).

name: Joi-Bench-Task
description: Voice agents use tools while a simulated caller changes a request or interrupts a reply. The evaluator tracks completion, responsiveness, and omitted information.

name: JointAVBench
