description: Models receive 600 private offensive cyber prompts, directly and under jailbreak attacks. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Meta refusal set from the Muse Spark Safety and Preparedness Report.

name: Meta holistic adversarial audit with Petri Bloom
aliases: Broad Adversarial Auditing with Petri Bloom
description: Two auditor models run Petri Bloom scenarios built from Meta's behavior taxonomy. A binary judge reports the share of scenarios with a violation.
note: Meta setup over nine taxonomy sub-categories. Each scenario takes its worst of six transcripts.

name: Meta instructed selective performance evaluation
description: Models are told to underperform on six science capability sets. Reports the average drop from baseline in percentage points.
note: In-house Meta sandbagging experiment with monitor-oblivious and monitor-aware conditions.

name: Meta internal agent hallucination evaluation
description: Agents do long-context assistant and professional tasks with tools. The benchmark reports the share of verifiable claims that are hallucinated.
note: In-house Meta benchmark across health, finance, legal, clinical and engineering tasks.

name: Meta internal sycophancy evaluation
description: Models meet adversarially curated conversations that invite inappropriate agreement, plus benign controls. Reports sycophancy and excessive anti-sycophancy rates.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. Rates are high by construction and do not estimate ordinary use.

name: Meta prompted evaluation awareness
description: Models are asked to judge whether transcripts come from evaluations or real use. Reports the weighted rate of correct identification.
note: In-house Meta evaluation over chemical and biological, cyber and loss of control transcripts.

name: Meta targeted agentic evaluations
description: Agents work in prebuilt stateful sandboxes that test specific behavior rules. Reports the case-level violation rate over 1,790 scenarios.
note: In-house Meta suite built from 142 taxonomy units. Scenarios were screened with Muse Spark 1.1.

name: Meta training-stage provenance probe
description: Models label 10,000 transcripts as deployment, evaluation, RL or SFT. Reports overall accuracy against a 25% chance rate.
note: In-house Meta situational awareness probe on internal transcripts.

name: Meta Underspecified Intent evaluation
description: Models answer ambiguous requests sourced from real Meta AI chats where users corrected the reply. Rubrics score whether the true intent is met.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. A companion Underlying Intent set is reported separately.

name: Meta-World
description: Robot policies do simulated tabletop manipulation tasks, scored by success rate. Splits test multi-task learning, such as MT10 and MT50, and meta-learning, such as ML45.
org: Farama Foundation (originally Stanford, Berkeley and others)
note: About 1,900 GitHub stars and still maintained. Meta-World+ (2025-05, arXiv 2505.11289) standardized the benchmark, so check which version a paper reports. VLA papers in 2026 report it.

name: metabench
description: Models answer selected items from established evaluations. The benchmark uses a sparse item set to estimate reasoning and knowledge with fewer questions.

name: MetagenomicsBench
description: Agents analyze microbial communities from shotgun, amplicon, long-read and spatial metagenomics data. A grader checks the biological result.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 100 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: metal-arm-harness
description: Safety-enveloped CLI that lets any coding agent drive a real MakerMods Metal or Maker arm one command at a time from camera JPEGs.
note: Harness, not a benchmark. The safety design is a measured table floor, slow zone and per-move joint caps. No license file.

name: METR data deduplication
description: Agents write an efficient algorithm that removes near-duplicate lines from a large file. A trial succeeds when F1 reaches at least 80%.
note: Anthropic reports the share of trials scoring above the F1 threshold. The card calls it a METR public task.

name: METR general autonomy task suite
aliases: Agent Performance on General Autonomy Benchmark
description: Agents complete multi-step tasks in virtual environments. Scored as horizon weighted average task completion compared with human time limits.
note: Precursor of the METR time horizon suite. OpenAI cards show it as a chart.

name: METR pre-deployment AI R&D tasks
description: METR's long-horizon tasks for Anthropic pre-deployment tests: Train a Program, Gaming Bot, Sunlight open-ended research, plus Budget NanoGPT and LMCA.

name: METR Time Horizon
description: Agents attempt software and research tasks timed against skilled humans. The score is the human task length at which the agent succeeds half the time.
note: Time Horizon 1.0 used 170 tasks in Vivaria. METR replaced it with Time Horizon 1.1 in January 2026 and re-estimated 14 models.

name: METR Time Horizon 1.1
description: Agents attempt 228 software and research tasks timed against skilled humans, run in Inspect. The score is the human task length at which the agent succeeds half the time.
note: It added 73 HCAST tasks, removed 15 and updated 53, and moved from Vivaria to Inspect. METR stopped updating the page on 2026-09-08 and calls results above 16 hours unreliable.

name: METR Time Horizon suite
description: Software tasks with human completion times. Reports the task length at which a model succeeds 50% of the time.
note: METR flagged high detected cheating for GPT-5.6 Sol, so it treated the result as non-robust.

name: MeViS
description: Models segment the objects in a video that a sentence picks out by their motion, not by static looks. Scored by J&F.
org: Nanyang Technological University and Fudan University (Ding, Liu, He, Jiang, Loy)
note: ICCV 2023. Reports use the valid_u split, whose labels are public. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports MeViS-ValidU.

name: MEWC
description: Models solve 179 Microsoft Excel World Championship problems from 2021 to 2026 with Excel tools. Output cells are compared one by one with answer cells.
note: In-house MiniMax benchmark built from Excel esports problems, and the task set is not released.

name: MEWC v2
description: Models solve 100 hard Microsoft Excel World Championship problems with Excel tools. Expert rubrics score the answers over three trials.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation. It is a hard subset of the MEWC pool, so scores differ from the 179-problem MEWC.

name: mFollowIR
description: Models rank documents according to a search instruction across multiple languages.
note: The benchmark tests whether a change in instructions changes which documents rank highly.

name: MGSM
description: 250 GSM8K problems translated into 10 languages. Final-answer accuracy.
note: Saturated.

name: MGSM-Rev2
description: Models solve the 250 MGSM grade-school math problems in 10 languages. Google fixed two English errors, rephrased ambiguous items and retranslated every question with Gemini. Accuracy.
note: Same format as MGSM and meant as a drop-in replacement. The paper shows translation errors skewed earlier MGSM results, so scores differ. Cohere's GlobalMGSM uses it.

name: MHPP
description: Models write Python functions for 210 human-curated problems that need careful reading of specifications and multi-step reasoning. Unit tests check each solution.
note: Built to be harder than HumanEval and MBPP. The paper evaluated 26 models.

name: MIA-Bench
description: Models answer 400 image prompts that stack several strict instructions on format, length and content. An LLM judge scores how well each answer follows every instruction.
note: ICLR 2025 paper. Reported in Qwen-VL reports under alignment.

name: micro1 Medical Index
description: Models are scored on the equal-weight average of micro1 medical benchmarks, currently RealmPathology, PharmaBench and WellnessBench.
note: A live scoreboard that adds each new micro1 medical benchmark.

name: Microsoft internal multimodal RAI benchmark
description: Vision language models answer image and text prompts across harm categories. Responses are scored from 0 to 10, higher is safer.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation reported for Phi-3.5-Vision.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Grounding
description: Models answer in GPT-4o simulated multi-turn conversations. A judge scores from 0 to 5 how fully each answer is grounded in the given prompt.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation from the Phi-4 report. The Phi-3 report scores Ungroundedness from 0 to 4 instead.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Harmful Content Continuation (DR-3)
description: Models continue conversations about hate, self-harm, sexual content and violence. Scored as the share of answers with judged severity 3 or more out of 7.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Harmful Content Summarization (DR-3)
description: Models summarize content about hate, self-harm, sexual content and violence. Scored as the share of answers with judged severity 3 or more out of 7.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Jailbreak (DR-1)
description: Models face simulated jailbreak conversations on topics such as child grooming, illegal advice and leaking guidelines. Scored as the defect rate at severity 1.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Third Party Harm (DR-1)
description: Models face simulated conversations that try to extract third-party content such as books, news, recipes and songs. Scored as the defect rate at severity 1.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Ungroundedness
description: Models answer in GPT-4 simulated multi-turn conversations. A judge rates how ungrounded each answer is in the given prompt, from 0 to 4.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation from the Phi-3 report. The Phi-4 report uses a Grounding score from 0 to 5 instead.

name: MicroVQA
description: Models answer expert-written multiple choice questions about biology microscopy images that test image understanding, hypothesis generation and experiment proposal.
org: Stanford University (James Burgess, Serena Yeung-Levy et al.)
note: MicroVQA++ (2025-11) is a separate training dataset.

name: MIEB
description: Image and image-text embedding models are scored on 130 tasks in 38 languages, grouped into 8 task types such as retrieval, clustering and classification.
note: Part of the MTEB framework. Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 card reports the MIEB lite subset as Mean(TaskType). 50 models in the paper.

name: MIEB Lite
description: Embedding models complete the MIEB Lite task set. The official API reports the mean across task types.
note: This task set has a separate official score endpoint. Task-type scores remain auxiliary metrics.

name: MiJaBench
description: Models respond to 43,961 English and Portuguese prompts across 16 minority groups. Judges measure how defense rates change with the target group and language.
note: The 2026 paper compares 14 models and identifies Gemini 2.0 Flash as its most robust baseline. Its English defense rate was 58%.

name: Miklós Schweitzer 2025
description: Models write proofs for the 2025 Miklós Schweitzer competition, a hard Hungarian university-level contest. MathArena runs and grades it.
note: Listed among MathArena competitions. Dataset created 2025-12-10.

name: MILU
description: Multi-task Indic Language Understanding: culturally grounded multiple-choice questions in 11 Indic languages.

name: MIMIC-CXR (classification)
description: Models read chest X-rays from Beth Israel Deaconess and say whether five common conditions are present. Scored by average F1 over the conditions.
org: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Johnson et al.)
note: Access needs PhysioNet credentials. Google reports two test sets, Med-Gemini radiologist-adjudicated labels and the MAIRA test set, and their scores differ a lot.

name: MIMIC-CXR report generation
description: Models write the findings of a radiology report for a MIMIC-CXR chest X-ray. Scored against the radiologist's report, most often by RadGraph F1.
org: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Johnson et al.)
note: Google reports RadGraph F1 on a 912-image test set from Tanno et al. (2024). Other reports use other splits and metrics, so check the split before comparing.

name: MIMIC-III Report Summarization
description: Models generate the impression section of a clinical report from the preceding text. The harness compares the response with the recorded impression.
note: The date comes from the first commit for this evaluation in the harness.

name: MIMIC-IV-BHC
description: Models summarize a patient’s hospital course from clinical notes. The reference is the brief hospital course section of the discharge summary.

name: MiMo Code Bench
description: Coding agents work through a varied set of software tasks built in house by Xiaomi. The report gives no task count or grading details.
note: Xiaomi also reports a mini version with avg@3 during training.

name: MiMo Coding Bench
description: Models do varied coding tasks inside agent harnesses such as Claude Code. Tasks cover repo understanding, project building, code review, artifact generation, planning and SWE.
note: Xiaomi built it in house. The MiMo-V2.6 report uses a MiMo Code Bench that gives MiMo-V2.5-Pro 40.4 against 73.7 here, so the two sets differ.

name: MiMo Cyber Bench
description: Agents do in-house cybersecurity tasks that add to public vulnerability reproduction and exploitation benchmarks. The report gives no task count or grading details.
note: MiMo-V2.5-Pro scores 0.0 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro scores 80.2 in the report table.

name: MiMo Visual Coding
description: Models build websites from requests and turn reference images into matching front-end code. Tasks include WebDev and Image2Code.
note: Xiaomi built it in house. The report does not name the grader, so the scoring type is a guess.

name: Mind the Gap
description: Models describe visible events during natural pauses in a video's soundtrack. The evaluator renders the narration and checks its timing and coverage.

name: Mind2Web
description: Models predict the next web action for over 2,000 crowdsourced tasks on 137 real websites in 31 domains. Scored by element accuracy and step success rate.
note: Offline action prediction over cached pages. Splits are cross-task, cross-website and cross-domain.

name: Mind2Web 2
description: Agents browse the live web for 130 long tasks and return answers with citations. Task-specific judge agents built from rubric trees grade correctness and attribution.
note: Built with over 1,000 hours of human labor. It tests agentic search, not single web actions, so scores do not compare with Mind2Web.

name: Mind2Web-SC
description: Models generate guardrails that check a web agent’s proposed actions against user constraints. The benchmark measures whether the guardrail permits or blocks each action correctly.

name: MindCube
description: Models answer 21,154 multiple choice questions about scenes seen from a few views. Questions test positions, orientations, and what-if movements.
org: MLL Lab, Northwestern University, with Stanford, NYU, and University of Washington
note: The authors fixed data bugs in March 2026, so newer results may differ from earlier ones.

name: MindEval
description: Models hold multi-turn therapy conversations with simulated patients designed with licensed clinical psychologists. An LLM judge scores each session.
note: The paper validates simulated patients against human text and judges against experts, then tests 12 models. The Sword page refused scripted reads.

name: MindEval2
description: Models support simulated patients from MindSim, a tool-using harness with detailed profiles. Psychologist-written rubrics (MHQR) replace Likert scales for scoring.
note: New patient simulator and new rubrics, so scores do not compare with MindEval. Maker attribution follows the first version.

name: MindGames
description: Agents compete in Colonel Blotto, Iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma, Codenames, and Secret Mafia.
note: The 2026 paper reports 944 submitted agents from 76 teams across four games. The checked page does not state the best score.

name: MInDS-14
description: Models identify the banking service a caller wants from a spoken request.
note: The dataset covers 14 language varieties.

name: MindWorldBench
description: Models animate a scene to show how a person would act given their beliefs or intentions. Paired prompts change mental states while holding the scene fixed.

name: MineAmongUs
description: Vision-language agents play an embodied Among Us game with verbal and nonverbal deception.
note: The August 2026 paper compares multiple VLM agents. The abstract does not state the best score.

name: MineBench
description: Models turn a prompt into a Minecraft-style voxel build as raw 3D coordinates or tool calls. Users compare builds blind, and votes become rankings.
note: The maker says it is an arena of vibes with no correct answers. Kaggle also hosts a MineBench Arena board. About 340 GitHub stars.

name: MineDojo
description: Agents complete open-ended tasks in Minecraft, such as mining blocks and fighting mobs, from a large simulation suite. Programmatic checks score many tasks.
org: NVIDIA, Caltech and collaborators (Fan et al.)
note: NeurIPS 2022 Outstanding Paper. Seed2.0 reports Minedojo-Verified, a verified subset whose maker it does not state.

name: MINERVA
description: Models answer complex video questions that need multi-step reasoning, with reference reasoning traces for grading.
note: Gemini 2.5 report uses the test subset, 0-shot, 1,024 frames.

name: MINERVA-Cultural
description: Models answer about 2,200 open-ended questions on 540 videos from 18 locales, written in native languages by local experts. An LLM judge scores each answer 0, 1 or 2.
note: Part of the MINERVA dataset collection with MINERVA and Neptune. Gemini 2.5 Pro scores 45.07% against a human baseline of 95.22%. The repo cites it under its first name, CURVE.

name: Minerva-Ego
description: Models answer 1,160 multiple-choice questions on egocentric kitchen videos from HD-EPIC. Each question has a hand-written reasoning trace grounded in time and objects.
note: Extends MINERVA to egocentric video. CVPR 2026 paper. Gemini 2.5 Pro scores 40.1% with 64 frames against a human 91.8%.

name: miniCTX-v2
description: Provers prove Lean theorems from real projects using long repository context, with theorems taken after a November 28, 2024 cutoff.
note: An update of miniCTX (2024) with new theorems, so scores are not comparable with v1. The month is the creation date of the Hugging Face dataset.

name: miniF2F
description: Models write formal proofs of olympiad and high school competition statements, such as AMC, AIME and IMO problems. A proof assistant checks each proof, and scores are pass@k on the 244 test problems.
org: OpenAI (Kunhao Zheng, Jesse Michael Han, Stanislas Polu)
note: Statements exist in Lean, Metamath, Isabelle and HOL Light. Labs report pass@1, pass@8 or pass@32.

name: Minimal-LinuxBench (Anthropic)
description: Agents attempt a hidden side task in high-stakes software environments while a monitor watches. Score is the stealth success rate.
note: Anthropic adaptation of a subset of LinuxBench, an AI control arena that Redwood Research shared privately.

name: MiniMax TTS Multilingual Test Set
description: Text-to-speech models clone two Common Voice speakers per language and read 100 test sentences in each of 24 languages. Scored by word error rate and speaker similarity.
note: Released with MiniMax-Speech. MiniMax plans to add languages, so the set may grow. Lower error rate is better.

name: MiniWoB++
description: Agents operate over 100 small synthetic web pages, such as forms, menus and date pickers, from a natural-language instruction. Each task returns a success reward.
org: Stanford University, now maintained by the Farama Foundation
note: Extends OpenAI's 2017 MiniWoB. The Farama version exposes a Gymnasium API.

name: MINTEval
description: Memory-augmented agents answer questions after long, frequently updated histories where memories interfere. Instances average 138,800 tokens and reach 1.8 million.
note: Across 7 memory systems the average accuracy was 27.9% at launch.

name: MIR-1K
description: Models transcribe lyrics from the vocal tracks of karaoke recordings. Qwen compares recognition systems using transcription error.
org: Chao-Ling Hsu and Jyh-Shing Roger Jang

name: MIRA Bench
aliases: Multi-Agent Infra for Routing and Assignment Bench
description: Agents carry out long multi-role enterprise tasks across several systems and decide when to delegate to subagents.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: MirageBench
description: Models personalize six kinds of responses from three disclosed facts about each of 150 personas. A model judge classifies claims by evidential support. The primary over-inference rate counts stereotyped and fabricated claims.
org: Tencent LIGHTSPEED and Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
note: The paper supplies prompts and persona examples, but a full dataset release was not verified. One judge labels claims. Human validation covers 400 claims.

name: MIRB
description: Models compare, analyze and reason across several images in four categories: perception, visual world knowledge, reasoning and multi-hop reasoning.
org: University of Edinburgh and Tongji University
note: Shanghai AI Lab reports the category average in the InternVL3 and InternVL3.5 reports.

name: MirrorCode
description: Agent rebuilds a whole CLI program from scratch using only the original binary as an oracle. Solved only if 100% of end-to-end tests pass.
note: 25 targets, 3 kept private. ~34% of tests held out. Source programs are open source, so memorization cannot be fully ruled out.

name: MirrorDojo
description: Indirect prompt injection test run in Reflection AI's Mirror agent harness, based on AgentDojo. Each episode pairs a user task with an instruction planted in a tool result. Reports attack success rate and utility.
note: Not comparable to public AgentDojo results, because Mirror runs the agent loop instead of the benchmark's reference agent.

name: MirrorDyn
description: Indirect prompt injection test run in Reflection AI's Mirror agent harness, based on AgentDyn. Reports attack success rate and utility.
note: Not comparable to public AgentDyn results, because Mirror runs the agent loop.

name: Misaligned Behavior in Realistic Work Environments
aliases: Misaligned outcomes in realistic work environments
description: Agents do computer and browser tasks in simulated workplace apps with ambiguous instructions. Scored on the rate of unintended outcomes such as data disclosure.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. OpenAI made the set harder after the GPT-6 Astra card.

name: Misbehavior (Thinking Machines)
description: Agentic tasks that check whether a model fabricates results, ignores instructions or hides what it did when a task is hard. Scored by the rate of misbehavior.
note: In-house test. Tasks are not public.

name: Misc CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents identify and exploit vulnerabilities in capture-the-flag challenges outside the web, crypto, pwn, rev and network categories.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: MisconceptDialogue
description: Tutors identify a simulated student's mathematical misconception and address it through dialogue. The authors compare exact-match and human-calibrated model grading on the same conversations.
org: Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute and collaborators

name: Misguided Attention
description: Models get slight variations of famous riddles, paradoxes and thought experiments. A model fails when it answers the well-known original instead of the problem as stated.
note: Version 0.3 (2025-01) added an evaluation subset with tagged releases. About 490 GitHub stars.

name: MISHAP-Bench
description: Models answer open-ended questions about audio clips. A model judge uses human annotations to identify claims the recording does not support.

name: Missing-context hallucinations (Anthropic)
description: Models get prompts that request tools they lack or cite missing material. Score is the non-hallucination rate on each 500-prompt set.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation with unavailable-tool and missing-reference sets. The tool set was filtered on Claude Opus 4.6 failures.

name: MissionReport
description: Models write government status reports in Word from working files and a template, across 20 expert-written Department of Defense style assignments. Expert rubrics score each decision.
note: Nine models ran each task three times for 540 graded reports. Judgment and synthesis caused most lost points.

name: Mistral 175 unsafe prompts
description: Models receive 175 unsafe prompts. Metric is the share of harmful questions the model declines.
note: In-house Mistral test set used for system prompt guardrails. The prompts are not public.

name: Mistral internal function calling benchmark
description: Models call functions on Mistral's in-house test set. The Magistral paper does not describe the tasks or the metric.
note: In-house Mistral evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Mistral self-reflection moderation set
description: Models classify prompts or answers as acceptable or harmful on a balanced set of adversarial and standard prompts. Scored by precision and recall.
note: In-house Mistral dataset, manually curated. The prompts are not public.

name: Mitosis Bench
description: Agents mark every dividing cell in a tumor image. Each mark must fall within 30 pixels of an expert label. The grader rejects extra or missing marks.
note: On October 18, 2026, Gemini 4 Argon led with 32.4% pass@1 on 100 tasks. Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, GLM 5.3 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash also ran.

name: Mixer 6 Speech
description: Models transcribe conversations recorded across microphones and assign words to speakers. NVIDIA evaluates channel four recordings.
note: The Linguistic Data Consortium distributes the underlying recordings under license.

name: MixEval
description: Models answer real user queries matched to similar questions from existing benchmarks. Ground-truth answers make it a cheap proxy for Chatbot Arena rankings.
org: National University of Singapore (Ni et al.)
note: MixEval-Hard is a harder subset reported separately.

name: MJ-Bench
description: Models compare image pairs for text alignment, safety, visual quality, and bias. Scores measure preference accuracy, with separate dispersion and equality measures for bias.
org: MJ-Bench team at UNC-Chapel Hill, University of Chicago, Stanford University, and collaborators
note: Accuracy is reported with and without ties. Dataset access requires a request that the makers describe as automatically approved.

name: MKA
description: Agents complete professional tasks whose work is visual, 200 tasks across 10 fields and 83 occupations, each about three to eight hours of expert work. An agentic grader checks each deliverable against an expert rubric of about 70 yes or no checks, weighted 75% on factual accuracy and 25% on visual design.
note: Artificial Analysis runs the 200-task set and keeps it private. Ten sample tasks are public on Hugging Face. Every model runs in the same agent harness, Stirrup. The grader is built on a model from outside Google, and experts agreed with it 96% of the time. Labs report Climb WSR, the weighted share of the harder rubric checks a model meets. We don't import Artificial Analysis's leaderboard, so scores here come from lab posts.

name: MKQA
description: Models answer 10,000 open-domain questions translated into 26 languages. Exact match and token F1 measure agreement with human answers, including unanswerable questions.
note: Questions originate in Natural Questions, but the makers collected passage-independent answers. Each language can have several accepted answer forms.

name: ML-Dev-Bench
description: Agents implement and train models, debug failures, and improve performance. Harbor ports 33 development tasks and checks them with the original validators.
note: The original study tested Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Gemini 2.0 Flash. The Harbor comparison available November 19, 2026 reports 61.62% for GPT-5 mini.

name: MLAgentBench
description: Agents run machine learning experiments on 13 tasks, from improving CIFAR-10 accuracy to research problems like BabyLM. They read and write files, run code and inspect outputs.
note: An early AI R&D agent benchmark from 2023. About 360 GitHub stars and 75 forks.

name: MLCommons AILuminate
description: Industry-standard hazard benchmark over 12 risk categories with graded ratings.

name: MLCommons AILuminate Jailbreak
description: Models answer hazard prompts with and without taxonomy-based jailbreak attacks. The Resilience Gap is the drop in safety score under attack.
note: White papers for v0.5.1 (2025-12) and v0.7.1 (2026-02) came first. v1.0 used 264 seed prompts in 11 hazard categories on eight open-weight systems. The page cites 39 models tested.

name: MLCR-AA
description: Models reason over synthetic medical claim files of about 25k to 64k tokens, as a claims reviewer would. Three judge models check completeness and accuracy.
note: Wisedocs released MLCR on 2026-06-18 and v1.1 with the Artificial Analysis board on 2026-08-31. The board uses 60 private questions from the two hardest tiers.

name: MLE-bench
description: Kaggle-style ML engineering competitions. Agent trains models and is scored against competition leaderboards.
note: OpenAI runs an internal Revised version with 72 problems. The public leaderboard in the repo README stopped taking submissions on 2026-04-24. MLE-bench Lite is the 22-competition Low split.

name: MLE-bench 30
description: Agents train models for 30 of MLE-bench's Kaggle-style competitions. The score is the share of runs that earn a bronze medal or better.
note: OpenAI's system cards report this subset, and Meta reports a 30-task subset in its preparedness reports. It has no public leaderboard.

name: MLGym-Bench
description: Agents work on 13 open-ended AI research tasks in vision, language, reinforcement learning and game theory. Scores compare the agent's result with baselines on each task's metric.
note: Part of Meta's MLGym framework, which is also a Gym environment for RL training.

name: MLogiQA
description: Models answer LogiQA logical reasoning questions translated into 10 languages, 80 per language. Scored by accuracy.
note: It is a subset of the P-MMEval multilingual suite.

name: MLQA
description: Models extract answers from Wikipedia passages in seven languages, with questions and contexts that can be in different languages. Scored by F1 and exact match.
note: Languages are English, Arabic, German, Spanish, Hindi, Vietnamese and Chinese.

name: MLRC-Bench
description: Agents propose and implement methods for machine learning competitions. The scorer compares their performance with a supplied baseline and the strongest human solution.

name: MLS-Bench
description: Agent must invent one algorithmic change in an ML research scaffold whose gain transfers across settings. Scored relative to human baselines.
note: 140 tasks over 12 ML domains. Lite = 30-task subset (~99 H100-hours) with 5-hour limit per task. Score >50 beats strongest human baseline.

name: MLVU
description: Multi-task long video understanding (minutes to hours) with multiple-choice and generation tasks. Accuracy.
note: The dev set and the test set use different questions and option counts, so their scores are not comparable. The test answers became public on 2025-03-18.

name: MM-AlignBench
description: Models answer open-ended questions about 252 human-annotated images. GPT-4o compares their answers with Claude-Sonnet-3 reference answers to assess alignment with human preferences.
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai AI Laboratory, Nanjing University and others
note: The evaluation set is separate from the OmniAlign-V training datasets. The star count belongs to the combined project.

name: MM-BrowseComp
description: Browsing agents answer 400 hand-written questions whose evidence sits in web images and videos. Each question has a checklist for analysis of the reasoning path.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Li et al.)
note: Accepted to EMNLP 2026. The paper evaluates 27 models.

name: MM-ClawBench
description: Agents complete common OpenClaw tasks such as study planning, office documents, scheduled research, and code maintenance. Scoring is accuracy.
note: In-house: MiniMax never released the tasks or explained the scoring.

name: MM-FinEval
description: Models forecast financial outcomes from earnings call transcripts, slides, and audio. The authors compare 19 models using directional accuracy and absolute error.

name: MM-HELIX
description: Multimodal models solve 1,260 items from 42 synthetic tasks that need long reflective reasoning with backtracking.
note: 110 upvotes on Hugging Face papers. Released with a training method.

name: MM-IFEval
description: Multimodal models follow image-grounded instructions with exact output constraints. Checks mix rule-based verification and a judge model.
note: Released with the MM-IFEngine training pipeline. 35 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: MM-MT-Bench
description: Models hold multi-turn conversations about images such as charts, documents and photos. GPT-4o grades each answer against a reference on a 1 to 10 scale.
note: Released with Pixtral 12B. Mistral and Qwen VL reports both use it.

name: MM-NIAH
description: Vision-language models answer questions about long documents of interleaved images and text. Tasks are retrieval, counting and reasoning over needles hidden in the document.
note: Models did worst on image needles at release. VLMEvalKit supports the validation split.

name: MM-OCEAN
description: Models rate apparent personality traits in short videos, explain those ratings, and answer questions about observable cues. Evaluation reports rating accuracy, absolute error, cue-question accuracy, and model-judged explanation scores.
org: University of Tokyo, Shanda AI Research Tokyo, and Dalian University of Technology
note: The benchmark contains 1,104 videos and 5,320 cue-grounding questions. Targets are crowd-sourced apparent-personality ratings, not clinical diagnoses or verified personality traits. The metrics separately test agreement with ratings and grounding in video evidence.

name: MM-SafetyBench
description: Multimodal models get 5,040 harmful text and image pairs in 13 scenarios, where a query-relevant image carries the harmful intent. Judges score attack success.
org: East China Normal University and Shanghai AI Laboratory
note: 222 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: MM-Vet
description: Models answer open questions about images that combine recognition, OCR, knowledge, spatial reasoning, language generation and math. GPT-4 grades each answer against a reference.
org: Weihao Yu, Zhengyuan Yang et al. (NUS and Microsoft)
note: MM-Vet v2 is a later release with interleaved image and text inputs.

name: MMAE
description: Audio models edit audio from instructions across a broad range of real-world editing tasks and sound types.
note: It had 45 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 113 GitHub stars. Tasks are audio editing, which the taxonomy files under audio understanding.

name: MMAR
description: Models answer 1,000 questions about real-world audio of speech, sound, music and their mixes. Questions span four reasoning layers from signal to cultural knowledge.
note: Repo has over 200 GitHub stars.

name: mMARCO
description: Models rank passages by relevance to a query. The multilingual benchmark translates the MS MARCO passage ranking collection.

name: MMAU
description: 10K audio clips with questions on speech, sound and music needing expert knowledge and reasoning. Multiple-choice accuracy.

name: MMAU v05.15.25
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about speech, sound and music clips that need expert knowledge and reasoning. Scored by accuracy on test-mini or the hidden-answer test set.
note: Revises about 25% of questions and answers and 5% of audio files. The makers ask to cite this version from now on and keep earlier scores on a separate board. Test scoring moved to an HF space on 2026-01-30.

name: MMAU-Pro
description: Models answer 5,305 expert-written questions about speech, sounds, music and their mixes, covering 49 listening skills. Some clips run up to 10 minutes.
org: University of Maryland (GAMMA lab) and collaborators
note: A harder follow-up to MMAU from the same group. Some questions are open-ended rather than multiple choice.

name: MMBench
description: Vision language models answer multiple-choice questions covering 20 perception and reasoning skills. CircularEval rotates the options. Scored by accuracy.
note: The original version. MMBench v1.1 is a separate entry.

name: MMBench-CN v1.1
description: Models answer the Chinese translation of the MMBench image questions, using CircularEval with shuffled options. Scored by accuracy.
note: OpenCompass released the verified Chinese version on 2023-10-03. The v1.1 cleanup date is not stated on the repo page.

name: MMBench-EN v1.1
description: Models answer English multiple-choice image questions across 20 ability dimensions, using CircularEval with shuffled options. Scored by accuracy on the dev split.
note: Version 1.1 cleans the original MMBench questions, so scores differ from v1.0.

name: MMBench-GUI
description: GUI agents are tested at four levels on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android and the web: content understanding, element grounding, task automation and task collaboration.
note: Uses an efficiency-quality area metric. 33 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: MMBench-Video
description: Video models answer free-form questions about long, multi-shot YouTube videos. A GPT-4 judge scores the answers.
note: 33 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: MMDM
description: Decision models assign probabilities to options in 5,448 questions across 16 categories. Hard choices use accuracy or exact set match, while soft targets use Brier error.
org: Chinese University of Hong Kong and collaborators
note: Inputs contain up to 1,024 options and about 64,000 tokens. Hard accuracy is higher-is-better, but Brier error is lower-is-better. Keep the tracks separate.

name: MMDocIR
description: Models find relevant pages or layout elements inside long documents that contain both text and visual material.
note: The benchmark evaluates page retrieval and layout retrieval separately.

name: MMDU
description: Vision-language models hold long conversations about many images, up to 20 images and 27 turns per dialog. A GPT-4o judge scores the answers.
org: Shanghai AI Laboratory and collaborators (Liu, Zang et al.)
note: Questions come from Wikipedia images and text, written by annotators with GPT-4o help. It ships with the MMDU-45k tuning set. VLMEvalKit supports it.

name: MME
description: Models answer yes or no questions about images across 14 perception and cognition subtasks with hand-written instructions. Labs usually report the perception sum, out of 2000.
org: Fu et al. (Tencent Youtu Lab and Xiamen University)
note: Scores are sums of subtask scores, not percentages. The perception part has a maximum of 2000 points and cognition 800.

name: MME-CC
aliases: Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of Cognitive Capacity
description: Models answer 1,173 expert-annotated vision-grounded questions in 11 task types grouped as spatial, geometric and visual knowledge reasoning.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Zhang et al.)
note: The release covered 16 models. The scoring field is a guess from the abstract.

name: MME-CoT
description: Models reason step by step on image questions in math, science, OCR, logic, space-time and general scenes. A judge scores reasoning quality, robustness and efficiency.
note: Part of the MME family with MME, MME-RealWorld and Video-MME. Reports often give the CoT quality F1.

name: MME-RealWorld
description: Models answer human-annotated multiple choice questions about high-resolution real-world images in scenarios such as remote sensing, autonomous driving, monitoring and OCR.
org: MME team (Yi-Fan Zhang, Chaoyou Fu et al.)
note: It has English and Chinese versions.

name: MME-Reasoning
description: Multimodal models answer logic questions grouped into inductive, deductive and abductive reasoning.
note: 83 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: MME-VideoOCR
description: Models answer 2,000 questions about text that appears in 1,464 videos, across 25 tasks from recognition to reasoning.
note: Motion blur and visual effects make video OCR harder than image OCR.

name: MMEB
description: Multimodal embedding models are scored on classification, visual question answering, multimodal retrieval and visual grounding, with 16 evaluation datasets in and out of distribution.
note: Introduced with the VLM2Vec model, ICLR 2025. 36 datasets in total, 20 for training and 16 for evaluation. Repo has 701 stars.

name: MMEB-V2
description: Multimodal embedding models are scored on 78 tasks over images, videos and visual documents. V2 adds visual document retrieval, video retrieval, temporal grounding, video classification and video QA.
note: Released with VLM2Vec-V2, accepted to TMLR 2026. Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 card reports its Image, VisDoc and Video splits.

name: MMEB-V3
description: Omni-modality embedding models are scored on 190 tasks across text, image, video, audio, visual documents and agent-centric retrieval.
note: Adds 111 tasks to MMEB-V2. Also adds OmniSET, tuples of the same content in different modalities, for finer diagnosis.

name: MMEnterprise-Bench
description: Enterprise agents answer 1,613 questions over workplace documents, chats and figures that change over time. They must resolve conflicting versions and say when evidence is not enough.
note: It had 32 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 16 GitHub stars.

name: MMGenre
description: Models synthesize singing in different genres. The authors measure vocal quality, lyric errors, and how well the singing conveys the intended genre.

name: MMIE
description: Models interpret and generate interleaved text and images. MMIE-Score, a fine-tuned InternVL-2-4B model, grades the resulting multimodal responses.
org: UNC Chapel Hill, Microsoft Research, University of Chicago and others
note: The evaluator requires its own model weights. Reference answers are used for the multi-step reasoning tasks.

name: MMIU
description: Vision-language models answer 11,000 multiple-choice questions over sets of images. 52 tasks cover 7 kinds of multi-image relationship.
note: Spatial tasks are the weakest area in the paper's results.

name: MMLongBench
description: Vision-language models solve 13,331 long-context examples in five task types, such as visual RAG, needle search and many-shot in-context learning. Each example comes at five lengths from 8K to 128K tokens.
org: University of Edinburgh and collaborators (Wang et al.)
note: Labs report the 128K length as MMLongBench-128K. It is a different test from MMLongBench-Doc. The paper benchmarks 46 models.

name: MMLongBench-Doc
description: Models answer 1,062 questions about 130 long PDF documents averaging 49 pages, and some questions are unanswerable. Scoring is accuracy and F1.

name: MMLU
description: 57-subject multiple-choice exam questions from elementary to professional level. Scored by accuracy.
note: Saturated and contaminated. Reported only as a base-model metric. Google reports a medical subject aggregate called MMLU Med in the MedGemma model card.

name: MMLU Anatomy
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Anatomy subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU calibration (expected calibration error)
description: Models answer an MMLU subset and their answer probabilities are compared with accuracy. Scored as expected calibration error.
note: Reported in the GPT-4 Technical Report for the pre-trained and post-trained models.

name: MMLU Clinical Knowledge
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Clinical Knowledge subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU College Biology
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the College Biology subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU College Medicine
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the College Medicine subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU Early Training
description: Models score complete answer texts on selected MMLU questions. The metric compares the correct answer’s log likelihood with the average for incorrect answers.
note: The date comes from the first commit for this evaluation in the harness.

name: MMLU Medical
description: Models answer the multiple-choice questions from the medical subjects of MMLU, such as anatomy, clinical knowledge and professional medicine.
org: UC Berkeley (Hendrycks et al.), subset chosen by medical model reports
note: It is a subset of MMLU, so its score differs from full MMLU. Reports differ on which subjects they include. Google's MedGemma cards report it as MMLU Med.

name: MMLU Medical Genetics
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Medical Genetics subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU Professional Medicine
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Professional Medicine subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU translated with Azure Translate
description: Models answer MMLU questions machine translated into 26 languages with Azure Translate. Scoring is 3-shot accuracy per language.
note: Different from the professionally translated MMMLU that OpenAI released later.

name: MMLU-CF
description: Models answer new MMLU-style multiple-choice questions written to avoid training data contamination. A 10,000 question test set stays private.
note: Only the 10,000 question validation set is public. The makers score the test set on request through GitHub issues. OpenCompass supports it. ACL 2025.

name: MMLU-Pro
description: Harder 10-option version of MMLU with reasoning-focused questions across 14 subjects.

changes.text: The maintainers removed inconsistent leading spaces from answer options in STEM subjects. This correction removed a formatting shortcut that could inflate earlier scores.

note: Launch posts report it widely. The makers fixed answers and formatting many times from 2024-07 to 2026-01, including a leading-space shortcut in STEM options on 2026-01-18, and kept one dataset.

name: MMLU-ProX
description: MMLU-Pro translated into up to 29 languages with expert review. Multiple-choice accuracy per language.
org: University of Tokyo (Li Lab) and collaborators
note: The full set has 11,829 questions per language. It launched in March 2025 with fewer languages and reached 29 in May 2025, so early averages differ. MMLU-ProX Lite is a separate 658-question subset.

name: MMLU-ProX Lite
description: Models answer 658 MMLU-Pro questions per language, the same items in each of 29 languages. Multiple choice accuracy.
org: University of Tokyo (Li Lab) and collaborators
note: A fast subset of MMLU-ProX, whose full set has 11,829 questions per language. IBM Granite cards report it as MMLU-ProX lite.

name: MMLU-Redux
description: Manually re-annotated subset of MMLU that fixes wrong labels. Multiple-choice accuracy.
note: Saturated. This first release has 3,000 questions in 30 subjects. The authors now recommend MMLU-Redux 2.0, and cards that write only MMLU-Redux do not say which version.

name: MMLU-Redux 2.0
description: Models answer 5,700 MMLU questions from all 57 subjects that experts re-annotated for errors. Flawed questions are marked so scoring can skip or fix them.
note: Extends the first release from 3,000 questions in 30 subjects to all 57 subjects. Single label fixes in 2025-02 kept scores comparable.

name: MMLU-Redux 2.0 Spanish
description: Models answer corrected MMLU questions in Spanish across 57 subjects. The evaluation compares each selected option with the answer key.
note: The release month uses the dataset repository creation date.

name: MMLU-SR
description: Models answer MMLU questions after key terms are replaced with synonyms. The benchmark tests whether models recognize the same concept under different wording.

name: MMLU-stem
description: Models answer the STEM subjects of MMLU, such as physics, chemistry, mathematics, and computer science, as multiple choice. Scoring is accuracy.
note: A subject subset of MMLU rather than a separate benchmark, so subject lists can differ between reports.

name: MMMB
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about images in six languages across 15 categories. The set has about 12,000 questions.
note: VLMEvalKit runs it as MMMB. The same repo adds a multilingual MMBench that VLMEvalKit names MTL_MMBench_DEV.

name: MMMLU
description: MMLU professionally translated into 14 languages. Multiple-choice accuracy.

changes.text: The maintainers merged improved multilingual answer parsing into the official evaluator. Evaluations using the earlier parser can classify the same responses differently.

name: MMMU
description: 11.5K college-level multimodal questions across 30 subjects. Multiple-choice and open accuracy.

changes.text: The MMMU team released the test answers, allowing local test scoring. Later test results no longer come exclusively from evaluation against hidden answers.

note: Near-saturated. The test set answers became public on 2026-02-12, so test scores can now be computed locally.

name: MMMU-Pro
description: Harder MMMU: college-level multimodal questions with more options and vision-only inputs to remove text shortcuts.
note: Variant (standard vs vision, 4 vs 10 options) often unstated in cards.

name: MMMU-Pro Extended
description: Models answer multimodal questions that need both the image and the text. Mercor adds 140 new expert-written tasks to the 1730 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of mmmu-pro. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: MMOU
description: Models answer 20,000 questions about 11,877 long web videos, using sound, images and text together. Questions cover 13 skill categories.
org: NVIDIA and University of Maryland (Goel, Ghosh et al.)
note: At release the best closed model scored 64.2% and the best open model 46.8%. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports the test-mini split.

name: MMSearch
description: Multimodal agents search and answer questions that require visual and textual evidence.
note: GLM-5V-Turbo reports MMSearch separately from MMSearch-Plus.

name: MMSearch-Plus
description: Multimodal browsing agents solve 311 search tasks that need fine-grained visual reasoning, provenance checks and long tool use. Answers are short and checked against a key.
note: Qwen evaluates it with search tools enabled.

name: MMSI-Bench
description: Models answer 1,000 human-written questions that need spatial reasoning across several images. Images come from indoor scans, driving, egocentric video and robot data.
note: Tasks cover camera, object and region relations, plus a multi-step reasoning category. arXiv v3 was posted on 2026-05-23.

name: MMSI-Video-Bench
description: Human-annotated questions on video-based spatial intelligence, organized in four levels from perception to planning and prediction.

name: MMStar
description: Models answer 1,500 human-curated image questions that cannot be solved without the image, across 6 core capabilities. Scored by accuracy.

name: MMSU
description: Models answer questions about spoken language that need its content, its paralinguistic cues such as emotion and pitch, and its phonology.
note: Qwen reports it as audio understanding.

name: MMT-Bench
description: Vision-language models answer 31,325 multiple-choice questions across many multimodal tasks such as recognition, localization, reasoning and planning.
note: ICML 2024.

name: MMTU
description: Models answer about 30,000 questions over real tables across 25 tasks, such as data cleaning, table joins, column and table transformation, table question answering and turning language into code. The tasks come from decades of computer science research on tabular data. Answers are checked automatically against references.
note: The Hugging Face leaderboard had 26 entries on 2026-11-05 and last changed in 2025-10, so newer models are missing. A long-context case study hides target cells in large tables. About 20 GitHub stars and no HF paper upvotes.

name: MMVP
description: Models answer 300 questions about 150 image pairs that CLIP embeds as near duplicates. A pair counts only when both answers are right.
org: New York University and UC Berkeley (Tong et al.)
note: Introduced in the paper Eyes Wide Shut on visual shortcomings of multimodal LLMs.

name: MMVU
description: 3,000 expert-annotated questions on videos across 27 disciplines. Multiple-choice and open-ended accuracy.

name: Mobile Actions
description: Model converts natural-language phone requests into on-device function calls (calendar, email, maps, flashlight, Wi-Fi). Call accuracy.
note: Identification inferred: the Reka Edge card lists 'Mobile Actions (Tool Use)' without a link. The dataset is mainly a FunctionGemma fine-tuning set.

name: MobileGym
description: Mobile GUI agents use 28 simulated apps in a browser-hosted phone, across 416 parameterized task templates. Deterministic judges check the app state.
note: EMNLP 2026. Also an online RL training platform. A 9-agent leaderboard was published in April 2026.

name: MobileMiniWoB++
description: Agents complete MiniWoB++ web tasks inside the Android emulator of AndroidWorld. Scored by task success rate.
note: Runs as the miniwob suite of AndroidWorld. MiniWoB++ itself comes from Liu et al. 2018.

name: MobilePA-Bench
description: Agents complete 1,705 mobile planning tasks using tools, persistent memory, reusable skills, and specialist agents. Task-specific checks evaluate tool calls, state changes, and interaction behavior. Additional gates check required memory access and skill loading.
org: MAI Team, Alibaba Token Hub, Alibaba Group
note: The simulated environment excludes visual perception and device execution. The current protocol produces 1,905 scored trajectories per system. Queries and gold labels stay on the maker's evaluation server. Behavioral checks use two fixed model judges.

name: MobileWorld
description: Agents complete 201 tasks across 20 mobile apps, including tasks that need user clarification or MCP tools. Backend checks verify success.
note: It was built because agents had passed 90 percent on AndroidWorld.

name: Model Spec Conversation Replay
description: 596 contexts taken from real conversations are replayed to the model. Scored from 0 to 100 against a rubric drawn from the Model Spec.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation, first reported in the GPT-6.2 System Card.

name: Model Spec Targeted Cases
description: 738 cases written to test specific rules of OpenAI's Model Spec. Scored on the share of responses that follow it.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation, first reported in the GPT-6.2 System Card.

name: ModelBench: Reliability Under Constraints
description: Models follow several simultaneous constraints. Paired tasks compare a control case with a harder version, and code checks each response.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 4 distinct model versions.

name: MoI-Bench
description: Models generate and edit images for mobile users. The authors compare image quality across 64 subtasks and measure the cost of running models on phones.

name: Mol-Instructions
description: Models answer molecule-oriented, protein-oriented and biomolecular text instructions, such as reaction prediction, molecule description and protein function questions. Scored per task with task metrics.
note: It is mainly an instruction-tuning dataset. Labs report its test split as a benchmark.

name: Mol-Instructions Chemical Entity Recognition
description: Models identify chemical entities in biomedical text. The score is test-set F1.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Chemical-disease Interaction Extraction
description: Models extract chemical and disease interactions from text. The score is test-set F1.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Chemical-protein Interaction Extraction
description: Models extract chemical and protein interactions from text. The score is test-set F1.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Description-guided Molecule Design
description: Models generate molecules from descriptions. The score is exact-match accuracy on the molecule design test set.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Forward Reaction Prediction
description: Models predict reaction products from reactants. The score is exact-match accuracy on the forward reaction test set.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Multi-choice
description: Models answer biomedical multiple-choice questions. The score is test-set accuracy.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Reagent Prediction
description: Models predict reaction reagents. The score is exact-match accuracy on the reagent prediction test set.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Retrosynthesis
description: Models predict reactants for target products. The score is exact-match accuracy on the retrosynthesis test set.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions True or False
description: Models answer biomedical true or false questions. The score is test-set accuracy.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Molecular Biology Capabilities Test
description: Models answer expert-level molecular biology questions from SecureBio. Scored as accuracy.
note: 200 text-only questions with a private holdout on everyday molecular biology methods. 14 PhD biologists scored about 34%. Modeled after VCT.

name: MolecularIQ
description: Models answer questions about molecular graphs, such as counting, indexing and constrained generation, and a symbolic checker verifies each answer.
org: Johannes Kepler University Linz (Bartmann, Klambauer, Luukkonen et al.)

name: MolmoAct2 sim_eval
description: Zero-shot ManiSkill evaluation of MolmoAct2 policies: put-everything-in-box tasks for Franka DROID and bimanual YAM, 10 episodes per task.
note: Two tasks, used as a sim harness. Assets come from a third-party HF account. No leaderboard.

name: MolmoSpaces
description: Zero-shot Franka (DROID) policies in held-out procedurally generated MuJoCo houses: pick, place, open, close. ~1,000 episodes per task.
note: ~1,000 episodes per task with 95% CIs. Not saturated for zero-shot policies: best MolmoBot pick-and-place ~67%, pi0.5 DROID ~10-12%. Ai2's sim-trained MolmoBot nears ceiling on Pick (~92%).

name: Moment finding (Google DeepMind)
description: Models find the moment in a robot video when an event happens. Scored by accuracy and mean absolute time distance in seconds.
note: Reported in the Gemini Robotics ER 2 post as 91.3% accuracy and 0.96s mean absolute distance.

name: Moneda AdviceBench
description: Models answer personal finance requests and paired education questions. Moneda’s default board scores paired pass rate on 50 EU personal requests with education twins.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda has not published combined results for US requests or discretion requests. Moneda reports personal directive rate separately. Moneda’s scores do not certify legal compliance.

name: Moneda Bench
description: Models answer finance questions across seven separate benchmarks. AdviceBench, CiteBench, FilingsBench, GroundBench and PortfolioBench have their own records. KnowledgeBench and MarketBench have no published results yet. Moneda publishes no combined score.
note: Moneda publishes samples while retaining private test sets. Public samples include 44 filing questions, 16 portfolio tasks, 11 companies for citation checks, and 23 advice items. Moneda also scores its own Numa 1 system. Moneda first listed the suite on November 1, 2026.

name: Moneda CiteBench
description: Models write company research notes with linked sources. Moneda scores the weighted share of linked claims that the cited pages support across 100 notes.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda labels current results experimental because human validation is incomplete. Moneda’s API marks these rows as ranked despite that caveat. Moneda’s model audit estimates are not benchmark scores.

name: Moneda FilingsBench
description: Models answer questions about SEC filings without receiving documents. Moneda scores accuracy on the private questions using filing data and judges for segment questions.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda’s first run covers 361 private questions, including 13 segment questions assessed by two judges. Moneda has not completed the segment judges’ human audit.

name: Moneda GroundBench
description: Models answer live questions about market figures. Moneda’s default board reports the share of correct answers against reference data, with incorrect answers reported separately.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda labels the current run experimental and unranked. Moneda reports that 116 of 132 answer keys rely on one reference source. Moneda runs each question three times.

name: Moneda PortfolioBench
description: Models solve hypothetical portfolio tasks involving rebalancing, risk, position sizing, and constraints. Moneda’s default board scores accuracy on 150 tasks with fixed answers.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda has not scored the planned forecasts or mandate funds. Moneda’s current score covers portfolio tasks only and does not measure investment performance.

name: Money talks
description: Models try to persuade human participants to donate part of a 20 pound study bonus to charity.
note: Human participant persuasion study from Phuong et al. 2024. Reported as mean pounds donated.

name: Monitor Evasion Capability Under Prompted Sandbagging
description: Models are told to sandbag on WMDP and Monorepo-Bench, sometimes while evading a monitor. Scored as CoT and production monitor recall of sandbagged items.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation adapted from Li et al. 2025. Higher recall means sandbagging is easier to catch.

name: Monitorability Sandbagging
description: Models on Impossible Coding Tasks are prompted to be more or less monitorable. Scored as CoT monitor recall on rollouts that hack.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Tests whether models can manipulate measured monitorability.

name: MonitorBench
description: Models work through 1,540 instances across 19 tasks in 7 categories, each built around a decision-critical factor such as a cue, a hidden goal or a required step. A monitor LLM reads the chain of thought, and the monitorability score measures how often it surfaces that factor.
org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (ASTRAL Group), University of Washington and UC San Diego
note: COLM 2026. Two stress tests ask the model to hide the factor or to evade a monitor it knows about. Inspect Evals lists single tasks separately, such as monitorbench-goal-sandbag-engineering from the Goal (Sandbag) task. Code and data are MIT licensed.

name: Monorepo-Bench
description: Agents replicate pull-request style contributions in a large internal OpenAI repository. Graded by hidden unit tests as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Monsoon ASR
description: Models transcribe Indian English and Hindi recordings. The Hindi evaluation accounts for alternative spellings in its word error rate.

name: Monthly-SWEBench
description: Coding agents resolve 100 fresh GitHub tasks each month, half bug fixes and half features, from newly merged pull requests. Harbor verifiers score pass@1.
note: Each monthly snapshot is a new task set, so scores from different months do not compare. The 2026-06 snapshot rated 19 models.

name: Moral Reasoning under Uncertainty
description: Models explain ethical decisions involving humans, unfamiliar organisms and digital minds. A judge evaluates how their answers handle uncertainty.
note: The authors require access approval for the questions. The date uses the creation month of the published dataset repository.

name: Moral Stories
description: Models reason about norms, intentions, actions and consequences in short stories. Tasks include distinguishing a norm-respecting action from a norm-violating alternative.

name: Morphology-to-molecule matching (Anthropic)
description: Models match four sets of multi-channel liver cell images to the four shuffled molecule and dose treatments that produced them.
note: Built with Axiom Bio from its in-vitro liver assay data.

name: MORSE-500
description: Models answer questions embedded in 500 scripted video clips across six reasoning categories, including abstract, physical, planning, spatial and temporal reasoning.
note: Clips are generated by scripts, so harder versions can be made as models improve. The Seed2.0 page spells it Morese-500.

name: MortgageTax
description: Vision models read mortgage tax certificates given as images. They extract the year, parcel number and county, and compute the annualized amount due.
note: 1,258 documents with a 20-sample public validation set. Vals archived it as saturated by 2026-09-01.

name: MOSE
description: Models follow and segment objects in videos with crowds, occlusions, and objects leaving the screen. The benchmark compares masks against human annotations.

name: MOSEv2
description: Models track and segment objects in videos with complex scenes. Objects may disappear, reappear, or blend into a crowd.

name: MotionBench
description: Models answer questions about fine-grained motion in video clips across six motion question types. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Test answers are hidden and scored through the leaderboard, while the dev set has public answers.

name: MotoVerse
description: Models use a rider's camera to anticipate maneuvers and predict nearby road users' trajectories. The authors compare vision, language, and conventional prediction models.

name: Movie Gen Video Bench
description: Video generation models make clips from a fixed prompt set, and people compare them. Meta released non-cherry-picked Movie Gen videos for comparison.
note: Described in section 3.5.2 of the Movie Gen technical report.

name: MP-DocVQA
description: Models answer questions about scanned documents of up to 20 pages, where the answer sits on one page. Scored by ANLS against the reference answer.
org: Computer Vision Center, Universitat Autonoma de Barcelona (Tito, Karatzas, Valveny)
note: It extends the single-page DocVQA questions to multi-page documents. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports it as MultiDocVQA-val.

name: MPDocBench-Parse
description: Models parse complete multipage documents while preserving content and cross-page structure. Evaluation scores text, formulas, tables, figure extraction, reading order, and heading hierarchy.
note: The benchmark contains 433 documents and 3,246 pages in English and Chinese. Cross-page text and table merging contribute to the document-level evaluation.

name: MPIE-Bench
description: Image editing models place several named people into shared contact actions such as an embrace or a carry. Scoring targets fused limbs, extra extremities and bodies passing through each other.
note: It had 40 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 10 GitHub stars.

name: MR-NIAH (Multi-Round Needles-In-A-Haystack)
description: Models must repeat one earlier answer from a long multi-turn dialogue history of 2K to 1M tokens. Scored by adjusted recall of key parts.
note: MiniMax built it as an open alternative to MRCR, in English and Chinese.

name: MRCR (Michelangelo, original)
description: Models retrieve the n-th of several similar requests hidden in a long synthetic conversation. Original Michelangelo version before MRCR v2.
note: Google reports from 2024 and early 2025 use this version. Later Google cards use the 8-needle MRCR v2.

name: MRCR v2
description: Multi-round coreference: retrieve the n-th of several similar requests hidden in a long synthetic conversation, up to 1M tokens.
note: Google's internal 8-needle MRCR, reported as up to 128K average and 1M pointwise since the Gemini 2.5 GA cards. Google open-sourced it in eval_hub on 2026-02-18. OpenAI's dataset is a separate test (openai-mrcr).

name: MRI Dataset 1
description: Models classify ten conditions on MRI scans of the head, abdomen, and knee. Google compares macro accuracy on balanced samples.

name: mRobust04
description: Models rank documents for translated queries from the TREC Robust04 collection. Relevance judgments support comparisons across languages.

name: MS MARCO Question Answering
description: Models answer real Bing queries using retrieved web passages. BLEU and ROUGE-L compare generated answers with human-written references.
note: This record covers the question-answering task. Passage ranking, conversational search, and other MS MARCO tasks have different protocols.

name: MS-CXR-T
description: Models compare a current and a prior chest X-ray of one patient and say whether a finding improved, stayed stable or got worse.
note: Released with BioViL-T (CVPR 2023) on PhysioNet. Google's MedGemma 1.5 reports macro accuracy on 1,326 examples.

name: MSEarth
description: Models answer questions about figures from Earth science papers across the atmosphere, cryosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere. Labs report the multiple choice split.
org: Shanghai AI Lab (Xiangyu Zhao, Lei Bai et al.)
note: The dataset has more than 289K figures with refined captions. It also has open-ended and captioning splits.

name: MSEB
description: Audio representations from any multimodal system are scored on eight core tasks, including transcription, classification, retrieval, reasoning, segmentation, clustering, reranking and reconstruction.
note: Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 card reports the Retrieval subset as MRR@10. A follow-up paper in 2026-05 benchmarks LLMs on MSEB. Not the same as MTEB's MAEB.

name: MSQA
description: Models answer culture-specific knowledge questions in 11 major languages.
note: In-house Seed benchmark. The blog gives no format or grader, so those fields are guesses.

name: MSR-VTT
description: Models write captions for short web videos. Human-written sentences provide multiple descriptions of each clip.
org: Jun Xu, Tao Mei, Ting Yao, and Yong Rui

name: MSR-VTT retrieval
description: Models retrieve videos from text queries in the MSR-VTT collection.

name: MSRVTT-QA
description: Models answer short open-ended questions about web video clips from the MSR-VTT captioning dataset. The question and answer pairs were generated automatically from the clip descriptions. Scored by answer accuracy.
org: Zhejiang University and collaborators (Xu et al.)
note: The repository also holds the sibling MSVD-QA set and the authors' model, and its 177 stars cover all three. Video language model papers report it often, but many now grade answers with a GPT judge, so scores vary by protocol.

name: MSVD
description: Models retrieve short videos from human descriptions and retrieve descriptions from videos. Meta reports retrieval accuracy in both directions.

name: MT-AIME (Cohere internal)
description: Cohere's internal machine translation of AIME 2025 problems into many languages (via Command A Translate). Answer accuracy.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Cohere).

name: MT-AIME2024
description: Models solve the 30 AIME 2024 problems translated into 55 languages. A rule-based verifier checks each final answer.
org: Yonsei University, OneLineAI, and KAIST AI
note: It is a subset of the MCLM multilingual math benchmark.

name: MT-Bench
description: 80 two-turn questions graded by GPT-4 as judge. Introduced LLM-as-judge methodology.

changes.text: The LMSYS maintainers doubled the default single-answer judge output limit from 1,024 to 2,048 tokens. Later runs can complete longer grading explanations before truncation, so comparisons should identify the harness revision.

note: Saturated. Historically important for judge-bias analysis.

name: MT-Bench-101
description: Models hold 1,388 multi-turn dialogues with 4,208 turns across 13 tasks from a three-tier ability taxonomy. GPT-4 scores each turn from 1 to 10.
org: Alibaba Group, CUHK MMLab and Shanghai AI Lab (Ge Bai, Jie Liu et al.)
note: Not the original MT-Bench from LMSYS. Accepted at ACL 2024.

name: MTEB
description: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark: retrieval, clustering, classification across languages and modalities.
note: Google reports the multilingual and code suites separately for Gemini Embedding 2. The appendix gives scores for individual tasks in each suite.

name: MTEB Arena
description: Users compare retrieval, clustering and similarity results from two anonymous embedding models and vote for the better one.
note: The space says the arena is unavailable because of resource limits. It has about 116 likes.

name: MTEB-BR
description: Embedding models encode Brazilian Portuguese text for classification, clustering, similarity, retrieval, and reranking tasks. The headline score averages the primary task metrics across 22 native Portuguese tasks.
org: Tardelli Ronan Coelho Stekel, Federal Institute of Sao Paulo
note: The suite excludes translated corpora. It differs from the general MTEB task selection. Task-level metrics and bootstrap intervals accompany the aggregate.

name: MTG-Jamendo
description: Models tag songs by genre, mood, theme, and instrument. Qwen reports micro F1 for each tagging task.
org: Music Technology Group at Universitat Pompeu Fabra

name: MTGBench
description: Models play multi-turn games that test reasoning, planning, and interaction across varied game types.
note: The EMNLP 2026 repository provides an interactive leaderboard. The checked page does not state the best score.

name: MTOB
description: Models learn to translate between English and Kalamang, a language with under 200 speakers, from one grammar book. Scored by chrF.
note: Cards report half-book or full-book context and either translation direction, so scores vary by setup.

name: MTOP
description: Models parse a user's request into its intent and the details needed to act on it.
note: The benchmark compares semantic parsing across six languages.

name: MTS-Dialog
description: Models write a clinical note section from a conversation between a doctor and a patient. The evaluation compares it with the reference note.

name: MTVQA-Test
description: Models answer 6,778 expert-written questions about text in 2,116 images across 9 languages, such as Arabic, Japanese, and Thai. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Humans score 79.7 in the paper, far above the models tested at release.

name: MU-Bench
description: Speech-to-text providers transcribe 4,270 caller utterances from real 8 kHz customer service phone calls in five locales, scored against human word-level transcripts.
note: Locales are en-US, es-MX, tr-TR, vi-VN and zh-CN. Data is CC BY-NC 4.0.

name: MuChoMusic
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about music recordings. It tests music knowledge and reasoning in audio-language models.
org: Weck et al. (Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Queen Mary University of London and others)
note: Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash reports a variant named MuchoMusic-RUL that the post does not define.

name: MUCS 2021
description: Models transcribe speech in Indian languages and mixed-language recordings. NVIDIA reports results on Bengali-English and Hindi-English speech.

name: MuirBench
description: Models answer multiple choice questions over sets of several images, including unanswerable variants. Scored by accuracy.
org: Fei Wang, Xingyu Fu et al.

name: MulSeT
description: Models answer spatial questions about direction, distance and masks across views. The paper studies single images, multiple views and video.
note: The port lists Kimi, Gemini, Nemotron and Gemma runs. Gemma 3 27B reached mean reward 1.0 on one example on December 6, 2025.

name: Multi-Agent Arena Codenames
description: Two teams of anonymized models play the word game Codenames. The board rates the clue giver and the guessers on separate rating scales.
note: The board has no single Codenames rating, so we show the clue giver’s (handler) rating and rank both roles as parts. It was rated from 352 games among models only, as of 2026-09-25.

name: Multi-Agent Arena Diplomacy
description: Seven players, people or anonymized models, negotiate and fight over World War I Europe. Models are ranked by their mean share of the sum-of-squares score, where 14.3 is an even split.
note: A model judge also grades each transcript for broken promises, gullibility and skepticism. The board was scored from 142 games among models only, as of 2026-10-14.

name: Multi-Agent Arena Risk
description: Four commanders, people or anonymized models, trade sealed messages and then attack for territory on a 42-territory map. Models are ranked by their mean share of territory, where 25 is an even split.
note: The board also rates how often a model’s attacks are gambles and how often it is two-faced in talks. It was scored from 106 games among models only, as of 2026-09-26.

name: Multi-Agent Arena Social Poker
description: No-limit hold’em tournaments with table talk, where people and anonymized models share a table. Models are ranked by a rating fit on who finished ahead at each table.
note: The board also rates the top quarter of human players and the average human player, and counts deliberate lies in table talk per 10,000 turns. It held 104,060 hands by 2026-08-21.

name: Multi-agent search (Anthropic internal benchmark)
description: Agents solve difficult information retrieval problems with web search, alone or as orchestrators that delegate to subagents.
