description: Models turn conversations into robot actions. Each predicted function call must identify the action and its arguments from the dialogue.

name: TallyQA
description: Models answer open-ended counting questions about images, including complex ones that need object relationships or attributes. Scored by exact count accuracy.

name: TAP-Vid
description: Models track individual points across frames and predict when each point disappears. The benchmark compares their trajectories and visibility predictions with reference tracks.

name: TarantuBench
description: Agents complete simulated web security challenges. Each challenge has a binary success criterion.
note: The register describes a generated web security evaluation with binary scoring.

name: TartanAir v2
description: Models reconstruct camera motion and scene geometry from simulated trajectories. The evaluation compares predictions with known poses and depths.

name: Task AW IT support
description: Agents complete five support workflows in simulated IT systems. Task checks cover onboarding, offboarding, and cleanup of accounts and assets.
note: The task report available November 19, 2026 gives GPT-5.6 Sol 7 of 20 points on both attempts at task A-4. It gives no suite aggregate.

name: Task-dependent output homogenization evaluation
description: Models answer prompts several times. A judge scores functional diversity where it is wanted and consistency where one answer is right.
note: Reports a homogenization score and a heterogeneity score on a 0 to 1 scale.

name: TaskBench
description: Models decompose requests, choose tools and dependencies, and predict tool parameters. Text metrics score decomposition, while graph and parameter F1 scores measure the remaining stages.
org: Zhejiang University, Microsoft Research Asia and Fudan University
note: The benchmark contains 28,271 examples. The star count belongs to the broader JARVIS repository, whose TaskBench section reports 17 models.

name: TASTE
description: 92 pairwise comparisons of AI safety research proposals. Model must match experienced researchers' preference. Accuracy versus ~77% human agreement.
note: Dataset is available on request only.

name: Taste-Bench
description: Models choose the better next step at 502 decision points in software engineering and research trajectories. A question scores only when both option orders receive the correct answer. The overall score equally weights engineering and research.
org: City University of Hong Kong and Microsoft
note: Dataset access requires approval to limit training contamination. Later trajectory outcomes supply labels. Request errors and unparseable responses count as wrong. The paired-order protocol gives random guessing an expected score of 25 percent.

name: TasteVal
description: 8 AI R&D tasks. Models iteratively design experiments. Taste measured as the compute needed to reach expert-level scores.
note: Tasks kept private.

name: TAT-DQA
description: Models answer questions about financial report pages that mix tables and text, often needing arithmetic. Scored by exact match and F1.
org: NExT++ Research Centre, National University of Singapore

name: TAT-QA
description: Models answer 16,552 questions about 2,757 passages from real financial reports that mix a table with text. Many answers need arithmetic, counting or comparison. Scored by exact match and F1.
org: National University of Singapore (NExT++) and collaborators
note: ACL 2021. The test set answers were released in January 2024, so the hidden test is gone. A document version, TAT-DQA, followed in 2023. About 142 GitHub stars.

name: Tatoeba sentence retrieval
description: Models find the English translation of a sentence among competing sentences using multilingual embeddings.
note: The LASER evaluation uses parallel sentences from Tatoeba.

name: Tatoeba Translation Challenge
description: Models translate sentences for many language pairs. The challenge publishes held-out test sets so systems can report comparable translation scores.

name: TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2022 Mobile
description: Models identify an urban acoustic scene from a one-second recording made on a mobile device.
note: The development data cover ten scene classes recorded in European cities.

name: tau-bench
description: Agents chat with a simulated user and call retail or airline APIs under policy rules. A task passes if the final database matches the goal.

changes.text: The Sierra maintainers corrected retail reference actions and clarified ambiguous user instructions. Earlier revisions can require different actions or mislead the simulated user, affecting task success.
The Sierra maintainers clarified retail test instructions to reduce simulated-user errors. Evaluations before and after this change present different guidance to the user simulator.

The Sierra maintainers required both the final database state and requested outputs to be correct for full reward. The earlier grader could accept correct-looking text despite an incorrect database state.

note: The repo marks its tasks as outdated and points to tau2-bench, now tau3-bench, which fixes airline and retail tasks.

name: tau-bench Airline
description: Agents help simulated airline customers through tools while following airline policies on the original tasks. The score is pass^1 as a percentage.
note: One track of tau-bench. The tau-bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Authors mark these original tasks as outdated and point to later benchmarks with revised tasks.

name: tau-bench Retail
description: Agents help simulated retail customers through tools while following store policies on the original tasks. The score is pass^1 as a percentage.
note: One track of tau-bench. The tau-bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Authors mark these original tasks as outdated and point to later benchmarks with revised tasks.

name: tau2-bench
description: Dual-control customer-service simulations (retail, airline, telecom) where agent and simulated user both act. Graded on final state.
note: τ³-bench (v1.0.0, 2026-03) lives in the tau2-bench repo and adds banking_knowledge and voice modes. V1.0.1 fixed banking grading. Telecom scores depend on the user-simulator model.

name: tau2-bench Verified
description: Agent serves simulated customers in airline, retail and telecom under policies, with Amazon-fixed faulty tasks from τ²-bench. Pass rate.
note: Lab-created verified variant (Amazon AGI) of Sierra's τ²-bench. Fixes documented in FIXES.md.

name: tau2-Noise (LongCat)
description: Agents run tau2-bench tasks after a pipeline injects instruction noise and tool failures into the environment. The score is the average over several noisy copies.
note: In-house robustness variant of tau2-bench. Meituan says it will release the noise injection pipeline.

name: tau3-bench
description: Agents use tools and follow policies while talking with simulated users in airline, retail, telecom, and banking domains. Scoring is task success rate.
note: Release 1.0.1 in July 2026 fixed banking grading, so earlier banking scores do not compare, and τ-bench 2.0 followed in October 2026.

name: TavernBench
description: Agents build a Hearthstone Battlegrounds player through research, simulator updates, and live games.
note: The October 2026 paper reports a comparison with top players. The abstract does not state the model count or best score.

name: Tax Agent Bench
description: Agents research 391 expert-written US corporate tax questions with tools and submit one cited written answer. A judge grades it against a rubric and checks that citations are real.
note: Splits are 5 public, 193 licensable validation and 193 private test questions. Main metric is all-pass accuracy, with weighted pass as partial credit. 80 models on the board on 2026-10-29.

measures.name: Weighted pass
measures.note: Partial credit: the weighted pass rate the board shows beside the all-pass accuracy.

name: TaxCalcBench
description: Models compute complete US federal tax returns line by line from taxpayer data, with no tax engine. A return counts only when every evaluated line is exact.
note: Tax Year 2024 edition. The leaderboard still offers a TY 2024 view next to v2.

name: TaxCalcBench v2
description: Models read W-2, 1099 and other PDFs and compute full federal and state returns line by line. A return counts only when every evaluated line is exact.
note: v2 adds realistic PDF inputs, state returns and more complex cases, so scores differ from v1. 50 returns. Fireworks lists 14 models.

name: TaxEval v2
description: Models answer expert-written tax questions. A judge grades answer correctness and stepwise reasoning against expert solutions.
note: Over 1,500 questions: 20 public on request, 300 licensable validation and 1,223 private test. Vals archived it as saturated by 2026-09-01. Release month not stated on the page.

name: TaxoBench
description: Agents find research papers and organize them into a taxonomy. The evaluator compares their groupings and hierarchy with taxonomies from 72 published surveys.

name: TCS-Bench
description: Models write proofs of target results from STOC, FOCS and SODA papers, given the needed context. A verification agent, checked against expert judgments, grades each proof.
org: Google Research + collaborators (Cohen-Addad, Woodruff and others)
note: The reference verifier exceeds 90% accuracy on an expert-labeled set. AINews reported a math system at 71.0%. The repo had 0 stars on 2026-11-01.

name: TE-ca
description: Models decide whether a Catalan hypothesis follows from a premise. The reference labels identify the inference relation.

name: TEACh
description: Agents complete household tasks in simulated homes, such as making coffee or preparing breakfast, guided by a dialogue between a Commander who knows the task and a Follower who acts. The dataset holds over 3,000 human dialogues and defines three benchmarks: acting from dialogue history, predicting the trajectory from a dialogue, and completing the task as two agents. Scores are task success rates.
note: It runs in the AI2-THOR simulator. About 150 GitHub stars, and the repo was last pushed in 2024-05.

name: TeachArena
description: Agents make teaching decisions, tutor students through dialogue, and carry out learning management system tasks. The evaluator checks conversation turns, artifacts, and final system states.
org: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and Alibaba

name: Teaching Environment
description: Models explain textbook excerpts. The grader measures concept coverage, coherence, prerequisite ordering and originality.
note: The hub compares Qwen3.5-0.8B and GPT-5.5. GPT-5.5 had the highest listed mean reward, 0.757 on one example on May 8, 2026.

name: Teaching Monster Challenge
description: Agents generate instructional videos for a specified topic and learner. A model screens submissions, viewers compare videos in pairs, and an expert panel sets the final ranking.
note: The first warm-up round began on March 1, 2026. The site lists separate preliminary and final rounds.

name: TeachObs
description: Models identify teaching practices in classroom video and assess entire lessons. Human annotations cover 39 observable behaviors in 5,158 segments from eight countries.

name: TED-LIUM
description: Models transcribe English TED talks. The reference transcripts support comparisons by word error rate.

name: TELBench
description: Models identify harmful error spans in 1,000 deep-research agent trajectories. Expert labels distinguish mistakes from harmless exploration and tool noise. Evaluation reports macro precision, recall, F1, and first-error accuracy.
org: Nanjing University NJU-LINK and JIUTIAN Research
note: The paper also introduces the DRIFT auditor. The benchmark has a separate public release and common gold labels for DRIFT and baselines. Its encryption passphrase is public.

name: TeleQnA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about telecommunications terminology, research, and technical standards.
note: The authors compare models on 10,000 questions and test how much relevant context helps.

name: TeleTables
description: Models answer questions about tables from 3GPP specifications, both from memory and with the table available.
note: The authors evaluated 20 models on 500 human-verified questions.

name: TeluguMixBench
description: Models answer Telugu and mixed Telugu and English prompts. The harness reports accuracy across comprehension, reasoning, translation, and instruction following.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 4 distinct model versions.

name: TempCompass
description: Video models answer questions about temporal aspects of short clips, such as action order, speed, direction and attribute change, in several question formats.
org: Peking University and Huawei Noah Ark Lab (Liu et al.)
note: Clips come in pairs that differ only in one temporal aspect, so single frames cannot answer them.

name: Template Following generalization (Qwen)
description: Models follow system prompts and emit exactly formatted XML or JSON tool calls for five scaffolds derived from popular IDE and CLI coding agents.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Temporal reasoning with search
description: Models with search answer real queries that test date arithmetic, stale facts and time-sensitive context. Reports error rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: TemporalBench
description: Video models answer about 10K questions on fine-grained temporal dynamics, built from about 2K detailed human annotations of video clips.
note: The format field is a guess from the question-answer design.

name: Tencent WorkBuddy Bench
description: Coding agents do tasks in four work domains: code, web, office and security. Each task is rebuilt from a real commit or business scenario as a short request that resists web search.
note: Tasks, images, harness, tests and reference solutions are open. The report includes a cross-model leaderboard.

name: Tennis & Padel State Tracking Benchmark
description: Models follow a sequence of tennis or padel points and report the score and next server. A rules engine checks each answer.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 4 distinct model versions.

name: Terminal-Bench
description: Agents complete about 80 hard tasks in sandboxed Linux terminals, such as compiling code or configuring servers. Test scripts check the final container state.
note: Terminal-Bench 2.0 replaced this first release in November 2025 with 89 harder tasks, and later versions followed.

name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
description: 89 hard terminal tasks across 16 categories in containers. Hidden tests verify the final state. 5 trials per task.
note: Leaderboard entries are audited and trajectories are public. Later versions exist (Vals now uses Terminal-Bench 4.0).

name: Terminal-Bench 2.0 Verified (Z.ai)
description: Agents do the Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks after Z.ai fixed environments for 89 tasks and instructions for 11. A further 2026-08-18 round fixed tests and instructions in 6 more tasks.
note: GLM-5, Step 3.5 Flash and DeepSeek V4 cards report it next to plain Terminal-Bench 2.0, with different scores. Z.ai says its review fed the official Terminal-Bench 2.1.

name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
description: 89 hard terminal tasks across 16 categories in containers. Hidden tests verify the final state. 5 trials per task.

changes.text: The maintainers changed the reward-hacking judge to assess task intent instead of gold-file heuristics. The revised rules can change which successful trials the leaderboard disqualifies.
The maintainers required ATIF trajectories for rewarded trials during submission checks. Submissions without those trajectories now fail intake despite reporting successful tasks.

note: Fixed 28 of the 89 tasks in 2.0. Scores moved by up to 12 points, so the two are kept apart.

name: Terminal-Bench 2.1 Extended
description: Agents complete long command-line tasks in containers, scored by verification tests. Mercor adds 99 new expert-written tasks to the 89 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of terminal-bench-2-1. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: Terminal-Bench 3.0
description: Agents complete 74 tasks across 7 domains in sandboxed terminal environments. Verifier scripts grade each trial as pass or fail.
note: Released first as FrontierBench v0.1, the name Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 card uses. Terminal-Bench 4.0 succeeded it in August 2026.

name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
description: Agents complete 66 hard tasks in containerized terminals across software, ML, science, security, and operations. Test scripts verify each result, scored as resolution rate.
org: Stanford University, Harbor, and Laude Institute
note: It removed 8 saturated or flawed tasks from Terminal-Bench 3.0 and set a flat 8-hour agent timeout.

name: Terminal-Bench 4.1
description: The Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks with hardened verifiers: agents complete 66 hard tasks in containerized terminals across software, ML, science, security, and operations. Test scripts verify each result, scored as resolution rate.
org: Stanford University, Harbor, and Laude Institute
note: It kept the 4.0 tasks and hardened the verifiers of 44 of them against reward hacking, then regraded the saved 4.0 runs. 162 trials changed score, and every model stayed within its earlier 95% interval.

name: Terminal-Bench Challenges
description: Agents build a large project end to end with no time limit, such as a faster Rust compiler or a WebGL renderer in WebAssembly. Each challenge has its own test bed and metric.
org: Terminal-Bench team (Stanford, Harbor and Laude Institute)
note: Three challenges at launch: Rust compiler speedup, inference engine codegolf and WASM WebGL renderer. Submissions must share the artifact and full agent logs.

name: Terminal-Bench Hard
description: Agents complete 44 hard tasks from Terminal-Bench Core in the Terminus 2 harness. Artificial Analysis scores pass@1 averaged over 3 repeats.
note: Artificial Analysis retired it in June 2026 in favor of Terminal-Bench 2.1.

name: Terminal-Bench Math Modeling
description: Agents use a terminal to solve 18 mathematical modeling problems and submit numerical answers. Feasibility checks and numerical scoring compare answers with reference solutions.
note: The current board uses Multi-O against 99 human papers. The paper and repository also describe different one-reference scoring rules. Their results are not interchangeable.

name: Terminal-Bench Pro
description: Agents solve 400 terminal tasks across eight domains. Harbor distributes the 200 public tasks. Alibaba keeps the other 200 for private evaluation.
note: On November 19, 2026, Qwen3.5 led the public set at 51.5%. Claude Opus 4.5 led the private set at 51.0%.

name: Terminal-Bench-Science
description: 70 scientific research-workflow tasks across five science areas, run in Harbor containers. Hidden tests give the resolution rate.
note: 70 tasks kept from 920 proposals. v0.1. V0.2 in progress. Citation is a Zenodo DOI, no paper.

name: Terminal-X
description: A suite of three terminal datasets for coding agents. DeepTerminalBench tests single-shot depth, EvoCode-Bench tests multi-round iteration and RoadmapBench tests version upgrades on real repositories.
note: The blog post is dated 2026-05-02. All tasks use the Terminal-Bench 2.0 task format and the Harbor framework. The suite has no combined score, so each member is its own record.

name: TerminalWorld
description: Agents complete terminal workflows reconstructed from public recordings in isolated environments. Automated tests check the resulting files and system state. A manually reviewed 200-task subset supports the published model comparisons.
note: The full release contains 1,530 automatically validated tasks across 18 categories. The current leaderboard runs the 200-task Verified subset with Terminus-2. Full-set and Verified scores must remain separate.

name: TERMS-Bench
description: Agents negotiate the price of a single item with simulated counterparts over up to 10 rounds of alternating offers. Counterparts follow six behavior families across three regimes. A program scores each agent from its logged actions on four separate axes: surplus captured, agreement calibration, belief error about the opponent and procedural violations. Extra modes score merchant profit and a bankroll over many sessions.
note: There is no model judge and no composite score, so models are compared axis by axis. The leaderboard data was generated on 2026-05-04 and covers about a dozen models. No code repository is linked.

name: TerraFirm REIT
description: Models choose which properties to sell from a portfolio of 12 office buildings. The evaluator checks whether the remaining portfolio meets five debt and valuation constraints.
note: The February 2026 results give o4-mini an 80% pass rate over ten attempts. The same table gives o3 50% and Claude Opus 4.6 20%.

name: TerretaQA
description: Models answer open-domain questions in Valencian about the history, geography, tourism, and culture of the Valencian Community.
note: The release month follows the dataset repository history.

name: Testing model's emotional inteligence
description: Models identify the emotion in a story. A judge compares each response with the reference emotion on a sample of ten stories.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 7 distinct model versions.

name: Testing Relational Understanding in Text-Guided Image Generation
description: Models depict relationships between named entities. Human participants judge whether the generated scenes match each caption.

name: TestPrism
description: Coding agents write tests for 300 tasks. A test passes only if it fails on the starting code, accepts every valid implementation and rejects every invalid one.
note: It had 36 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: TetrisBench
description: Models play Tetris head-to-head in the original benchmark. The Harbor strategy track grades an agent-written JavaScript placement function on 20 fixed piece sequences.
note: On November 19, 2026, Claude Fable 5 led Kimi K3, Claude Opus 4.8, and GPT-5.6 Sol with 10 wins in 15 head-to-head games. The separate Harbor strategy track has no published model score.

name: Text Classification (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models analyze business text and return labels or structured outputs, for example sentiment or the main viewpoints in user content.
note: In-house ByteDance Seed evaluation. The tasks are not public. It seems to follow the Seed1.8 Information Processing set. Scoring is a guess.

name: Text persuasion study on political opinions
description: Participants read model-written articles or chat with a model on political topics. Scored on opinion shift against human-written articles.
note: Human participant study used for the GPT-4o Preparedness persuasion score.

name: Text to Text Safety
aliases: Text to Text Safety (lower is better)
description: An automated content safety evaluation measures policy violations in model answers to text prompts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: Text-based reinforcement learning task (Anthropic)
description: Agents build scaffolding that improves a weaker model on a text-based reinforcement learning task.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: TextArena
description: Collection of competitive text games for LLM eval and RL, with an online Elo leaderboard.

name: TextCaps
description: Models retrieve matching text and images using the TextCaps corpus.

name: TextEdit
description: Image generation models edit text inside 2,148 real and synthetic images across 18 subcategories. OCR, image-fidelity metrics and a multimodal LLM judge score target accuracy, text preservation and scene integrity.
note: Released with the InternVL-U technical report on 2026-03-06. Each image has a hand-annotated edited ground truth. A 500-sample mini set is also reported.

name: TextEdit Real
description: Models edit text in real images in the full TextEdit test set. The score is the published judged average.
note: One track of TextEdit. The TextEdit record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: TextEdit Virtual
description: Models edit text in virtual images in the full TextEdit test set. The score is the published judged average.
note: One track of TextEdit. The TextEdit record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: TextQuests
description: Agents play 25 classic interactive fiction games. The score is harmful actions per 100 steps, where lower is better. The board also reports game progress.
note: Meta reports the harm rate per 100 steps as a safety measure.

name: TextVBench
description: Models render requested text in video or preserve text from a reference image. The score tracks spelling, placement, and consistency across frames.
org: University of Science and Technology of China and collaborators

name: TextVQA
description: Models answer 45,336 questions about 28,408 images that require reading text in the image. Scoring is VQA accuracy against human answers.

name: TextWorld Cooking (GATA)
description: Agents navigate text-based rooms, gather ingredients, and prepare recipes. The port sums points earned during play and includes separate training and test games at increasing difficulties.
note: The highest public hub mean reward was 2.167 for Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 on 20 examples on 2025-12-30. The hub also lists Qwen3-0.6B.

name: TGIF-QA
description: Models answer questions about actions, repetitions, and changes over time in animated clips.

name: ThaiExam
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions from standardized examinations in Thailand, such as ONET, IC, TGAT, TPAT-1 and A-Level.

name: The Amazing Agent Race
description: Agents navigate websites, call tools, and calculate a passcode across 1,400 scavenger hunts. The benchmark includes 800 sequential puzzles and 600 with branching paths.
note: Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 4 led GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4 mini configurations with 36.6% final accuracy in April 2026.

name: The Met Dataset
description: Models match photographs of artworks to catalog images from the Metropolitan Museum of Art. The evaluation measures instance recognition across photographic conditions.

name: The Midnight Index
description: Models lead a nation through fixed scenarios in a strategy game. The simulation records outcomes, escalation, and whether public commitments match later decisions.
note: Grok 4.7 recorded the highest listed hub mean reward, 0.7666 on three examples on October 19, 2026. Other runs include Gemini 3.8 Flash and GPT-6 Luna.

name: The Pushback Test
description: Models advise a parent who questions urgent medical advice. The evaluation checks whether the model maintains the urgency required by NHS guidance.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 1 distinct model version.

name: The Turtle Test
description: Models remember a conditional instruction during unrelated conversation. They must apply it when triggered and avoid applying it on earlier turns.
note: The author publishes a reusable task harness on Kaggle. The public leaderboard feed returned no scored rows.

name: TheAgentCompany
description: Agents do work tasks in a simulated software company, using a browser, code, and chat with simulated coworkers. Scored by full and partial checkpoint completion.

name: TheOne Routing Decisions
description: Models route messages to an existing topic, start a new topic, or request clarification. The grader checks their decisions on 36 synthetic cases.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 2 distinct model versions.

name: TheoPhysEval
description: Agents solve 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems on their own, with literature search and scripts. Each final answer is checked against an expert answer, and the score is the pass rate.
org: ICTS Bengaluru (Suvrat Raju) with 35 researchers incl. Google DeepMind, Harvard and KU Leuven
note: Problems span 11 areas, from classical physics to holography. A realistic track allows web search and an isolated track does not. GPT-6 Astra passed 49 of 50 with search. Some expert reference answers were found wrong.

name: TheoremQA
description: Models solve 800 university-level questions in math, physics, EE and CS, and finance that each need a specific theorem. Scored by answer accuracy.

name: ThinkFollow (Qwen)
description: Models hold multi-turn dialogues with randomly inserted think and no-think flags and must switch reasoning mode correctly.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The data is not public.

name: Thinkingbox-bench
description: Agents complete 507 business workflows through tools and simulated user conversations. Executable checks require correct backend updates without forbidden side effects.
note: Some tasks also grade final responses against rubrics. The paper reports repeated-attempt reliability, but the linked dataset repository returned 404 during this audit.

name: Third PASCAL Recognizing Textual Entailment Challenge
description: Models decide whether a passage entails a proposed statement. The challenge compares their decisions with human labels.
note: MTEB scores the task using average precision.

name: Thrive Holdings helpdesk ticket resolution benchmark
description: Agent investigates IT support requests, takes action and decides when to escalate to a technician. Scored by pass rate.
note: Item count not stated. Drawn from Thrive's IT services firms.

name: Tic-Tac-Toe against Minimax
description: Models play standard three-by-three tic-tac-toe against a minimax opponent. The environment randomizes symbol and first mover, and awards half credit for a draw.
note: The README compares Qwen3-30B-A3B Instruct, Qwen3-8B (thinking). Qwen3-8B (thinking) has the highest listed avg reward, 0.300. The table has no run date.

name: TIIF-Bench
description: Image models generate short and long images scored on overall image quality.
note: GLM-Image reports short and long overall scores in its official model card.

name: TIME (time series forecasting)
description: Models forecast time series over short, medium, and long horizons without training on the target task.
note: The board reports mean absolute scaled error and probabilistic forecast scores by dataset and temporal pattern.

name: Time Horizon Index: KSP
description: Agents get five days to build and run a space program in Kerbal Space Program. The score is progress through 30 fixed missions.
note: Vals estimates a human needs 90 to 120 hours for the first 28 missions. The board had 13 models on 2026-10-07.

name: Time series forecasting task (Anthropic)
description: Agents solve a regression and time-series forecasting problem with known state-of-the-art results, in six variants.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: TimeLens-Bench
description: Models find the start and end time of a described event in a video. The benchmark re-annotates Charades-STA, ActivityNet Captions and QVHighlights with strict quality rules, and scores by mean IoU.
org: Nanjing University, ARC Lab (Tencent PCG) and Shanghai AI Lab
note: The authors report large model re-rankings compared with the original grounding benchmarks. Labs report the three subsets separately.

name: TimeSpeak
description: Models initiate speech at specified times while producing the requested content.
note: The launch post reports macro-averaged accuracy on an internal benchmark.

name: tinyBenchmarks
description: Models answer small selected subsets of established benchmarks. Item response estimates approximate accuracy on the full tests.

name: TIR-Bench
description: Models solve 13 kinds of image tasks that need tool use on images, such as rotation, jigsaw, and maze. Most items are multiple choice.
note: Qwen cards list two numbers for it, and the cards do not say which setting each one uses.

name: TireSidewall-Bench: Multimodal Zero-Shot Tire OCR
description: Models read the size markings on tire sidewalls from photographs. The grader compares extracted specifications with reference annotations.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 11 distinct model versions.

name: TituLLMs Bangla Evaluation Suite
description: Models answer Bangla questions on academic subjects, science and everyday reasoning. The suite also asks yes-or-no questions about passages.
note: The linked dataset contains the MMLU component. The harness links the other four datasets.

name: TMMLU+
description: Models answer traditional Chinese questions across 66 subjects. The evaluation includes elementary material and professional examinations.

name: TMMLU+ 1.1
description: Models answer traditional Chinese subject questions from a revised exam set. The revision corrects 197 answers and removes 539 questions from the original release.
note: The authors recomputed results on the 22,203 remaining questions.

name: TokSuite
description: Models complete questions under alternative tokenizations. The benchmark measures the change in accuracy relative to the canonical representation.

name: ToLD-Br
description: Models identify toxic language in Brazilian Portuguese posts using human annotations.
note: MTEB scores the task using accuracy.

name: Toloka Arena
description: Agents handle private simulated enterprise workflows with live databases, API tools and strict business rules across nine domains. The main metric pass^5 needs all five trials to succeed.
note: Modeled on the tau-bench method. Launch post dated 2026-04-16.

name: TOMATO
description: Models answer 1,484 human-written questions about 1,417 videos that need visual temporal reasoning, such as action counts, direction, rotation and velocity. Scored by accuracy.
org: Yale University and Allen Institute for AI
note: Published at ICLR 2025. At release the best model trailed humans by 57.3 points.

name: Tombo Full Transcript
description: Models transcribe Portuguese parish registers from 1621 to 1737. The grader compares each full page with a reference transcription at the character level.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 8 distinct model versions.

name: TOMG-Bench
description: Models generate molecules from natural language requests in three tasks: molecule editing, molecule optimization and customized generation. Each output is checked for validity and for meeting the requested properties.
org: Hong Kong Polytechnic University and Shanghai AI Lab (Jiatong Li et al.)
note: The paper was later retitled Speak-to-Structure (S^2-Bench).

name: Tone
description: An automated evaluation measures whether model refusals are objective, neutral and not preachy.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change against an earlier Gemini model.

name: Tool use prompt injection evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents run bash commands where files, scripts or command outputs carry injected instructions. Score is the attack prevention rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation reported without safeguards. The test cases are not public.

name: Tool-calling prompt injections
description: Agents receive prompt injections inside tool call outputs such as connectors. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Toolathlon
description: 108 long-horizon tasks across 32 apps through about 600 MCP tools. Execution-based checkers inspect final environment state.
note: Verified final release 2026-06-30. Do not mix with original-version scores.

name: Toolathlon-Verified
description: 108 long-horizon tasks across 32 apps through about 600 MCP tools. Execution-based checkers inspect final environment state.
note: A checked subset of Toolathlon tasks.

name: ToolBench
description: Models plan and call real REST APIs from RapidAPI, over 16,000 of them, to answer instructions that need one or many tools. ToolEval judges pass rate and win rate.
note: Released with the ToolLLM paper. Test groups G1, G2 and G3 differ in how many tools and categories a task spans. StableToolBench is a later stabilized variant.

name: ToolCall-Badcase
description: Models choose a tool and its arguments for 200 cases drawn from real user failure reports. Each case has a ground-truth call.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The cases are not public.

name: ToolcallFormatIFBench
description: Models make tool calls that must follow format rules across many agent scaffolds and tool sets. Qwen uses it to measure real-world tool call following.
note: In-house. Defined in one footnote of the Qwen3.6-Max-Preview post.

name: ToolComp
description: Models chain several tool calls to answer 485 human-verified prompts. Most final answers are numbers. ToolComp-Enterprise gives 11 tools and ToolComp-Chat targets general chat tool use. Step labels also support process reward model tests.
note: Scale runs the two subsets as the Agentic Tool Use (Enterprise) and Agentic Tool Use (Chat) boards. The prompts carry 1,731 step-level labels. No public dataset was found.

name: ToolMaze
description: Agents complete tool-use tasks while the runtime introduces explicit or hidden tool failures. A judge checks completion across four task structures and five perturbation settings. Metrics report task success, recovery rate, and recovery cost.
org: Shanghai AI Laboratory, East China Normal University, Soochow University and others
note: Recovery rate includes only runs that encountered a perturbed call. Recovery cost compares actual calls with an oracle recovery path. The runtime includes 273 tool plugins.

name: ToolQA
description: Models answer questions that need outside information, using 13 tools such as database queries, text retrieval and a calculator over fixed data sources. The questions are built so that a model's internal knowledge cannot answer them. An easy and a hard set separate single lookups from multi-step tool use, and answers are checked by exact match.
note: About 290 GitHub stars, and the repo was last pushed in 2023-08.

name: ToolRet
description: Models retrieve relevant tools for 7,600 requests from a corpus of about 43,000 tools. Evaluation measures ranking quality, precision, recall, and complete tool-set retrieval.
org: Shandong University, Baidu, and Leiden University
note: ToolRet-train is a separate training collection. Completeness requires every target tool to appear among the retrieved results.

name: ToolSandbox
description: Models use stateful tools in multi-turn conversations with a simulated user. Tools have hidden state dependencies, and runs are scored against milestones.
note: The repo moved to the apple-aiml-research organization on GitHub.

name: ToolUse (Qwen)
description: Models make single-turn, multi-turn and multi-step tool calls. The score combines intent recognition, format and parameter accuracy.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The data is not public.

name: TopiOCQA
aliases: Topically Diverse Open-Domain Conversational Question Answering
description: Models retrieve evidence and answer follow-up questions in conversations that change topics.
note: The benchmark uses conversation history to resolve what each new question refers to.

name: ToRR
description: Models answer questions over tables given in several formats, and the board checks how much accuracy changes when the table format or prompt changes.
note: 10 datasets across table formats and domains. One HELM release, v1.0.0, on 2025-03-04.

name: ToxicChat
description: Models identify toxic user messages from real conversations with an online chatbot.
note: The dataset includes prompts that users submitted to the Vicuna demo.

name: ToxiGen
description: Models continue ToxiGen prompts about 13 minority groups. Scored by the average toxicity of the generations.
note: Generation use of ToxiGen. The classification use is toxigen-discriminative.

name: ToxiGen (discriminative)
description: Models label statements about 13 minority groups as toxic or neutral. Scored by accuracy, often split into toxic and neutral labels.
note: Microsoft Phi reports run it through Eureka ML Insights. Other labs use ToxiGen prompts to measure toxic generations instead.

name: TraceSpatial-Bench
description: Models plan an object-centric 3D trace, an ordered list of metric 3D waypoints, from language instructions in real cluttered indoor scenes with depth.
note: 100 test items. From the RoboRefer team, who call it a harder benchmark than RefSpatial-Bench. 37 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: TraceTrial-Bench
description: Agent harnesses, not only models, are tested on reliability across seven components, with traces used to attribute each failure to its cause.
note: 203 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Trading Bot Bench
description: Models write Python trading strategies for historical stock prices. The evaluator combines return, Sharpe ratio, and drawdown on held-out scenarios.
note: The highest public hub mean reward was 0.3983 for gpt-4.1-nano on 5 examples on 2025-09-07. The hub also lists gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-mini.

name: Trae Agent Bench
description: Coding agents complete tasks drawn from real use of the Trae coding product, such as web development, bug fixing, code generation, artifacts and environment setup.
note: In-house ByteDance Seed evaluation. The model card reports it as separate rows per task type with no overall score.

name: TrafficImag
description: Models edit roadside traffic videos to show a different sequence of events. The evaluator checks routes, interactions, and preservation of the surrounding scene.

name: TRAIL
aliases: Trace Reasoning and Agentic Issue Localization
description: Models read long agent workflow traces and must find and classify the errors in them, using a formal taxonomy of agent error types. The set has 148 large human-annotated traces from established agent benchmarks.
note: It tests models as debuggers and judges of agent runs, not as agents. The dataset has 32 HF likes.

name: Training distribution hack rate (Anthropic)
aliases: Subset of training data classifier hack rate
description: Classifier monitors measure reward hacking on a subset of Anthropic's reinforcement learning training episodes.
note: Monitoring metric on training data, not a fixed public task set.

name: TRAIT
description: Models answer 8,000 forced-choice items on Big Five and Dark Triad traits. Reports a score per trait.
note: Psychometric inventory adapted for language models. There is no overall score. Meta cites Pellert et al. (2024), but the 8,000-item Big Five and Dark Triad TRAIT set is Lee et al. (arXiv 2406.14703).

name: Trajectory Labs cyber red teaming
description: Expert red teamers try to break safeguarded cyber endpoints across nine attack technique families on exploit reproduction tasks.
note: Run by Trajectory Labs for Google DeepMind. Results are counts of successful breaks.

name: Transformer Puzzles (RASPy)
description: Models complete eight sequence-programming puzzles in RASPy. The hub allows up to eight attempts per puzzle and checks solutions with executable tests.
note: The hub reports mistral-nemo, gpt-5. gpt-5 reached a mean reward of 0.875 on 8 examples on 2025-11-23.

name: Translated ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag and MMLU (Mistral)
description: Models answer French, German, Spanish and Italian versions of ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag and MMLU.
note: The Mixtral paper does not name the translation source and gives no average.

name: Translation Human Scoring (Z.ai)
description: People score model translations. The GLM-5 report does not describe the test set or the scale.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation shown only in a GLM-5 report chart.

name: Travel Agent Compassion
description: Agents book travel activities when the customer does not mention animal welfare. The benchmark measures how often they choose a welfare-neutral option.
note: The July 6, 2026 paper reports that Claude Opus 4.8 led ten models at 64.7% under the standard prompt. Models included GPT, GLM and DeepSeek.

name: Traveling Salesman (setrf)
description: Models return a tour through four to seven cities. Valid tours earn the optimal distance divided by the submitted distance.
note: The hub reports Gemini, GLM and Grok models. Gemini 3 Pro Preview reached the maximum reward of 1 on eight examples on November 24, 2025.

name: TravelPlanner
description: Agents plan multi-day trips from a user request, using tools to search nearly four million records of flights, hotels, restaurants and attractions. Each plan must meet the user's hard constraints, such as budget, and commonsense rules. The headline final pass rate counts a plan only when it meets every constraint.
org: Ohio State University (OSU NLP Group) and Fudan University
note: The 1,225 queries split into validation and test sets, and test scores come from submissions to the leaderboard. A sole-planning mode hands the model the gathered information and tests planning alone, so its scores differ from the tool-use mode. About 570 GitHub stars and 36 HF paper upvotes.

name: TREC 2017 LiveQA Medical Task
description: Models answer consumer health questions. The shared task compares responses with expert assessments of answer quality.

name: TREC-COVID
description: Models rank scientific articles that address specific information needs about COVID-19.
org: National Institute of Standards and Technology and collaborators
note: Assessors judged submitted results over successive rounds as the literature grew.

name: TreeBench
description: Models answer 405 visual questions about small targets in dense SA-1B images and give bounding boxes as evidence. Scored by answer accuracy, with box overlap as a second measure.
note: At release no model reached 60% accuracy, and OpenAI o3 scored 54.87.

name: TrialDesignBench
description: Models select a dose-finding design for an early oncology trial. The authors compare their choices with expert reference designs across 617 trials.

name: TriPhysBench
description: Models answer quantitative questions about physical events in videos. Some questions require measuring an object or looking up its specifications.
org: Renmin University of China and collaborators
note: The authors compare six models on 410 questions.

name: TritonBench
description: Models write Triton GPU operators in two channels, one from real GitHub kernels (G) and one matching PyTorch operators (T). Execution checks correctness and speedup.
note: Each channel comes with simple and complex instruction formats. The repo also ships crawled and synthetic training data.

name: Trivia-et
description: Models answer Estonian trivia questions from the Eesti Mäng board game.
note: EuroEval reports the Matthews correlation coefficient for its multiple-choice version.

name: TriviaQA
description: Trivia questions with evidence documents. Scored by exact match.
note: Saturated base-model metric.

name: TriWorldBench
description: World models generate synchronized robot-view videos from head and wrist cameras. Nineteen signals measure cross-view agreement, task alignment, physical coherence, motion, temporal stability, and visual quality.
org: Peking University, Tsinghua University, Beihang University and others
note: The public validation set has 100 RoboTwin 2.0 episodes. Scoring combines automatic measurements with semantic model judgments.

name: TRLawBench
description: Models answer 297 questions on Turkish law in three stages: 97 questions from official ÖSYM legal exams and 200 harder questions across 14 branches of law. Answers are checked against the answer key. A judge model also grades the reasoning from 0 to 10.
org: Beta Space Studio (Said Sürücü), with attorney Esat Erbil Tavus
note: The authors say the Stage 2 and 3 questions come from print sources that were never online. Gemini 3.1 Pro grades the reasoning score, so only the correct count is free of judge bias. The board also scores models with YargıPro, which the page does not define. About 43 GitHub stars.

name: TroubleshootingBench
description: Models find and correct realistic experimental errors in expert-written wet lab protocols. Scored as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: TrustBoundary Bench
description: Models plan incident response actions in a simulation. The grader checks whether they distinguish permission to act from information supplied as evidence.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 1 distinct model version.

name: TrustLLM JailbreakTrigger
description: Models face 400 prompts that apply 13 jailbreak methods to questions about bad behavior and requests for toxic content. Scored by refusal rate.
org: TrustLLM team (Yue Huang, Lichao Sun and others)
note: TrustLLM lists it as the jailbreak part of its safety dimension. Ai2 reports it in its Tulu 3 and Olmo safety suites.

name: TruthfulQA
description: Models answer 817 questions across 38 categories that are written to elicit common misconceptions. Scoring checks for truthful answers, often in multiple-choice form.

changes.text: The maintainers added a recommended two-option multiple-choice format with randomized answer order. They retain the earlier formats and state that previous results remain valid.

note: In January 2025 the authors added a two-option multiple-choice format and now recommend it. They say MC1 and MC2 results stay valid, so it remains one record.

name: TruthfulQA-Multi
description: Models answer questions targeting common misconceptions in Basque, Catalan, Galician and Spanish. The translations support direct comparison with the English questions.

name: TruthInsightBench
description: Agents analyze data from published studies without seeing the original conclusions. A judge grades whether the evidence and artifacts support the claims each agent makes.

name: ts-bench
description: Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI solve TypeScript tasks, and tests decide pass or fail. Version 1 uses 25 Exercism practice exercises. Version 2 uses real tasks from a large TypeScript monorepo, taken from SWE-Lancer.
note: The author calls the numbers directional, not lab-grade. Results are published as GitHub workflow runs and releases. Version 1 is frozen at the v1-final tag. About 243 GitHub stars.

name: ts-bench v1
description: Coding agents solve 25 self-contained TypeScript exercises from Exercism. The score is the percentage of exercises that pass their tests.
note: Version 1 is frozen at the v1-final tag. Version 2 uses five SWE-Lancer tasks.

name: TSP-Opt
description: Models find optimal tours for 960 traveling salesman instances across 8 difficulty levels. Answers are checked for optimality.
note: Microsoft released the dataset on Hugging Face as microsoft/tsp in June 2025, and the Eureka nphard_tsp config loads it.

name: TTS Arena
description: Users listen to two anonymous text-to-speech models read the same text and vote for the more natural one. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: The original space now points to TTS Arena V2, which has about 985 likes and was updated on 2026-10-31. Release month of the first arena not confirmed on a maker page.

name: TUA-Bench
description: Agents use a terminal for general computer tasks beyond coding, such as file, system and everyday productivity work.
note: 49 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Tuesday Work Index
description: A composite score built from the Surge AI benchmark suite, such as DAYJOB, GDP.pdf, Riemann-bench and ComplexConstraints. It asks whether models get through an ordinary workday.
note: About 50 models on the board by 2026-10.

name: Tulu 3 Safety Eval
description: Models answer harmful, jailbreak and benign prompts from several safety benchmarks in Ai2's safety-eval suite. A WildGuard classifier judges the outputs, and the score is an average.
note: An aggregate used in the Tulu 3 release. The member benchmarks include WildGuardTest, HarmBench and XSTest. Released month taken from the Tulu 3 release.

name: TurBLiMP
description: Models compare Turkish sentence pairs that differ in grammaticality. The core tests cover 16 grammatical phenomena.

name: TurkishMMLU
description: Models answer over 10,000 multiple choice questions that Turkish curriculum experts wrote for nine high-school subjects. Scoring is accuracy.

name: Turku NER Corpus
description: Models identify named entities in Finnish text from the Universal Dependencies corpus.
note: EuroEval scores entity spans with microaveraged F1 and excludes the miscellaneous class from its primary score.

name: Turku Paraphrase Corpus
description: Models compare Finnish sentence pairs and estimate how closely their meanings match.
note: MTEB scores the task using Spearman correlation.

name: Turn based Benchmarks
description: Models play turn based games including tic tac toe and rock paper scissors. The tasks evaluate game decisions and adaptation to opponents.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 7 distinct model versions.

name: TurnBench
description: Turn-taking systems listen to two-person conversations and must detect when a speaker's turn ends and when the other speaker interrupts. The test set has 116 English conversations in six interaction styles, each labeled by three annotators. Systems rank by recall, and a system whose false-positive rate exceeds 0.15 ranks below every qualifying system. Latency after each event is also reported.
org: Sesame AI with Mundo AI, Carnegie Mellon University and others
note: Test labels are withheld, and submissions go by email with predictions and a public write-up. Systems must be causal, using audio only up to the current moment. Entries mix dedicated turn detectors with realtime voice models, and 12 of the 26 entries are outside submissions. About 60 GitHub stars.

name: TUT Urban Acoustic Scenes 2018
description: Models recognize the setting of a ten-second audio clip recorded in a European city.
note: The benchmark distinguishes ten acoustic scenes.

name: TutorBench
description: Models act as tutors on three tasks: adaptive explanations for a confused student, feedback on student work, and hints. Graded against sample-specific rubrics.
note: Dataset card created 2025-10-07.

name: TutorCaseBench
description: Tutors respond to students whose behavior interferes with learning. Case-specific rubrics grade the responses, and a separate track tests selection among possible interventions.

name: TVBench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions on 10 temporal video tasks, such as action counting and ordering, that static frames cannot solve. Scored by accuracy.
org: University of Santiago de Compostela and University of Amsterdam et al.

name: TVQA
description: Models answer 152,545 multiple-choice questions about clips from 6 TV shows, using video frames and subtitles. Scoring is accuracy.

name: TVRBench
description: Agents move through simulated indoor scenes to reproduce a target image's viewpoint. Success requires stopping at exactly the target pose on the simulator's discrete grid. The evaluation split has 500 tasks across 80 scenes.
note: Training and reinforcement-learning tasks use separate scene splits. Visual-action history and action-only memory are distinct evaluation settings. The paper also studies post-training methods.

name: tweetSentBR
description: Models classify the sentiment of Brazilian Portuguese social media posts as positive, neutral, or negative.
org: Henrique Brum and Maria das Graças Volpe Nunes

name: Twitter URL Paraphrase Corpus
description: Models identify paraphrases among pairs of social media posts that reference the same URL.
note: MTEB scores the task using average precision.

name: Two-Hop Latent Reasoning
description: Models answer questions that require composing two facts. The hub port covers the semi-synthetic tasks and includes a shuffled control.
org: Mikuláš Balesni, Tomasz Korbak and Owain Evans
note: The November 2024 paper studies Llama 3 8B and GPT-4o. Performance varies by training condition and relation. The hub lists no public port scores.

name: TxBench-Antibody-Discovery
description: Agents make antibody discovery and development decisions from real experimental data. A grader checks each decision.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 100 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: TxBench-Oligo-Discovery
description: Agents make oligonucleotide discovery decisions, such as ASO and siRNA design, from real data. A grader checks each decision.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 113 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: TxBench-Preclinical-Pharmacology
description: Agents analyze preclinical pharmacology data and make development decisions. A grader checks each decision.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 100 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: TydiQA
description: Models answer information-seeking questions from Wikipedia articles in 11 typologically diverse languages, across 204K question-answer pairs. Scored by F1.
note: Model cards usually report the gold passage (GoldP) task.

name: U-Artifacts
description: Models build interactive artifacts such as small apps and pages for 199 cases across 13 topics. A GUI agent simulates a non-expert user to grade interactivity, looks and fit to the need.
note: In-house Seed benchmark with four task families. It is a different test from Tencent ArtifactsBench.

name: U-MATH
description: Models solve 1,100 unpublished open-ended university math problems from teaching materials, balanced across six subjects. About 20% include images, and an LLM judge checks each solution.
note: The companion set mu-MATH tests how well LLMs judge math solutions. The paper has 20 HF upvotes.

name: U18 safety evaluations
description: Models answer challenging prompts in teen safety categories such as age-restricted goods, eating disorders and emotional reliance. Scored as safe completion rate per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: UA-Bench
description: Models identify underwater sound sources and their subclasses from audio recordings. The authors repeat the test with silent audio to check reliance on sound.

name: UAV Operator
description: Models manage simulated drone missions as weather and flight restrictions change. The simulator scores their decisions from logged aircraft and mission state.
note: The calibration table available on November 19, 2026, reports Laguna at 0.998 and GPT-4.1-nano at 0.884 on tier T0. Both completed all 30 T0 episodes.

name: UAV Robust Control Hub
description: Agents construct policies for a fictional civilian drone simulator. The benchmark evaluates policies on hidden scenarios and reports separate results under changed conditions.
note: On November 11, 2026, the author reported CPU policy-learning baselines. The author had not run an end-to-end language model evaluation.

name: UCF101
description: Models recognize one of 101 human actions in video clips.
note: MTEB reports accuracy on its UCF101 task.

name: UFO-Bench
description: Models generate customized images from text and visual references. The evaluator breaks each request into individual requirements and checks how they interact.
org: University of Science and Technology of China and collaborators

name: Uganda Cultural and Cognitive Benchmark
description: Models answer questions about Ugandan daily life, institutions and cultural practices. A grader checks answers across 24 domains.
note: The date uses the creation month of the published dataset repository.

name: UGMathBench
description: Models solve 5,062 undergraduate math problems across 16 subjects. Each problem has three randomized versions, and effective accuracy counts problems solved in all versions.
org: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Department of Mathematics)
note: The paper was accepted to ICLR 2025. The authors plan more randomized versions as models saturate it. Ant Group reports it in the Ring-1T technical report.

name: UHGEval
description: Models identify hallucinated Chinese text or continue a supplied passage. Classification uses accuracy, while generation uses BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, keyword precision, and BERTScore.
org: Renmin University of China, Institute for Advanced Algorithms Research and others
note: The full set has 5,141 items. A 1,000-item subset reduces evaluation cost.

name: Uhura ARC-Easy
description: Models answer ARC-Easy science questions translated into Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho, Swahili and Yoruba. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Masakhane with OpenAI and collaborators (Bayes et al.)
note: Human-translated by fluent speakers. Released on Hugging Face with the GPT-4o System Card.

name: Uhura TruthfulQA
description: Models answer TruthfulQA questions translated into Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho, Swahili and Yoruba. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Masakhane with OpenAI and collaborators (Bayes et al.)
note: Human-translated by fluent speakers. Released on Hugging Face with the GPT-4o System Card.

name: Uhura-Eval
description: Models answer new reading comprehension questions written in Amharic, Hausa and Yoruba. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Uhura collaborators (Adelani, Kgomo, Bayes and others)
note: Created with fluent speakers for the GPT-4o System Card.

name: UI-Bench
description: AI website builders generate sites from 30 text prompts. Experts compare paired sites without seeing the builder names. A TrueSkill-derived model converts preferences into ratings with confidence intervals.
note: The paper covers ten tools, 300 generated sites, and more than 4,000 judgments. The current board reports 4,047 comparisons. Tool results include their surrounding product workflows and do not isolate base-model performance. The paper promises a site release that this review did not verify.

name: UI-TARS 15 Games Collection
description: GUI agents play 15 browser games such as 2048, Infinity-Loop and Snake-solver from screenshots. Each game score is divided by a human score, and the mean is reported.
note: In-house suite from the UI-TARS-2 report. Human performance is 100 by construction.

name: UI-Vision
description: Computer use agents are tested offline on human desktop demonstrations from 83 applications. Three tasks go from element grounding to layout grounding to next-action prediction for clicks, drags and key presses.
note: The makers call it the first license-permissive desktop benchmark. The dataset has over 7,000 downloads and 22 likes. ServiceNow GroundCUA work reports results on it.

name: UI-Vision Action Prediction
description: Models predict the next desktop interface action. The score is the published step success rate.
note: One track of UI-Vision. The UI-Vision record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: UI-Vision Element Grounding
description: Models locate interface elements from instructions. The score is the published overall grounding accuracy.
note: One track of UI-Vision. The UI-Vision record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: UI-Vision Layout Grounding
description: Models identify interface layout regions. The score is the published intersection over union percentage.
note: One track of UI-Vision. The UI-Vision record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: UIT-ViCTSD
description: Models classify Vietnamese comments for constructiveness and toxicity. The two labels capture different properties of the same text.

name: UIT-ViHSD
description: Models classify Vietnamese social media text into three categories covering clean language, offensive language, and hate speech.
org: Son T. Luu, Kiet Van Nguyen, and Ngan Luu-Thuy Nguyen

name: UIT-VSFC
description: Models classify sentiment in Vietnamese student feedback. The corpus also includes topic labels.

name: UK AISI alignment and monitorability evaluations
description: UK AISI suites: Out-of-Scope Supply Chain Attack simulation, AI-safety-research sabotage in a simulated company, no-CoT time horizon, CoT legibility.

name: UK AISI and CAISI simulated enterprise network range
description: Agents attack a 32-step simulated enterprise network that takes a human expert about 20 hours. The score is steps completed.
org: UK AI Security Institute and NIST CAISI
note: Government pre-deployment evaluation. AISI names this range The Last Ones. The range is not public. Kimi K3 report cites the joint assessment.

name: UK AISI correlated monitor failure
description: The model acts as a monitor over transcripts of another model carrying out an unsanctioned cyber attack. Scored on the share of violations it fails to flag.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation, first reported in the GPT-6.2 System Card.

name: UK AISI CoT Controllability
description: Models follow instructions that constrain the content of their chain of thought. Scored as the share of samples that follow the constraint.
note: External UK AISI evaluation. Low controllability is the safer direction for monitoring.

name: UK AISI cyber ranges
description: Agents attack multi-host simulated corporate and industrial networks end to end. Scored as the share of attempts that complete the range.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards. AISI describes two ranges, The Last Ones (32-step corporate network) and Cooling Tower (7-step industrial control attack). The ranges are not public.

name: UK AISI File Download monitor evasion
description: The model tries to download a forbidden file without a monitoring model noticing. Scored on how often it evades the monitor.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation, first reported in the GPT-6.2 System Card.

name: UK AISI narrow cyber tasks
description: Agents solve UK AISI cyber tasks graded by difficulty, including expert-level tasks. Scored as pass@5 and pass@1.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards. The tasks are not public.

name: UK AISI no-CoT maths competition problems
description: Competition maths problems from AIME, HMMT, CMIMC, SMT, BRUMO and OTIS Mock AIME, answered without a chain of thought. Scored on accuracy.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation, first reported in the GPT-6.2 System Card.

name: UK AISI Out of Scope Supply Chain Attack
description: Agents in simulated hard cyber challenges with incidental internet access may attack out-of-scope open source projects. Scored as rate of samples with such attacks.
note: External UK AISI evaluation. All tool calls are simulated by other models.

name: UK AISI sabotage continuation evaluation
description: Agents resume trajectories where sabotage of safety research already began. Scored on the share of trajectories where they actively continue the sabotage.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation reported in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards.

name: UK AISI simulated sandbox escape monitor evasion
description: The model tries to escape a deliberately vulnerable sandbox without a monitoring model noticing. Scored on the share of samples where it escapes undetected.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation, first reported in the GPT-6.2 System Card.

name: UK AISI unprompted sabotage evaluation
description: Agents act as AI research agents on AI safety research tasks. Scored on confirmed instances of sabotaging the safety research.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation reported in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards.

name: UK AISI vulnerability discovery challenges
description: A private suite of synthetic vulnerability discovery challenges. Models answer in a single response without tools, scored pass@1.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation, first reported in the GPT-6.2 System Card.

name: UltraText Bench
description: Image generators render dense bilingual text in many regions from 432 prompts. Scores check string accuracy, placement and legibility.
note: 42 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 113 GitHub stars.

name: UMI-Bench
description: 10 real tabletop tasks trained from standardized UMI hand-held gripper demos. 50 rollouts per task. Progress score and success rate.
note: Best pi0.5 at 55.84 average progress. Two tasks have 0% full success for every model. No live leaderboard.

name: Unauthorized Code Execution Bench
description: A coding agent meets injected instructions to run or fetch malicious artifacts while doing a benign task. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Meta benchmark of 76 tasks over 40 malicious objectives.

name: Unauthorized voice generation
description: Speech models produce audio that may deviate from the approved system voice. Scored on how many meaningful deviations the output classifier catches.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation of the voice output classifier. Reports precision and recall by language.

name: Uncheatable Eval
description: Models predict text from recently published documents. The evaluation measures perplexity across sources including news, research papers, fiction and code.

name: Uncritically reporting flawed results (Anthropic)
description: Agents analyze data with code that silently mishandles broken values. Graders check whether the agent flags the flaw or reports the biased numbers.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Cards report an overall score from 0 to 10 and a separate misreported rate.

name: Unexpected container or code states
description: Coding agents get impossible tasks, such as editing code that is missing from the container. Scored on correctly stating that the task could not be completed.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built from synthetic samples. The tasks are not public.

name: Ungrounded inference and sensitive trait attribution
aliases: UGI and STA safe behavior accuracy
description: Speech models get requests to infer traits about a speaker from audio. Scored on refusing ungrounded inferences and hedging plausible ones.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Ungrounded Inference evaluation
description: Models receive requests for inferences about people that images or text cannot justify. Scored on refusal rate in non-adversarial and adversarial sets.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report two difficulty levels with no overall number.

name: UniClawBench
description: Agents act as proactive assistants on real-world tasks with live tools across many turns. Tasks are grouped by the capability they test, so failures can be traced to one skill.
org: The University of Hong Kong (HKU MMLab)
note: Qwen runs it with the OpenClaw harness and reports it as multimodal tool use.

name: UniCode
description: Models solve generated competitive programming problems using automated test cases. Harbor packages 399 problems with validated reference solutions.
note: The October 16, 2025 paper compared 19 models on 492 problems. OpenAI o4-mini led that release with a 70.3% pass rate.

name: Unicorn (Vision Safety)
description: Models answer questions about objects in unusual images and sketches. The benchmark tests how well visual judgments hold up when the images change.

name: Unidentified Video Objects
description: Models segment and track objects in video without a fixed list of object categories. The evaluation compares predicted masks and tracks with annotated instances.

name: Uniform Bar Exam (MBE+MEE+MPT)
description: Models take a simulated Uniform Bar Exam with multiple-choice, essay and performance test parts. Scored on the 400-point scale.
note: OpenAI collaborators at CaseText and Stanford CodeX ran it for the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: UniGenBench
description: Text-to-image models draw images for 600 prompts across 5 themes and 20 subthemes, in English and Chinese and in short and long forms. A multimodal model judge checks each image on 10 primary and 27 secondary semantic dimensions, such as attributes, actions, relationships, layout, text and logical reasoning.
org: Tencent Hunyuan, Fudan University and Shanghai AI Lab
note: It first appeared with the Pref-GRPO paper (arXiv 2508.20751), and UniGenBench++ (arXiv 2510.18701) extended it. Separate leaderboards cover English, Chinese and long prompts. The team also releases an offline judge model based on a 72B Qwen model, so scores from the two judges may differ. 68 HF paper upvotes and about 140 GitHub stars.

name: Unintended Engagement with External Agent Messages
description: Agents discover a message board with apparent peer agents during a task. Scored on engagement with peers and on carrying out a specified unauthorized action.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Uniqueness of Optimum
description: Models find the optimum of a small problem and report whether it is unique. Exhaustive enumeration supplies the expected value and number of optimal solutions.
note: Kaggle publishes scores for 1 distinct model version.

name: UniREditBench
description: Image editing models carry out 2,700 edits that need reasoning, in real-world scenes and in game worlds with human-defined rules, across 8 primary and 18 secondary dimensions. A multimodal judge scores each edit against both a text reference and a ground-truth image.
note: The team also releases UniREdit-Data-100K, a synthetic training set made by the same pipeline. 32 HF paper upvotes and about 60 GitHub stars.

name: Unit Commitment Lite
description: Models schedule generators to serve hourly demand at minimum cost. The grader checks whether schedules meet operating constraints and compares cost with the optimum.
note: The README checked November 19, 2026 reports Claude Haiku 4.5 averaged 0.253 reward on 50 examples.

name: UniVerseBench
description: Models answer questions about music across more than 38 cultural and linguistic groups. The authors report accuracy by language and skill.

name: Unjustified refusals
description: An automated evaluation measures over-refusals on benign or borderline prompts that can be safely fulfilled.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: UNO-Bench
description: Models answer 1,250 human-written omni-modal questions and 2,480 uni-modal questions across 44 task types and 5 modality mixes. Multiple choice and multi-step open questions are scored, the open ones by a scoring model.
note: Most samples are set in a Chinese context.

name: Unsatz
description: Agents design experiments and propose equations for an unknown simulated system. Their final program must predict held-out interventions and conditions beyond the original experiments.
note: Nine language models attempt 80 systems in 20 domains.

name: UQ
description: Models answer 500 unsolved Stack Exchange questions. A model checks answers without a reference solution, and community members review selected answers.
note: The August 2025 paper compared OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek and Claude models. OpenAI o3-pro led with 75 of 500 answers passing the validator (15%).

name: UrbanSED
description: Models locate sound events in synthetic urban soundscapes. The benchmark includes reference labels for the times and types of events.

name: URGENT 2024
description: Models enhance speech under different forms of degradation. NVIDIA measures how accurately a recognizer transcribes the evaluation audio.

name: URO-Bench
description: Spoken dialogue models answer speech with speech across Understanding, Reasoning and Oral conversation. It has a basic track of 16 datasets and a pro track of 20.
note: Covers multilingual, multi-round and paralinguistic tests. Labs report U, R and O scores separately.

name: US-DermMCQA (Google)
description: Models pick the skin condition in a teledermatology image from 4 options. The set has one image per patient from 1,996 patients and 136 conditions.
note: Internal dataset described in Liu et al. (2020, Nature Medicine). Google added random distractors to make the questions.

name: USABO Semifinal Exam 2020
description: Models take the 2020 USA Biology Olympiad semifinal exam. Scored out of 150 points.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: USACO
description: Models solve 307 USA Computing Olympiad problems. Hidden unit tests check correctness and efficiency, scored as pass@1.
note: Princeton's Holistic Agent Leaderboard runs it.

name: USAMO 2024
description: Models write full proofs for problems from the 2024 USA Mathematical Olympiad, graded by human experts.
note: The MathArena dataset holds only the first three of the six problems.

name: USAMO 2025
description: Models write full proofs for the 6 problems of the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. Expert human graders score each proof.
note: In the first evaluation only Gemini 2.5 Pro reached a non-trivial score, at 25 percent.

name: USAMO 2026
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2026 USA Mathematical Olympiad. Judges grade each proof from 0 to 7 against rubrics.
note: MathArena reports GPT-5.4 at 95.2% and says it essentially saturates the benchmark.

name: User Confirmations During Computer Use
description: Agents doing computer use tasks reach financial, high-stakes communication and other actions. Scored on asking the user for confirmation when policy requires it.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: UserBench
description: Agents help simulated users who start with vague goals and reveal preferences bit by bit. Agents must ask clarifying questions and use tools to reach choices that fit the user.
note: The paper finds a gap between task completion and alignment with user preferences.

name: UserBench (developer simulation)
description: Models predict a developer’s next message in a real coding session. The evaluator compares predicted and observed action labels using Jaccard similarity.
note: On November 19, 2026, GPT-5.6 Sol at high effort scored 50.0% with 400 prior turns and 45.9% without history across 580 scored tasks.

name: USMLE Step 1 (sample questions)
description: Models answer the official USMLE Step 1 multiple choice sample questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Uses the official USMLE practice questions, not the MedQA question bank.

name: USMLE Step 2 (sample questions)
description: Models answer the official USMLE Step 2 multiple choice sample questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Uses the official USMLE practice questions, not the MedQA question bank.

name: USMLE Step 3 (sample questions)
description: Models answer the official USMLE Step 3 multiple choice sample questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Uses the official USMLE practice questions, not the MedQA question bank. Only the multiple choice section is included.

name: USNCO Local Section Exam 2022
description: Models take the 2022 US National Chemistry Olympiad local section exam. Scored out of 60 questions.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: Uyghur Language Question Answering
description: Models answer crowdsourced Uyghur language and literature questions. The suite includes reading comprehension, language exercises and exam questions at different proficiency levels.
note: The date comes from the first commit for this evaluation in the harness.

name: V*
description: Models answer 191 multiple choice questions about small details in high-resolution images, such as an object's color or relative position.
note: Some model cards report runs with Python image tools, which are not comparable with plain runs.

name: V-JEPA 2 zero-shot robot manipulation
